- **A firmware built with `CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED=1`** (CubeMX: STM32_WPAN → Debugger,
  or `Core/Inc/app_conf.h`). Otherwise `APPD_Init` switches PA13/PA14 to analog and
  disables debug in low-power modes, and the probe cannot reach the MCU while it runs
  (the tool reports this after `--swd-timeout`, default 10 s).

## Notes

- The override lives in the GPIO registers: it survives the script exiting and is
  cleared by any reset. Booting with VBUS low cannot be simulated this way, because
  the firmware reconfigures PA2 during start-up.
- Use `--vid` / `--pid` if the USB descriptor changes, `--no-host` when the cable is
  not plugged into the machine running the script, `--sn` with several ST-Links.
- The ST-Link can get stuck when an SWD access is interrupted (libusb timeouts,
  `ST-LINK SN : -`). `reset-probe` resets it at USB level; unplugging it also works.
- `button` uses one SWD access per edge: the firmware only takes two presses for a double
  press when the second starts less than a second after the first (`HOLD_MSEC` in
  `FlySight/mode.c`), and one access already takes more than a tenth of a second.

### Linux

```bash

# Linux BLE Implementation

`c/linux/ble_linux.c` implements the C API of `c/include/flysight_ble.h` on top of the
**BlueZ D-Bus API**, through GDBus (part of GIO). It follows the contract of the macOS
implementation (`c/macos/ble_macos.m`): same callbacks, same status codes, same moments.

Checked on Ubuntu 24.04 (BlueZ 5.72, kernel 6.8) with a FlySight 2: first pairing, reconnection
with the FlySight idle and in pairing mode, reconnection from a saved identifier without a scan,
link ended by the FlySight, FlySight reset while connected.

## Building

```bash
sudo apt-get install cmake libglib2.0-dev     # Debian, Ubuntu
sudo dnf install cmake glib2-devel            # Fedora

./gradlew :core:buildNativeLib                # or: cd core/src/nativeInterop && ./build.sh
```

The result is `build/linux/libflysight_ble.so`. It depends on GLib and GIO only, which every
desktop distribution installs; `libdbus` is no longer used.

## How it works

One worker thread owns a GLib main context. Everything that talks to BlueZ runs on it, and so
does every callback given back to the caller. The functions of the C API hand their work to that
thread and wait for the answer, so:

- the state of the library needs no lock;
- the caller receives its callbacks from a single thread, in the order things happened (the
  Kotlin side relies on it, see `DesktopKmpBleSocket`);
- a function of the API may be called from inside a callback.

A `GDBusObjectManagerClient` on `org.bluez` keeps a view of the adapters, devices, services and
characteristics BlueZ knows, and reports their property changes. That is where scan results,
the end of a link and notifications come from.

| C API | BlueZ |
|-------|-------|
| `ble_start_scan` / `ble_stop_scan` | `Adapter1.SetDiscoveryFilter` (`Transport=le`, `DuplicateData=true`), `StartDiscovery`, `StopDiscovery` |
| scan callback | a `Device1` object appears, or its `RSSI`, `ManufacturerData` or `Name` changes |
| `ble_connect` | `Device1.Connect`, then `Device1.Pair` if the device is not paired |
| `ble_disconnect` | `Device1.Disconnect` |
| disconnect callback | `Device1.Connected` becomes false, or the device object is removed |
| `ble_discover_services_async` | waits for `Device1.ServicesResolved`, then reads the `GattService1` and `GattCharacteristic1` objects |
| `ble_read_characteristic` | `GattCharacteristic1.ReadValue` |
| `ble_write_characteristic` | `GattCharacteristic1.WriteValue`, `type=request` |
| `ble_write_characteristic_no_response` | `GattCharacteristic1.WriteValue`, `type=command` |
| `ble_enable_notifications` | `GattCharacteristic1.StartNotify`; each change of `Value` is a notification |

## What is specific to BlueZ

### A pairing agent is required

A FlySight pairs with "Just Works". Measured on BlueZ 5.72 without any agent registered:

- the adapter is not bondable (`bluetoothctl show` prints `Pairable: no`);
- the pairing is refused whether it is asked for with `Device1.Pair` or triggered by reading an
  encrypted characteristic: the kernel asks user space to confirm it and nobody answers. The
  FlySight reports `PAIRING_COMPLETE status=2 reason=0x0c`, and ends the link 30 seconds later.

`ble_init()` therefore registers an agent (`NoInputNoOutput`) for as long as the library is in
use, and `ble_connect()` calls `Device1.Pair` itself for a device that is not paired yet: BlueZ
then accepts the pairing without asking anybody, because it knows the caller wants it. The
connect callback fires once the pairing is done.
[... 46 lines omitted ...]
- A read of a characteristic that also has notifications enabled is delivered twice: to the read
  callback, and to the notification callback, because BlueZ updates `Value` in both cases.
- Scan results are limited to one callback per second for a device whose name and manufacturer
  data did not change.

abstract val version: Property<String>

    @get:OutputDirectory
    abstract val sourceDir: DirectoryProperty

    @get:Internal
    abstract val zipFile: RegularFileProperty

    @TaskAction
    fun execute() {
        val src = sourceDir.get().asFile
        if (src.resolve("CMakeLists.txt").exists()) {
            logger.lifecycle("eSpeak-ng source already present at $src")
            return
        }

        val zip = zipFile.get().asFile
        zip.parentFile.mkdirs()

        if (!zip.exists()) {
            val ver = version.get()
            val url = URI("https://github.com/espeak-ng/espeak-ng/archive/refs/tags/${ver}.zip").toURL()
            logger.lifecycle("Downloading eSpeak-ng $ver from $url ...")
            url.openStream().use { input ->
                zip.outputStream().use { output ->
                    input.copyTo(output)
                }
            }
        }

        logger.lifecycle("Extracting eSpeak-ng source to $src ...")
        val destDir: java.io.File = src.parentFile
        val tempExtractDir = destDir.resolve("espeak-ng-${version.get()}")
        ZipInputStream(zip.inputStream().buffered()).use { zis ->
            var entry = zis.nextEntry
            while (entry != null) {
                val outFile = destDir.resolve(entry.name)
                if (entry.isDirectory) {
                    outFile.mkdirs()
                } else {
                    outFile.parentFile.mkdirs()
                    outFile.outputStream().use { out -> zis.copyTo(out) }
                }
                zis.closeEntry()
                entry = zis.nextEntry
            }
        }
        // GitHub archives extract as espeak-ng-<version>/, rename to espeak-ng/
        // @OutputDirectory may pre-create an empty target dir — delete it before renaming
        if (tempExtractDir.exists()) {
            if (src.exists() && src.isDirectory && (src.list()?.isEmpty() != false)) {
                src.delete()
            }
            if (!src.exists()) {
                tempExtractDir.renameTo(src)
            }
        }
    }
}

#!/bin/bash

set -e

SCRIPT_DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" && pwd )"
BUILD_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/build"

OS_NAME=$(uname -s)
case "${OS_NAME}" in
    Linux*)     PLATFORM=linux;;
    Darwin*)    PLATFORM=macos;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*)    PLATFORM=windows;;
    *)          echo "Unsupported platform: ${OS_NAME}"; exit 1;;
esac

echo "Building skygames_tts for platform: ${PLATFORM}"

# Auto-detect eSpeak-ng source
if [ -z "${ESPEAK_NG_SOURCE_DIR}" ]; then
    DEFAULT_SRC_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/espeak-ng"
    if [ -f "${DEFAULT_SRC_DIR}/CMakeLists.txt" ]; then
        ESPEAK_NG_SOURCE_DIR="${DEFAULT_SRC_DIR}"
        echo "Auto-detected eSpeak-ng source at: ${ESPEAK_NG_SOURCE_DIR}"
    else
        echo "Error: eSpeak-ng source not found."
        echo "Run './gradlew :AudioModule:downloadEspeakNg' to download it automatically,"
        echo "or set ESPEAK_NG_SOURCE_DIR to the source path."
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# Prefer a locally vendored copy of libsonic over a network git fetch.
# eSpeak-ng's cmake/deps.cmake declares sonic via FetchContent(GIT_REPOSITORY).
# Recent CMake (4.x) fails that fetch's git-submodule version probe with
# "Git_VERSION=''" on reconfigure. Pointing FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SONIC-GIT at a
# vendored tree makes FetchContent use it directly and skip every git operation.
SONIC_VENDORED_DIR="${SCRIPT_DIR}/third_party/sonic"
SONIC_ARGS=()
if [ -f "${SONIC_VENDORED_DIR}/sonic.c" ]; then
    echo "Using vendored sonic source at: ${SONIC_VENDORED_DIR}"
    SONIC_ARGS+=("-DFETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_SONIC-GIT=${SONIC_VENDORED_DIR}")
fi

mkdir -p "${BUILD_DIR}/${PLATFORM}"
cd "${BUILD_DIR}/${PLATFORM}"

**Tool: Bash** — Give eSpeak-ng a larger path buffer and rebuild the text-to-speech native library

~~~~bash
cd ~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/MiddleWare/AudioModule/src/nativeInterop && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='CMakeLists.txt'; s=open(p).read()
old='''# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL to avoid building eSpeak-ng tests/docs,
# but we explicitly depend on 'data' below to get espeak-ng-data compiled.
add_subdirectory(${ESPEAK_NG_SOURCE_DIR} espeak-ng EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
'''
new='''# eSpeak-ng keeps the path of its data in a buffer of 160 characters and builds file names
# from it, at run time and while compiling the phonemes here. A build tree under a long home
# directory overflows it: the names are cut short and every phoneme fails with "Bad vowel
# file". Give it room.
add_compile_definitions(N_PATH_HOME=1024)

# EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL to avoid building eSpeak-ng tests/docs,
# but we explicitly depend on 'data' below to get espeak-ng-data compiled.
add_subdirectory(${ESPEAK_NG_SOURCE_DIR} espeak-ng EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Screenshot of the nested X display :99 to a PNG file. usage: shot.py out.png [scale]"""
import os, sys
from PIL import ImageGrab
img = ImageGrab.grab(xdisplay=os.environ.get("DISPLAY", ":99"))
if len(sys.argv) > 2:
    f = float(sys.argv[2]); img = img.resize((int(img.width * f), int(img.height * f)))
img.save(sys.argv[1]); print("saved", sys.argv[1], img.size)
EOF
DISPLAY=:99 XAUTHORITY=$XA python3 shot.py $S/gui/empty.png 2>&1 | tail -1; cat xephyr.log | head -5

package fr.hozakan.skygames.user.firebase

import com.sun.jna.Library
import com.sun.jna.Native

interface FirebaseNative : Library {

    companion object {
        private const val LIBRARY_NAME = "skygames_firebase"

        const val FIREBASE_SUCCESS = 0
        const val FIREBASE_ERROR_INIT_FAILED = -1
        const val FIREBASE_ERROR_AUTH_FAILED = -2
        const val FIREBASE_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL = -5
        const val FIREBASE_ERROR_NOT_SIGNED_IN = -6

        const val MAX_JSON_LEN = 8192
        const val MAX_ID_TOKEN_LEN = 8192

        val INSTANCE: FirebaseNative by lazy {
            try {
                Native.load(LIBRARY_NAME, FirebaseNative::class.java) as FirebaseNative
            } catch (e: UnsatisfiedLinkError) {
                val osName = System.getProperty("os.name")
                val osArch = System.getProperty("os.arch")
                throw IllegalStateException(
                    "Failed to load native library: $LIBRARY_NAME\n" +
                        "Platform: $osName ($osArch)\n" +
                        "Make sure the library is built with './gradlew buildNativeLib' " +
                        "and copied to resources.\n" +
                        "JNA searches for libraries in the JAR under platform-specific " +
                        "paths (e.g., darwin-aarch64/).",
                    e
                )
            }
        }
    }

    fun firebase_init(googleServicesJsonPath: String?): Int

    fun firebase_cleanup()

    fun firebase_sign_in_with_google(
        idToken: String,
        accessToken: String,
        resultJson: ByteArray,
        maxLen: Int
    ): Int

    fun firebase_sign_out(): Int

    fun firebase_get_current_user(resultJson: ByteArray, maxLen: Int): Int
    fun firebase_get_session(resultJson: ByteArray, maxLen: Int): Int

    /** The signed-in account's ID token, as text. [forceRefresh]: 0 or 1. */
    fun firebase_get_id_token(forceRefresh: Int, buffer: ByteArray, maxLen: Int): Int

    fun firebase_get_error_string(errorCode: Int): String
}

**Tool: Bash** — Build a local stand-in for the Firebase library (test only, git-ignored) so the app can start on Linux

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; mkdir -p $S/fbstub && cd $S/fbstub && cat > stub.c <<'EOF'
/*
 * Stand-in for libskygames_firebase.so, for BLE tests of the SkyGames desktop app on Linux only.
 * The real library cannot be linked on Linux (the Firebase C++ SDK ships static libraries that are
 * not position independent). Nobody is ever signed in with this one.
 */
#include <stddef.h>

#define FIREBASE_SUCCESS 0
#define FIREBASE_ERROR_AUTH_FAILED -2
#define FIREBASE_ERROR_NOT_SIGNED_IN -6

int firebase_init(const char *path) { (void) path; return FIREBASE_SUCCESS; }
void firebase_cleanup(void) {}
int firebase_sign_in_with_google(const char *id_token, const char *access_token, char *result_json, size_t max_len) {
    (void) id_token; (void) access_token; (void) result_json; (void) max_len;
    return FIREBASE_ERROR_AUTH_FAILED;
}
int firebase_sign_out(void) { return FIREBASE_SUCCESS; }
int firebase_get_current_user(char *result_json, size_t max_len) { (void) result_json; (void) max_len; return FIREBASE_ERROR_NOT_SIGNED_IN; }
int firebase_get_session(char *result_json, size_t max_len) { (void) result_json; (void) max_len; return FIREBASE_ERROR_NOT_SIGNED_IN; }
int firebase_get_id_token(int force_refresh, char *buffer, size_t max_len) { (void) force_refresh; (void) buffer; (void) max_len; return FIREBASE_ERROR_NOT_SIGNED_IN; }

// Wait for a Future to complete, with timeout.
static bool await_future(const firebase::FutureBase& future, int timeout_ms = kTimeoutMs) {
    int remaining = timeout_ms;
    while (future.status() == firebase::kFutureStatusPending && remaining > 0) {
        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(kSleepMs));
        remaining -= kSleepMs;
    }
    return future.status() == firebase::kFutureStatusComplete && future.error() == 0;
}

// Escape a string for JSON output.
static std::string json_escape(const std::string& s) {
    std::string result;
    result.reserve(s.size() + 8);
    for (char c : s) {
        switch (c) {
            case '"':  result += "\\\""; break;
            case '\\': result += "\\\\"; break;
            case '\b': result += "\\b";  break;
            case '\f': result += "\\f";  break;
            case '\n': result += "\\n";  break;
            case '\r': result += "\\r";  break;
            case '\t': result += "\\t";  break;
            default:   result += c;      break;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

// Write a string to a buffer, checking size.
static int write_to_buffer(const std::string& str, char* buf, size_t max_len) {
    if (str.size() + 1 > max_len) {
        return FIREBASE_ERROR_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL;
    }
    std::memcpy(buf, str.c_str(), str.size() + 1);
    return FIREBASE_SUCCESS;

actual class DefaultFirebaseSessionService actual constructor() : FirebaseSessionService {
    actual override suspend fun session(): FirebaseSession? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        val buffer = ByteArray(FirebaseNative.MAX_JSON_LEN)
        val result = FirebaseNative.INSTANCE.firebase_get_session(buffer, buffer.size)

        buffer.decodeToString().substringBefore('\u0000').ifEmpty { throw FirebaseIdTokenException() }

## Assistant (09:31)

Voici la solution 1 en détail. Je n'implémente rien tant que tu ne l'as pas validée.

## Le principe

Sous Linux, les bibliothèques du SDK Firebase C++ ne peuvent pas entrer dans une bibliothèque partagée, mais elles se lient dans un exécutable. Je l'ai vérifié avec un prototype hors dépôt : lié contre le SDK 13.13.0, lancé depuis `Apps/composeApp`, il répond `firebase_init -> 0 (Success)` puis `firebase_get_current_user -> -6 (No user is signed in)`.

L'idée : sous Linux uniquement, les 8 fonctions `firebase_*` vivent dans un petit exécutable que l'app lance et interroge par ses entrée/sortie standard. Le SDK reste le même, avec le même stockage de session.

## Ce qui change

| Où | Changement |
|---|---|
| [firebase_common.cpp](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/c/common/firebase_common.cpp) | Rien. Les 8 fonctions sont réutilisées telles quelles. |
| Nouveau `c/linux/helper_main.cpp` | Une boucle : lit une requête par ligne, appelle la fonction, écrit une réponse par ligne. S'arrête quand son entrée se ferme. |
| [CMakeLists.txt](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/CMakeLists.txt) et `cmake/linux.cmake` | Sous Linux, la cible devient un exécutable, lié aussi à libsecret. macOS et Windows inchangés. |
| [build.gradle.kts](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/Feature/UserModule/build.gradle.kts) | `copyNativeFirebaseLib` copie l'exécutable (et non `libskygames_firebase.so`) sous `linux-x86-64/`. |
| [FirebaseNative.kt](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/jvmMain/kotlin/fr/hozakan/skygames/user/firebase/FirebaseNative.kt) | Sous Linux, `INSTANCE` devient une classe qui implémente la même interface en parlant au processus : extraction de l'exécutable, lancement, un appel à la fois, relance s'il est mort. |
| `DesktopAuthServiceDelegate`, `DefaultFirebaseSessionService` | Rien : ils ne voient que l'interface. |

## Les inconvénients

- **Deux chemins à maintenir.** Linux passe par des tubes, macOS et Windows par JNA. Chaque fonction ajoutée à l'en-tête doit l'être aussi au protocole, et un bug peut n'exister que sous Linux.
- **Des jetons transitent entre deux processus.** Le jeton Google à l'aller, le jeton Firebase au retour. Ils ne passent pas par la ligne de commande, donc restent invisibles dans `ps`, et un processus du même utilisateur qui pourrait les lire pourrait déjà lire la mémoire de la JVM. Mais c'est un endroit de plus où ils existent, et il ne faudra jamais journaliser ces lignes.
- **Un exécutable extrait puis lancé.** Sur un système où le dossier d'extraction est monté `noexec`, ou confiné (snap, flatpak, AppArmor), le lancement échoue. Il faut choisir le dossier avec soin, et le paquet DEB demandera peut-être de l'installer comme fichier ordinaire plutôt que dans le jar.
- **Un processus à surveiller.** S'il plante ou se bloque, il faut des délais d'attente et une relance, sinon l'app reste figée ou déconnectée.
- **Dépendances Linux.** `libsecret-1-dev` à la compilation ; à l'exécution, un trousseau (GNOME Keyring, KWallet). Sans trousseau, la session n'est pas conservée entre deux lancements. Ce point vaut pour toute solution basée sur le SDK sous Linux.
- **Ça contourne, ça ne corrige pas.** La cause reste que Google livre des bibliothèques non PIC. S'il en livre un jour des PIC, l'exécutable devient inutile.
- **Non vérifié : la connexion Google elle-même.** Elle demande ton client OAuth « Desktop » dans `local.properties` et ton compte ; je ne peux tester que l'initialisation et l'état « personne connecté ».

## L'autre voie qui garde le SDK

Recompiler le SDK Firebase C++ depuis ses sources avec `-fPIC` : l'architecture resterait identique partout (JNA), sans second processus. En contrepartie, c'est une compilation lourde à refaire à chaque montée de version, et des binaires à héberger pour la CI. Je ne l'ai pas essayée.

## Ma recommandation

L'exécutable auxiliaire : petit, réversible, sans toucher à macOS ni Windows. Dis-moi si je l'implémente, ou si tu préfères d'abord que j'évalue la recompilation du SDK.

En attendant ta réponse, je valide la pile Kotlin/JNA de FlySightApi sous Linux sans passer par SkyGames, ce qui ne dépend pas de Firebase.

// Inside SkyGames (Libs/FlySightApi, an included build), this build takes SkyGames' version
// catalog as its `libs`: one set of versions for every module of the composite. Built on its own,
// it falls back to its own gradle/libs.versions.toml, which keeps the same aliases.
val hostCatalog = file("../../gradle/libs.versions.toml")
val sharesHostCatalog = gradle.parent != null && hostCatalog.exists()

dependencyResolutionManagement {
    if (sharesHostCatalog) {
        // The local catalog would otherwise be imported as `libs` too.
        defaultLibrariesExtensionName = "standaloneLibs"
        versionCatalogs {
            create("libs") {
                from(files(hostCatalog))
            }
        }
    }
    repositories {

Result:

~~~~
static FS_CRS_State_t FS_CRS_State_Read(void)
{
	FS_CRS_State_t next_state = FS_CRS_STATE_READ;
	Custom_CRS_Packet_t *packet;
	uint8_t *tx_buffer;
	UINT br;

	if (!Custom_APP_IsConnected())
	{
		next_state = FS_CRS_STATE_IDLE;
	}

	if (timeout_flag)
	{
		next_packet = next_ack;
		timeout_flag = 0;

		read_pos = read_offset + next_packet * read_stride;
		f_lseek(&file, read_pos);

		// Reset timeout timer
		HW_TS_Start(ack_timer_id, TX_TIMEOUT_TICKS);
	}

	while ((next_state == FS_CRS_STATE_READ) && (packet = Custom_CRS_GetNextRxPacket()))
	{
		if (packet->length >= 1)
		{
			// Handle commands
			switch (packet->data[0])
			{
			case FS_CRS_COMMAND_CANCEL:
				next_state = FS_CRS_STATE_IDLE;
				break;
			case FS_CRS_COMMAND_FILE_ACK:
				if (packet->length >= 2)
				{
					if (packet->data[1] == (next_ack & 0xff))
					{
						++next_ack;

						// Reset timeout timer
						HW_TS_Start(ack_timer_id, TX_TIMEOUT_TICKS);
					}
				}
				break;
			}
		}
	}

	while ((next_state == FS_CRS_STATE_READ) &&
			(tx_buffer = BLE_TX_Queue_GetNextTxPacket()) &&
			(next_packet < next_ack + FS_CRS_WINDOW_LENGTH) &&
			(next_packet < last_packet))
	{
		tx_buffer[0] = FS_CRS_COMMAND_FILE_DATA;
		tx_buffer[1] = (next_packet & 0xff);

		if (f_eof(&file))
		{
			// Send empty buffer to signal end of file
			BLE_TX_Queue_SendNextTxPacket(CUSTOM_STM_FT_PACKET_OUT, 2,
					&SizeFt_Packet_Out, FS_CRS_TxCallback);
			last_packet = ++next_packet;
		}
[... 23 lines omitted ...]

	if (next_state == FS_CRS_STATE_IDLE)
	{
		// Stop timeout timer
		HW_TS_Stop(ack_timer_id);

		// Close file
		f_close(&file);

		// De-initialize disk
		FS_ResourceManager_ReleaseResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);
	}

	return next_state;
}

~~~~
static FIL file;
static DIR dir;

static uint32_t read_offset;
static uint32_t read_stride;
static uint32_t read_pos;

static uint32_t next_packet;
static uint32_t next_ack;
static uint32_t last_packet;

static uint8_t ack_timer_id;
static volatile uint8_t timeout_flag;

static void FS_CRS_TxCallback()
{
	UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1<<CFG_TASK_FS_CRS_UPDATE_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
}

static void FS_CRS_SendPacket(uint8_t command, uint8_t *payload, uint8_t length)
{
	uint8_t *tx_buffer;

	if ((tx_buffer = BLE_TX_Queue_GetNextTxPacket()))
	{
		tx_buffer[0] = command;
		memcpy(&tx_buffer[1], payload, length);
		BLE_TX_Queue_SendNextTxPacket(CUSTOM_STM_FT_PACKET_OUT, length + 1,
				&SizeFt_Packet_Out, FS_CRS_TxCallback);
	}
}

static void FS_CRS_SendNak(uint8_t command)
{
	FS_CRS_SendPacket(FS_CRS_COMMAND_NAK, &command, sizeof(command));
}

static void FS_CRS_SendAck(uint8_t command)
{
	FS_CRS_SendPacket(FS_CRS_COMMAND_ACK, &command, sizeof(command));
}

static FS_CRS_State_t FS_CRS_State_Idle(void)
{
	FS_CRS_State_t next_state = FS_CRS_STATE_IDLE;
}

static void FS_CRS_Update(void)
{
	state = state_table[state]();
}

static void FS_CRS_Timeout(void)
{
	timeout_flag = 1;

	// Call update task
	UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1<<CFG_TASK_FS_CRS_UPDATE_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
}

void FS_CRS_Init(void)
{
	// Initialize CRS task
	UTIL_SEQ_RegTask(1<<CFG_TASK_FS_CRS_UPDATE_ID, UTIL_SEQ_RFU, FS_CRS_Update);

## Assistant, note while working (09:36)

J'ai trouvé la cause du blocage de lecture : dans crs.c, une commande reçue juste après l'accusé de réception d'un fichier est dépilée sans réponse, et BlueZ envoyant les deux écritures d'affilée, ça bloque CONFIG.TXT. Je vais d'abord mesurer la fréquence du problème avant de corriger.

package ca.flysight.api.ble

import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableSharedFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.SharedFlow
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.asSharedFlow

class KmpGattCallbackImpl(
    private val operationCallback: OperationCallback? = null
) : KmpMutableGattCallback {

    private val _eventFlow = MutableSharedFlow<GattCallbackEvent>(replay = 0)
    override val eventFlow: SharedFlow<GattCallbackEvent> = _eventFlow.asSharedFlow()

    override suspend fun sendEvent(event: GattCallbackEvent) {
        if (operationCallback != null) {
            operationCallback.exec.invoke(event)
        } else {
            _eventFlow.emit(event)
        }
    }

    data class OperationCallback(
        val characteristic: KmpGattCharacteristic,
        val exec: (GattCallbackEvent) -> Unit
    )
}

173	    private suspend fun handleReadTask(task: GattTask.ReadTask) {
   174	        val gatt = task.gatt
   175	        val characteristic = task.characteristic
   176	        task.commandLogger()
   177	        gatt.readCharacteristic(characteristic)
   178	        withTimeout(5000) {

   180	        }
   181	    }

   183	    private suspend fun handleWriteTask(task: GattTask.WriteTask) {
   184	        logger.i { "writing task $task" }
   185	        val gatt = task.gatt
   186	        val characteristic = task.characteristic
   187	        val command = task.command
   188	        val writeType = task.writeType
   189	        task.commandLogger()
   190	        gatt.writeCharacteristic(

   194	        )
   195	        if (writeType != WRITE_TYPE_NO_RESPONSE || policy == WriteNoResponseSystemCallbackPolicy.WaitSystemCallback) {
   196	            withTimeout(5000) {

   198	                logger.i { "task completed in time $task" }
   199	            }
   200	            logger.i { "task completed $task" }

   209	        val command = task.command

   234	        // Drain any queued-but-not-yet-processed tasks from the channel

## Assistant, note while working (09:49)

J'ai identifié un autre bug côté Kotlin, visible seulement sur plusieurs essais : les accusés de réception peuvent partir dans le désordre, ce qui fait que le FlySight renvoie la fin d'un fichier précédent et que le lecteur suivant la confond avec le début du sien. Je corrige l'ordre d'envoi et rends le lecteur strict sur le premier paquet, puis je relance une série de tests.

~~~~bash

# --- E. Tasks are queued in the order they are added
p='ble/src/commonMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/task/GattTaskQueue.kt'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new,count=1):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==count,(s.count(old),old[:70])
    s=s.replace(old,new)
rep('''            for (task in taskChannel) {
                logger.i { "[GattTaskQueue] new task being processed : $task" }
''','''            for (task in taskChannel) {
                tasksMutex.withLock { tasks += task }
                logger.i { "[GattTaskQueue] new task being processed : $task" }
''')
rep('''    fun addTask(task: GattTask) {
        scope.launch {
            tasksMutex.withLock {
                tasks += task
                taskChannel.send(task)
            }
        }
    }
''','''    fun addTask(task: GattTask) {
        // Queued right here, in the order of the calls. Launching a coroutine to do it let two
        // tasks added one after the other swap places. The device ignores a file acknowledgement
        // that arrives before the previous one, then sends the rest of that file again.
        taskChannel.trySend(task)
    }
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)

# --- F. A read starts with packet 0, and nothing else
p='core/src/commonMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/core/internal/bluetooth/operation/BleFileReader.kt'; s=open(p).read()
rep('''                if (cmd == Command.FILE_DATA) {
                    requestAnswered = true
                    handleFileDataPart(event.value.sliceArray(1 until event.value.size))
''','''                if (cmd == Command.FILE_DATA) {
                    handleFileDataPart(event.value.sliceArray(1 until event.value.size))
''')
rep('''        if (fileData == null) {
            logger.d { "[FILE] FIRST packet $packetId, starting file data" }
            fileDataPacketNumber = packetId
''','''        if (fileData == null) {
            if (packetId != 0) {
                // The packets of a read are numbered from 0. Another number here is the previous
                // transfer, which the device is still sending again: taking it would return the
                // end of another file as the content of this one. Acknowledging it lets the
                // device finish that transfer and accept the request for this one.
                logger.w { "[FILE] STRAY packet $packetId before the first one, acknowledged and dropped" }
                sendReadFileAck(packetId)
                return
            }
            requestAnswered = true
            logger.d { "[FILE] FIRST packet $packetId, starting file data" }
            fileDataPacketNumber = packetId
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

~~~~
# FlySight 2 BLE on Linux

What was measured on Linux on 8 October 2026, with the same bench FlySight as on macOS, and the
scripts that did it. The macOS, Android and iPadOS results are in
`../ble-pairing-fixes-report.html`.

## Bench

- The bench FlySight 2, on its battery, ST-Link attached, USB cable unplugged. Firmware: branch
  `fix/ble_pairing_issues` with the trace of `Scripts/cli/ble_trace.py`.
- A laptop under Ubuntu 24.04: kernel 6.8, BlueZ 5.72, Intel AX211 adapter, `main.conf` as
  shipped (`Privacy` off). Public address `E4:0D:36:**:**:**`.
- The ST-Link is driven through OpenOCD: `vbus.py` and `ble_trace.py` now use it when
  `STM32_Programmer_CLI` is not installed. See `Scripts/cli/README.md`, section Linux.

## Results

### The FlySight seen from BlueZ alone (`bluez_probe.py`)

No SkyGames code here: the probe scans, connects, reads `FT_Packet_In` (which needs an encrypted
link) and disconnects.

| Situation | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Address the PC connects from | its public identity address, no resolvable private address (`CONNECTED ... peer=E4:0D:36:**:**:** (public) peerRPA=none`), like the Mac |
| First pairing, no BlueZ agent registered, pairing triggered by the read | refused: the FlySight records `PAIRING_COMPLETE status=2 reason=0x0c`, the read never completes, and the FlySight closes the link at its 30-second timeout |
| First pairing, no agent, `Device1.Pair` called explicitly | refused the same way (`org.bluez.Error.AuthenticationFailed` after 0.3 s) |
| First pairing, an agent registered | paired and bonded, read OK (244 bytes) 1.1 s after the request |
| Bonded, FlySight idle | connects in 0.8 s, encrypted read OK, no new pairing |
| Bonded, FlySight in pairing mode | connects in 0.9 s, encrypted read OK, no new pairing |
| Same two, with the first fix switched off (`ble_trace.py set privacy off`) | connects in both, read OK: **Linux is not affected by bug 1** |
| Pairing window left to expire | flag `01` for 30.4 s, then `00`, still advertising 256 s after the double press |

Why bug 1 does not apply here: with `Privacy` off, a Linux host gives the FlySight no identity
resolving key when it bonds, and the controller only ignores a peer's identity address when it
holds such a key for it. That last part is the specification as I read it, not something
measured; what is measured is that the connection goes through with the fix off.

So on Linux the firmware was never the obstacle. Without an agent, BlueZ keeps the adapter
non-bondable (`bluetoothctl show`: `Pairable: no`) and the kernel's request to confirm a "Just
Works" pairing finds nobody to answer. An application has to register an agent, and then pair.

### The native library of SkyGames (`fs_probe.py`)

`Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/c/linux/ble_linux.c` could not work: six functions of
the header were missing, D-Bus signals were never dispatched (so no scan result and no
notification reached the caller), and nothing dealt with pairing. It was rewritten on GDBus; see
`LINUX_IMPLEMENTATION.md` next to it. The probe loads the library and calls it as the app does.

| Situation | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| Scan | the three FlySights in range, with their pairing flag |
| First pairing (FlySight in pairing mode) | connected and bonded in 1.6 s, encrypted read OK, ping acknowledged |
| Bonded, FlySight idle | connected in 0.6 s, read OK, ping acknowledged |
| Bonded, FlySight in pairing mode | connected in 0.3 s, read OK, ping acknowledged |
| New process, saved identifier, no scan (what the app does when it starts) | connected in 0.6 s |
| Identifier never seen | refused at once (`BLE_ERROR_INVALID_PARAM`) |
| 40 s connected, ping every 14 s | link kept, every ping acknowledged |
| No ping | disconnect callback 30.1 s after the last write (the FlySight's timeout) |
| FlySight reset while connected | disconnect callback 0.5 s later |
| Reconnection after that reset | connected in 0.6 s |
| A FlySight this PC is not bonded wi
[... output cut at 4000 characters, 9528 in total ...]

package fr.hozakan.skygames.backend

import com.google.firebase.auth.AuthErrorCode
import com.google.firebase.auth.FirebaseAuth
import com.google.firebase.auth.FirebaseAuthException
import fr.hozakan.skygames.model.backend.ApiError
import io.ktor.http.HttpHeaders
import io.ktor.http.HttpStatusCode
import io.ktor.server.application.ApplicationCall
import io.ktor.server.application.createRouteScopedPlugin
import io.ktor.server.routing.Route
import io.ktor.server.routing.RouteSelector
import io.ktor.server.routing.RouteSelectorEvaluation
import io.ktor.server.routing.RoutingResolveContext
import io.ktor.util.AttributeKey
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext

/**
 * Who makes a call: the account of the Firebase ID token it carries. Not a data class: its text
 * form must never show the uid or the address.
 */
class Caller(
    val uid: String,
    /** The address of the Firebase account, when it has one. */
    val email: String?,
    /** Whether Firebase says that address was verified (by Google, by Apple, or by a link Firebase sent). */
    val emailVerified: Boolean,
    /** When the token stops being valid, in epoch milliseconds. */
    val expiresAt: Long
)

/** Tells whose call it is from its ID token. Firebase in the server, a fake in the tests. */
fun interface TokenVerifier {
    /**
     * The account [idToken] was issued to, or null when Firebase does not vouch for it (not a
     * token, expired, of another project, a disabled account). Throws when it cannot be told now.
     */
    suspend fun verify(idToken: String): Caller?
}

/** [FirebaseAuth.verifyIdToken] of the official Firebase Admin SDK: the signature, the project and the expiry. */
class FirebaseTokenVerifier(private val auth: FirebaseAuth) : TokenVerifier {
    override suspend fun verify(idToken: String): Caller? = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
        try {
            val verified = auth.verifyIdToken(idToken)
            val expiresAt = (verified.claims["exp"] as? Number)?.toLong()?.times(1000) ?: return@withContext null
            Caller(verified.uid, verified.email, verified.isEmailVerified, expiresAt)
        } catch (e: FirebaseAuthException) {
            // Google's public keys could not be fetched: nobody can be told apart for now.
            if (e.authErrorCode == AuthErrorCode.CERTIFICATE_FETCH_FAILED) {
                throw ApiFailure(HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable, ApiError.UNAVAILABLE, "The identity of the caller cannot be checked now")
            }
            null
        } catch (_: IllegalArgumentException) {
            null
        }
    }
}

// JNA spells the two 64-bit architectures "aarch64" and "x86-64" on all three systems.
// Only the spellings JNA itself normalises are accepted: it maps "x86_64" and "amd64" onto
// "x86-64", but it does NOT map "arm64" onto "aarch64" -- it would compute "linux-arm64".
// Accepting "arm64" here would therefore refile the library under a name JNA never looks for.
// "unknown" is deliberate rather than an exception: this is evaluated at configuration time, on
// every build including Android and iOS ones, and an unsupported host must not break those.
// The copy task turns it into a hard error, which is where failing is safe.
val nativeArchSuffix = when (nativeOsArch) {
    "aarch64" -> "aarch64"
    "x86_64", "amd64" -> "x86-64"
    else -> "unknown"
}

/*
 * The Firebase bridge of SkyGames as a program, for Linux.
 *
 * The Firebase C++ SDK ships its Linux libraries as static archives that are not position
 * independent: they link into a program, not into a shared library, so the JVM cannot load them
 * through JNA as it does on macOS and Windows. This program links them instead, and serves the
 * functions of skygames_firebase.h to the JVM over its standard input and output.
 *
 * One request per line, one answer per line, fields separated by a tab:
 *
 *     request:  <function> [<argument> ...]
 *     answer:   <status> <text>
 *
 * <status> is what the function returns, and <text> what it writes in its output buffer, when it
 * has one. Inside a field, a backslash, a tab, a line feed and a carriage return are written
 * \\, \t, \n and \r. The program ends when its input is closed, that is when the JVM is gone.
 *
 * These lines carry tokens: they must never be logged. The other side is FirebaseHelperProcess.kt.
 */
#include "skygames_firebase.h"

#include <csignal>
#include <cstdio>
#include <iostream>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

#include <unistd.h>

// A request this program does not understand. Not a value of skygames_firebase.h.
static const int kProtocolError = -100;

static std::string escape(const std::string& text) {
    std::string result;
    result.reserve(text.size() + 8);
    for (char c : text) {
        switch (c) {
            case '\\': result += "\\\\"; break;
            case '\t': result += "\\t";  break;
            case '\n': result += "\\n";  break;
            case '\r': result += "\\r";  break;
            default:   result += c;      break;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

static std::string unescape(const std::string& text) {
    std::string result;
    result.reserve(text.size());
    for (size_t i = 0; i < text.size(); i++) {
        if (text[i] != '\\' || i + 1 == text.size()) {
            result += text[i];
            continue;
        }
        switch (text[++i]) {
            case 't': result += '\t'; break;
            case 'n': result += '\n'; break;
            case 'r': result += '\r'; break;
            default:  result += text[i]; break;
        }
    }
    return result;
}

package fr.hozakan.skygames.user.firebase

import com.sun.jna.Platform
import java.io.BufferedReader
import java.io.BufferedWriter
import java.io.File
import java.nio.file.Files
import java.nio.file.Path
import java.nio.file.StandardCopyOption

import java.security.MessageDigest
import java.util.concurrent.Callable
import java.util.concurrent.Executors
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit

/**
 * [FirebaseNative] on Linux, where the bridge is a program instead of a library.
 *
 * The Firebase C++ SDK ships its Linux libraries as static archives that are not position
 * independent: they link into a program, not into a shared library, so JNA has nothing to load.
 * The functions of `skygames_firebase.h` are built into `skygames_firebase_helper` instead
 * (`src/nativeInterop/c/linux/firebase_helper_main.cpp`, which also describes the protocol), and
 * this class starts that program and asks it: one line for the request, one line for the answer.
 *
 * The program is started at the first call, and again if it has died; in that case it is
 * initialised again before anything else is asked. It ends by itself when its input closes, so
 * it never outlives the JVM.
 *
 * The lines exchanged carry tokens: nothing of them is ever logged, here or in the program.
 */
internal class FirebaseHelperProcess(
    private val executable: () -> Path = ::extractHelper,
) : FirebaseNative {

    private class Answer(val status: Int, val text: String)

    private val lock = Any()
    private var process: Process? = null
    private var writer: BufferedWriter? = null
    private var reader: BufferedReader? = null

    // What firebase_init was last given, to give it again to a program that had to be restarted
    private var initialised = false
    private var initPath: String? = null

    // The exchange runs on this thread so that the caller can stop waiting for an answer
    private val exchanges = Executors.newSingleThreadExecutor { task ->
        Thread(task, "firebase-helper").apply { isDaemon = true }
    }

    init {
        Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(Thread { synchronized(lock) { stop() } })
    }

    override fun firebase_init(googleServicesJsonPath: String?): Int = synchronized(lock) {
        val answer = ask(INIT, googleServicesJsonPath.orEmpty()) ?: return FirebaseNative.FIREBASE_ERROR_INIT_FAILED
        if (answer.status == FirebaseNative.FIREBASE_SUCCESS) {
            initialised = true
            initPath = googleServicesJsonPath
        }
        answer.status
    }

    override fun firebase_cleanup() = synchronized(lock) {
        // Closing its input ends the program, which cleans up on its way out

**Tool: Bash** — Document the Linux helper program and the Linux build requirements in the SkyGames docs

~~~~bash
cd ~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='docs/native-libraries.md'; s=open(p).read()
old='''Rebuild is automatic when sources change. To force a rebuild manually:
```bash
rm -f Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libskygames_firebase.<ext>
./gradlew :UserModule:buildNativeFirebaseLib
```
'''
new='''Rebuild is automatic when sources change. To force a rebuild manually:
```bash
rm -f Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libskygames_firebase.<ext>
./gradlew :UserModule:buildNativeFirebaseLib
```

**On Linux the bridge is a program, not a library** (checked 2026-10-08, SDK 13.13.0, Ubuntu
24.04). The build never compiles the Firebase C++ SDK: it downloads Google's binary distribution
and links its static libraries. Those of Linux are not position independent, so they cannot go
into a shared library (`relocation R_X86_64_PC32 ... can not be used when making a shared object`),
only into a program. The same functions are therefore built into `skygames_firebase_helper`,
which the JVM starts and talks to over its standard input and output:

- **Source:** `c/common/firebase_common.cpp`, unchanged, and `c/linux/firebase_helper_main.cpp`,
  which holds the protocol.
- **Build output:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/build/linux/skygames_firebase_helper`
- **Resource output:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/jvmMain/resources/<jna-prefix>/skygames_firebase_helper`
- **JVM side:** `FirebaseHelperProcess.kt`, picked by `FirebaseNative.INSTANCE` on Linux. It copies
  the program to `~/.cache/skygames/firebase-helper-<version>/` and runs it from there.
- **Needs** `libsecret-1-dev` to build (`sudo apt-get install libsecret-1-dev`), and a keyring at
  run time (GNOME Keyring, KWallet) for the session to survive a restart of the application.

The lines exchanged with that program carry tokens: nothing of them may be logged. A function
added to `skygames_firebase.h` has to be added to both ends of the protocol too.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)

old='''To force a rebuild after modifying native source code:
```bash
rm -f Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libflysight_ble.<ext>
./gradlew -p Libs/FlySightApi :core:buildNativeLib
```
'''
new='''To force a rebuild after modifying native source code:
```bash
rm -f Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/build/<platform>/libflysight_ble.<ext>
./gradlew -p Libs/FlySightApi :core:buildNativeLib
```

On Linux it needs `cmake` and `libglib2.0-dev`; what it does with BlueZ is described in
`Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/LINUX_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git status --short; git -C Libs/FlySightApi status --short

## Assistant (10:11)

Les tests BLE par scripts passent tous sous Linux, et SkyGames se compile et démarre maintenant sur ce PC. Il ne reste que le test dans la fenêtre SkyGames, qui attend ta connexion Google.

## Pourquoi ça ne marchait pas sous Linux

- **BlueZ exige un agent d'appairage.** Sans agent, l'adaptateur n'est pas « bondable » et l'appairage du FlySight est refusé ; le FlySight coupe au bout de 30 s. Le firmware n'y est pour rien.
- **La couche native Linux de FlySightApi n'était pas terminée** (ni scan, ni notifications, ni appairage). Je l'ai réécrite : [ble_linux.c](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/c/linux/ble_linux.c), décrite dans [LINUX_IMPLEMENTATION.md](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/LINUX_IMPLEMENTATION.md).
- **Le bug 1 ne touche pas Linux.** Mesuré : correctif coupé à chaud, Linux se connecte quand même, au repos comme en mode pairing.

## Résultats

| Niveau | Résultat |
|---|---|
| BlueZ seul | premier appairage, reconnexion au repos et en mode pairing, fenêtre de pairing inutilisée (`01` pendant 30 s, puis `00`, encore visible à 256 s) |
| Lib native SkyGames | idem, plus reconnexion par identifiant enregistré sans scan, déconnexions détectées, reprise après reset du FlySight |
| Couches Kotlin de FlySightApi | 40 connexions sur 40 avec lecture de `FLYSIGHT.TXT` et `CONFIG.TXT`, contre 7 sur 10 avant corrections |

Le détail et les scripts sont dans [debug_ble/linux/README.md](debug_ble/linux/README.md).

## Quatre défauts trouvés en répétant les connexions

- **Firmware**, [crs.c](FlySight/crs.c) : une commande arrivant juste derrière le dernier accusé de réception d'un fichier est jetée sans réponse. `CONFIG.TXT` restait bloqué 20 s environ une fois sur deux. Corrigé, et l'app renvoie désormais une demande restée sans réponse : 20 sur 20 même sur un firmware non corrigé.
- **Kotlin, trois défauts d'ordre et de concurrence** : notifications traitées en parallèle, accusés de réception envoyés dans le désordre, liste modifiée sans verrou. Résultat possible : un fichier tronqué accepté comme complet. Corrigés dans [GattTaskQueue.kt](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/ble/src/commonMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/task/GattTaskQueue.kt), [BleFileReader.kt](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/commonMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/core/internal/bluetooth/operation/BleFileReader.kt) et [DesktopKmpBleSocket.kt](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/ble/src/desktopMain/kotlin/ca/flysight/api/ble/DesktopKmpBleSocket.kt).

Les deux premiers fichiers Kotlin sont partagés avec Android et iOS : ça compile pour Android, mais je ne l'ai exécuté que sous Linux.

## SkyGames sous Linux

- **Firebase** : sous Linux, la passerelle est maintenant l'exécutable auxiliaire, [firebase_helper_main.cpp](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/c/linux/firebase_helper_main.cpp) côté C++ et [FirebaseHelperProcess.kt](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/jvmMain/kotlin/fr/hozakan/skygames/user/firebase/FirebaseHelperProcess.kt) côté JVM. L'app démarre, initialise le SDK et affiche « Sign in with Google » ; le processus s'arrête avec elle. La connexion elle-même n'est pas testée.
- **eSpeak-ng** ne compilait pas à cause de la longueur de ton dossier personnel (tampon de 160 caractères). Corrigé dans le [CMakeLists.txt d'AudioModule](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Modules/MiddleWare/AudioModule/src/nativeInterop/CMakeLists.txt).
- J'ai créé les deux `local.properties` (ignorés par git) avec `sdk.dir` ; les clés Google y sont vides.

## État laissé

- **Rien n'est commité**, dans aucun des trois dépôts. Le sous-module FlySightApi est en HEAD détachée sur `ce53315` : il faudra passer sur `release/1.1.0` avant de commiter.
- **La carte** tourne sur le firmware de la branche avec le correctif `crs.c` et la trace BLE. Ce PC y est appairé (4 appareils au total).
- Les outils de banc fonctionnent sans STM32CubeProgrammer, via OpenOCD : [Scripts/cli/README.md](Scripts/cli/README.md).

## Ce qu'il me faut pour finir

1. Renseigner `google.clientId` et `google.clientSecret` dans [local.properties](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/local.properties), avec les valeurs de ton Mac.
2. Lancer l'app, te connecter avec Google, puis la fermer :

```bash
~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/gradlew -p ~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames :composeApp:run
```

La session reste dans le trousseau ; je relancerai ensuite l'app dans une fenêtre imbriquée pour dérouler les tests BLE dans l'interface.

~~~~bash

p='README.md'; s=open(p).read()
start=s.index('### The SkyGames application itself: starts, BLE not exercised in its window yet')
end=s.index('## Observations with no change proposed')
new='''### The SkyGames application itself

SkyGames did not build on this PC, for two reasons that have nothing to do with BLE, both dealt
with in the SkyGames repository:

- eSpeak-ng keeps paths in a buffer of 160 characters, and the build tree under a long home
  directory overflowed it (`Bad vowel file`). The buffer is now 1024 (`AudioModule`).
- The Firebase C++ SDK ships static libraries for Linux that are not position independent, so
  `libskygames_firebase.so` could not be linked. On Linux the same functions are now built into
  a program the JVM talks to (`skygames_firebase_helper`, `UserModule`; see
  `docs/native-libraries.md` there). Signing in with Google works through it.

Then, in the window of SkyGames, signed in, with the bond removed on the PC first:

| Situation | Result |
|-----------|--------|
| "Add a device", FlySight in pairing mode | the three FlySights in range are listed; the bench one connects, pairs (`PAIRING_COMPLETE status=0` on the FlySight) and its configuration is shown |
| Disconnect, then Connect, FlySight idle | connected, configuration shown |
| Disconnect, FlySight put back in pairing mode, Connect | connected, configuration shown: the sequence the investigation started from |
| Application closed and started again | still signed in; reconnects by itself to the saved FlySight, configuration shown |

The application ran in a nested X server without a window manager and with software rendering,
which is enough for these tests but says nothing of how it looks on a normal desktop.

'''
s=s[:start]+new+s[end:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
grep -n "^### The SkyGames" README.md

---
name: linux-bench-setup
description: How the FlySight BLE bench and the SkyGames UI tests are driven on the Linux PC ([hostname])
metadata:
  type: reference
---

On the Linux PC (Ubuntu 24.04, BlueZ 5.72), set up on 2026-10-08:

- **Bench FlySight**: on battery, ST-Link V3 attached. `Scripts/cli/vbus.py` and `ble_trace.py` work through OpenOCD (no STM32CubeProgrammer here). A udev rule gives the user access to the ST-Link; no sudo is available to me, the user runs sudo commands when asked.
- **Firmware builds**: no CubeIDE project build here; a Makefile in the session scratchpad compiled an exported tree with `arm-none-eabi-gcc` 13.2 (include paths taken from `.cproject`), flashed with `openocd ... -c "program x.elf verify reset exit"`. `ble_trace.py` needs the ELF that is running (`FLYSIGHT_ELF`).
- **Test scripts and results**: `debug_ble/linux/` in the firmware repo (BlueZ probe, probe for SkyGames' native library, headless JVM probe for FlySightApi, README with every result).
- **SkyGames UI tests without touching the user's pointer**: start `Xephyr :99` with an xauth file, run `./gradlew :composeApp:run` with `DISPLAY=:99 SKIKO_RENDER_API=SOFTWARE`, drive it with `xdotool`, screenshot with PIL `ImageGrab.grab(xdisplay=":99")`, resize the app window with `xdotool windowsize` (there is no window manager). The Google sign-in opens in the user's Chrome on the real display; the user completes it, and the session then persists in the keyring.
- SkyGames checkout: `~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames`, branch `release/1.1.0`; `local.properties` (git-ignored) holds `sdk.dir` and the user's Google keys.
- Gotcha: `pkill -f PATTERN` kills the calling shell when PATTERN also appears literally elsewhere in the same command line; use a bracket (`[X]ephyr`) and keep the plain text out of the command.

Related: [[link-files-and-show-commands]], [[no-ai-signature-in-commits]].

#!/bin/bash
# usage: build_variant.sh <git ref> <name> [patch]

PY

package fr.hozakan.skygames

import androidx.compose.runtime.CompositionLocalProvider
import androidx.compose.runtime.remember
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.painter.BitmapPainter
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.painter.Painter
import androidx.compose.ui.graphics.toComposeImageBitmap
import androidx.compose.ui.window.Window
import androidx.compose.ui.window.WindowPlacement
import androidx.compose.ui.window.application
import androidx.compose.ui.window.rememberWindowState
import ca.flysight.api.FlySightApi
import fr.hozakan.skygames.di.initKoin
import fr.hozakan.skygames.ui.auth.AccountFullscreenController
import fr.hozakan.skygames.ui.auth.LocalAccountFullscreenController
import io.github.aakira.napier.DebugAntilog
import io.github.aakira.napier.Napier
import org.jetbrains.skia.Image
import org.koin.java.KoinJavaComponent.getKoin

fun main() {
    Napier.base(DebugAntilog())
    initKoin()
    Runtime.getRuntime().addShutdownHook(Thread {
        try {
            getKoin().get<FlySightApi>().cancel()
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            // Koin may already be closed
        }
    })
    application {
        val windowState = rememberWindowState(placement = WindowPlacement.Maximized)
        val fullscreen = remember(windowState) {
            AccountFullscreenController {
                val previous = windowState.placement
                windowState.placement = WindowPlacement.Fullscreen
                return@AccountFullscreenController { windowState.placement = previous }
            }
        }
        Window(
            onCloseRequest = ::exitApplication,
            title = "SkyGames",
            icon = remember { classpathPainter("skygames_icon.png") },
            state = windowState,
        ) {
            CompositionLocalProvider(LocalAccountFullscreenController provides fullscreen) {
                App()
            }
        }
    }
}

/**
 * A PNG of this application's classpath (its `resources` directory), for the window icon — what
 * the deprecated `painterResource(String)` did, without the Compose resources library, which
 * would also ship the image in the Android and iOS builds.
 */
private fun classpathPainter(name: String): Painter {
    val bytes = requireNotNull(Thread.currentThread().contextClassLoader.getResourceAsStream(name)) {
        "$name is missing from the classpath"
    }.use { it.readBytes() }
    return BitmapPainter(Image.makeFromEncoded(bytes).toComposeImageBitmap())
}
~~~~

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""State of the SkyGames window in the nested display, read from a few pixels.

img = ImageGrab.grab(xdisplay=os.environ.get("DISPLAY", ":99")).convert("RGB")
if len(sys.argv) > 1:
    small = img.resize((int(img.width * 0.5), int(img.height * 0.5))); small.save(sys.argv[1])

    print("connected"); sys.exit(0)
r, g, b = img.getpixel((600, 450))        # the yellow Connect button, middle of the card
if r > 200 and 140 < g < 215 and b < 70:
    print("disconnected"); sys.exit(0)
r, g, b = img.getpixel((640, 300))        # the grey of an open card, against the white of the home screen

EOF

state() { python3 \$S/gui/uistate.py "\$@"; }
wait_state() { for i in \$(seq 1 \$2); do [ "\$(state)" = "\$1" ] && return 0; sleep 1; done; return 1; }
ensure_card() { [ "\$(state)" = "home" ] && { \$S/gui/ui.sh click 416 366; sleep 2; }; true; }
connect_check() {   # \$1 = label

  [ "\$(state)" = "disconnected" ] && \$S/gui/ui.sh click 640 450
  if wait_state connected 25; then
    for i in \$(seq 1 25); do sed -n "\$((N+1)),\\\$p" \$S/skygames-run.log | grep -q "readConfigFile: final _configFile=" && break; sleep 1; done
    sleep 1; state \$L/ui_\$1.png >/dev/null
    echo "SkyGames, \$1 : connected; \$(sed -n "\$((N+1)),\\\$p" \$S/skygames-run.log | grep -o 'readConfigFile: final _configFile=[A-Za-z]*' | tail -1 | sed 's/readConfigFile: final _configFile=/configuration /'); second requests=\$(sed -n "\$((N+1)),\\\$p" \$S/skygames-run.log | grep -c 'sending it again')"
  else
    state \$L/ui_\$1.png >/dev/null; echo "SkyGames, \$1 : NOT CONNECTED after 25 s (state=\$(state))"
  fi
}
disconnect() { [ "\$(state)" = "connected" ] && \$S/gui/ui.sh click 1190 87; wait_state disconnected 10 || echo "  (still \$(state) after Disconnect)"; }
ensure_card
[ "\$(state)" = "connected" ] && disconnect
sleep 2
connect_check "idle   "
disconnect; sleep 3
python3 \$CLI/vbus.py button >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
connect_check "pairing"
disconnect
EOF

**Tool: Bash** — Read a few firmware state variables over SWD while the FlySight is silent

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; E=$S/four/master-patched/build/master-patched.elf; arm-none-eabi-nm -S $E | grep -E " (request_pairing|BleApplicationContext|button_state|state|mode_state|timeout_flag|rx_read_index|rx_write_index|Custom_App_Context|next_ack|last_packet|next_packet|queue_read|queue_write|enable_ble)$" | sort; cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli && python3 - "$E" <<'EOF'
import subprocess, sys, types, vbus
elf = sys.argv[1]
out = subprocess.run(["arm-none-eabi-nm", "-S", elf], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
syms = {}
for line in out.splitlines():
    p = line.split()
    if len(p) == 4: syms.setdefault(p[3], []).append((int(p[0], 16), int(p[1], 16)))
swd = vbus.connect(types.SimpleNamespace(programmer=None, openocd=None, sn=None, swd_timeout=10))
for name in ["request_pairing", "button_state", "state", "timeout_flag", "rx_read_index", "rx_write_index", "next_ack", "last_packet", "next_packet", "queue_read", "queue_write"]:

**Tool: Bash** — Make the native library give its notification sessions back to BlueZ when a link ends (source only for now)

~~~~bash
cd ~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop && python3 - <<'EOF'
p='c/linux/ble_linux.c'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old)==1,(s.count(old),old[:60]); s=s.replace(old,new)

rep('''static void call_and_forget(const char *path, const char *interface, const char *method) {
    GDBusProxy *proxy = get_interface(path, interface);

    if (proxy) {
        g_dbus_proxy_call(proxy, method, NULL, G_DBUS_CALL_FLAGS_NONE, CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, NULL,
                          call_done, (gpointer) method);
        g_object_unref(proxy);
    }
}
''','''static void call_and_forget(const char *path, const char *interface, const char *method) {
    GDBusProxy *proxy = get_interface(path, interface);

    if (proxy) {
        g_dbus_proxy_call(proxy, method, NULL, G_DBUS_CALL_FLAGS_NONE, CALL_TIMEOUT_MS, NULL,
                          call_done, (gpointer) method);
        g_object_unref(proxy);
    }
}

/*
 * BlueZ keeps a notification session for as long as the program that asked for it is on the bus,
 * across disconnections, and turns the notifications on again by itself at the next connection.
 * It also emits each notification once per session: with a session left behind by this program
 * and one of another program, both would receive everything twice. So a link that ends gives
 * its sessions back.
 */
static void stop_notifications(link_t *link) {
    GHashTableIter iter;
    gpointer path;

    g_hash_table_iter_init(&iter, link->subscriptions);
    while (g_hash_table_iter_next(&iter, &path, NULL)) {
        GDBusProxy *proxy = get_interface(path, GATT_CHAR_IFACE);
        if (proxy) {
            /* Nothing to do about a failure, and nothing to say: the session is gone either way */
            g_dbus_proxy_call(proxy, "StopNotify", NULL, G_DBUS_CALL_FLAGS_NONE, CALL_TIMEOUT_MS,
                              NULL, NULL, NULL);
            g_object_unref(proxy);
        }
    }
}
''')
rep('''static void link_free(gpointer data) {
    link_t *link = data;

    remove_source(&link->discovery_timer);
''','''static void link_free(gpointer data) {
    link_t *link = data;

    stop_notifications(link);
    remove_source(&link->discovery_timer);
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/four/stale_subscriber.py`

~~~~
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduces what an idle application left behind before the library gave its sessions back:
connects to the bonded FlySight, starts notifications on its characteristics, disconnects, and
stays on the bus. BlueZ then emits every notification twice for whoever connects next.

usage: stale_subscriber.py [seconds to stay]
"""
import sys, time
import dbus, dbus.mainloop.glib
from gi.repository import GLib

STAY = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 300
dbus.mainloop.glib.DBusGMainLoop(set_as_default=True)
bus = dbus.SystemBus()
ctx = GLib.MainLoop().get_context()


def pump(seconds):
    end = time.time() + seconds
    while time.time() < end:
        ctx.iteration(False)
        time.sleep(0.02)


def objects():
    return dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', '/'), 'org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager').GetManagedObjects()


path = next(p for p, i in objects().items()
            if 'org.bluez.Device1' in i and str(i['org.bluez.Device1'].get('Name', '')) == 'FlySight'
            and i['org.bluez.Device1'].get('Paired'))
device = dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', path), 'org.bluez.Device1')
props = dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', path), 'org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties')
device.Connect()
for _ in range(100):
    if props.Get('org.bluez.Device1', 'ServicesResolved'):
        break
    pump(0.1)
started = 0
for p, i in objects().items():
    c = i.get('org.bluez.GattCharacteristic1')
    if p.startswith(path + '/') and c and ('notify' in c['Flags'] or 'indicate' in c['Flags']):
        try:
            dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', p), 'org.bluez.GattCharacteristic1').StartNotify()
            started += 1
        except dbus.DBusException:
            pass
pump(1.0)
device.Disconnect()
print('stale subscriber: %d notification sessions left behind, staying %.0f s' % (started, STAY), flush=True)
pump(STAY)
~~~~

#!/bin/bash
# usage: repro.sh <attempt>   Replays the sequence after which master + patch went silent, with every
# notification doubled by a stale subscriber, then listens for the FlySight.
N=$1
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli; LNX=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux
P=$LNX/jvm-probe/build/install/fs-jvm-probe/bin/fs-jvm-probe; ID=58:6B:2A:E4:31:C1
L=$S/four/repro; mkdir -p $L
(python3 $S/four/stale_subscriber.py 150 > $L/stale_$N.log 2>&1 &)
for i in $(seq 1 30); do grep -q "stale subscriber" $L/stale_$N.log && break; sleep 1; done
cat $L/stale_$N.log
sleep 3
timeout 90 python3 $LNX/fs_probe.py connect --flag 00 > $L/lib_idle_$N.log 2>&1; echo "library, idle    : exit=$? $(grep -c 'notification' $L/lib_idle_$N.log) notification lines"
python3 $CLI/vbus.py button > /dev/null; timeout 90 python3 $LNX/fs_probe.py connect --flag 01 > $L/lib_pair_$N.log 2>&1; echo "library, pairing : exit=$?"
sleep 3
timeout 120 $P FlySight $ID > $L/jvm_idle_$N.log 2>&1; echo "Kotlin, idle     : exit=$? $(grep -o 'config.txt[^|]*' $L/jvm_idle_$N.log | cut -c1-40); packets received twice=$(grep -c 'OLD packet' $L/jvm_idle_$N.log) NAK=$(grep -c 'received cmd NAK' $L/jvm_idle_$N.log) second requests=$(grep -c 'sending it again' $L/jvm_idle_$N.log)"
sleep 2; python3 $CLI/vbus.py button > /dev/null; sleep 1
timeout 120 $P FlySight $ID > $L/jvm_pair_$N.log 2>&1; echo "Kotlin, pairing  : exit=$? $(grep -o 'connect() -> [A-Za-z]* after [0-9]* ms' $L/jvm_pair_$N.log)"
python3 $LNX/scan.py 12 > $L/scan_$N.log 2>&1
echo "adverts from the FlySight in the 12 s that follow: $(grep -c "name='FlySight' " $L/scan_$N.log)"
echo REPRO_DONE $N

#!/bin/bash
# The perturbed sequence, repeated on several firmwares, to see which ones end in the error handler.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 8; }
in_error_handler() {   # says where the firmware is executing, from the given ELF
  PC=$(timeout 20 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}" -c "init" -c "halt" -c "echo [format PC=%s [reg pc]]" -c "resume" -c "exit" 2>&1 | grep "^PC=" | grep -o "0x[0-9a-f]*" | tail -1)
  echo "firmware is in: $(arm-none-eabi-addr2line -f -e $1 $PC | head -1)"
}
run() {   # $1 = label, $2 = elf, $3... = attempt names
  LABEL=$1; ELF=$2; shift 2
  echo "################ $LABEL"; flash $ELF
  for A in "$@"; do
    echo "--- attempt $A"
    "$S/four/repro.sh" $A | grep -v "stale subscriber\|REPRO_DONE"
    in_error_handler $ELF
    python3 $CLI/vbus.py reset --settle 6 > /dev/null 2>&1
    sleep 4
  done
}
run "branch firmware (with the file-transfer fix)" $S/fw/build/flysight.elf b2
run "master 9ec7186, unmodified" $S/four/master-unmodified/build/master-unmodified.elf u1 u2 u3
run "master + patch" $S/four/master-patched/build/master-patched.elf p2 p3
echo "################ back to the bench firmware"; flash $S/fw/build/flysight.elf
echo SERIES_DONE
~~~~

'''
new='''### Notification sessions outlive the link

`StartNotify` opens a session that BlueZ keeps for as long as the program that asked for it is
on the bus: across disconnections, turning the notifications on again by itself at the next
connection, whoever makes it. And BlueZ emits each notification once per session, to everybody.
An application that stayed open after a disconnection therefore made every other program
connected to the same FlySight receive each notification twice, which is enough to derail a file
transfer. When a link ends, the library calls `StopNotify` on everything it had subscribed to.

Two programs connected to the same FlySight at the same time, both subscribed, still get every
notification twice: that is how the D-Bus API of BlueZ behaves.

### The Battery Service
'''
assert s.count(old)==1; s=s.replace(old,new); open(p,'w').write(s)

## Assistant (11:35)

Le jeu de tests est refait sur les quatre firmwares du rapport, et tout passe sous Linux. Il a aussi fait apparaître un blocage du firmware, indépendant du patch et non corrigé.

## Les quatre firmwares, depuis Linux

| Firmware | Lib native (repos / pairing) | Pile Kotlin (repos / pairing) | SkyGames (repos / pairing) | Fenêtre de pairing inutilisée |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `master` 9ec7186, non modifié | OK / OK | OK / OK | OK / OK | `01` 30 s, puis `00`, encore visible à 255 s |
| `master` + patch | OK / OK | OK / OK | OK / OK | `01` 30 s, puis `00`, encore visible à 256 s |
| `develop` e67ee9f, non modifié | OK / OK | OK / OK | OK / OK | `01` pendant 209 s, puis plus rien (bug 2) |
| `develop` + patch | OK / OK | OK / OK | OK / OK | `01` 30 s, puis `00`, encore visible à 255 s |

- **Bug 1** : Linux se connecte aussi sur les deux firmwares non modifiés, donc il n'est pas concerné.
- **Bug 2** : visible depuis Linux sur `develop` non modifié, supprimé par le patch.
- La ligne `master` + patch est son second passage ; le premier a échoué pour les deux raisons ci-dessous.

## Ce que le premier passage a révélé

- **Un défaut de ma couche native, corrigé.** SkyGames restée ouverte gardait ses abonnements BlueZ après déconnexion, et BlueZ envoyait alors chaque notification en double à tous les programmes. [ble_linux.c](/home/[user]/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames/Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/c/linux/ble_linux.c) résilie maintenant ses abonnements à la fin d'un lien ; vérifié, plus aucun doublon.
- **Un blocage du firmware, non corrigé.** Dans ces sessions perturbées, le FlySight s'est retrouvé dans `Error_Handler()` : boucle infinie, plus de BLE jusqu'à un reset. Pile lue par SWD : demande de lecture → `FatFS_Init` → `f_mount` échoue ([resource_manager.c](FlySight/resource_manager.c)).
  - Rejoué volontairement : 2 sessions sur 4 sur `master` + patch, 1 sur 4 sur `master` non modifié, donc le patch n'en est pas la cause. 0 sur 2 sur le firmware de la branche.
  - Je n'ai pas établi pourquoi le montage échoue à ce moment-là.

## Affichage de SkyGames sous Linux

}

static FS_ResourceManager_Result_t FatFS_Init(void)
{
	FS_ResourceManager_Result_t ret = FS_RESOURCE_MANAGER_FAILURE;

	if (resource_counts[FS_RESOURCE_FATFS] == 0)
	{
		/* Initialize microSD */
		if (FS_ResourceManager_RequestResource(FS_RESOURCE_MICROSD)
				== FS_RESOURCE_MANAGER_SUCCESS)
		{
			/* Initialize FatFS */
			if (MX_FATFS_Init() != APP_OK)
			{
				Error_Handler();
			}

			/* Enable microSD card */
			if (f_mount(&fs, "0:/", 1) != FR_OK)
			{
				Error_Handler();
			}

			++resource_counts[FS_RESOURCE_FATFS];

			ret =  FS_RESOURCE_MANAGER_SUCCESS;
		}
	}

	return ret;
}

static void FatFS_DeInit(void)
{
	if (resource_counts[FS_RESOURCE_FATFS] == 1)
	{
		--resource_counts[FS_RESOURCE_FATFS];

		/* Disable microSD card */
		if (f_mount(0, "0:/", 0) != FR_OK)
		{
			Error_Handler();
		}

		/* Disable FatFS */
		if (MX_FATFS_DeInit() != APP_OK)
		{
			Error_Handler();
		}

		/* De-initialize microSD */
		FS_ResourceManager_ReleaseResource(FS_RESOURCE_MICROSD);
	}
	else
	{
		Error_Handler();
	}
}

/**
  * @brief  Initializes the SD/SD communication.
  * @param  None
  * @retval The SD Response:
  *         - MSD_ERROR: Sequence failed
  *         - MSD_OK: Sequence succeed
  */
uint8_t BSP_SD_Init(void)
{
  uint8_t result;

  /* Configure IO functionalities for SD pin */
  SD_IO_Init();

  /* SD detection pin is not physically mapped on the Adafruit shield */
  SdStatus = SD_PRESENT;

  /* SD initialized and set to SPI mode properly */
  result = SD_GoIdleState();

  if (result == BSP_SD_OK)
  {
    if (SD_EnableHighSpeedMode() == BSP_SD_OK)
    {
      /* Card accepted SD high-speed mode; restore CubeMX operating speed. */
      SD_IO_SetFastSpeed();
    }
    else
    {
      /* Keep cards that stay in default-speed mode below the 25 MHz limit. */
      SD_IO_SetDefaultSpeed();
    }
  }

  return result;
}

S="[scratchpad]"; cd $S/four && rm -rf master-diag && cp -a master-unmodified master-diag && cd master-diag && python3 - <<'PY'
import re
p='FlySight/resource_manager.c'; s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''static FATFS fs;
''','''static FATFS fs;

/* DIAG: one entry per mount attempt, read over SWD */
volatile struct
{
	uint32_t off_tick;
	uint32_t count;
	struct
	{
		uint32_t gap_ms;     /* time the card stayed without power before this mount */
		uint8_t  fr;         /* result of f_mount */
		uint8_t  stage;      /* where SD_GoIdleState stopped */
		uint8_t  tries;      /* CMD0 attempts */
		uint8_t  r1;         /* last R1 answer */
	} log[32];
} fs_diag;
extern volatile uint8_t sd_diag_stage, sd_diag_tries, sd_diag_r1;
''',1)
s=s.replace('''			/* Disable VCC */
			HAL_GPIO_WritePin(VCC_EN_GPIO_Port, VCC_EN_Pin, GPIO_PIN_RESET);
''','''			/* Disable VCC */
			HAL_GPIO_WritePin(VCC_EN_GPIO_Port, VCC_EN_Pin, GPIO_PIN_RESET);
			fs_diag.off_tick = HAL_GetTick();
''',1)
s=s.replace('''			/* Enable microSD card */
			if (f_mount(&fs, "0:/", 1) != FR_OK)
			{
				Error_Handler();
			}
''','''			/* Enable microSD card */
			{
				uint32_t gap = HAL_GetTick() - fs_diag.off_tick;
				FRESULT fr = f_mount(&fs, "0:/", 1);
				uint32_t i = fs_diag.count++ & 31;
				fs_diag.log[i].gap_ms = fs_diag.off_tick ? gap : 0xffffffff;
				fs_diag.log[i].fr = fr;
				fs_diag.log[i].stage = sd_diag_stage;
				fs_diag.log[i].tries = sd_diag_tries;
				fs_diag.log[i].r1 = sd_diag_r1;
				if (fr != FR_OK)
				{
					Error_Handler();
				}
			}
''',1)
open(p,'w').write(s)

a=s.index('uint8_t SD_GoIdleState(void)\n{'); b=s.index('uint8_t SD_ReadData(void)')
body=s[a:b]
n=[0]

    return 'do { sd_diag_stage = %d; sd_diag_r1 = response.r1; return BSP_SD_ERROR; } while (0);' % n[0]

body=body.replace('  return BSP_SD_OK;\n}','  sd_diag_stage = 100; sd_diag_r1 = response.r1;\n  return BSP_SD_OK;\n}',1)

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/sd/read_diag.py`

~~~~
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reads over SWD what the diagnostic firmware recorded about each mount of the microSD card.

usage: read_diag.py <elf>
"""
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

ELF = sys.argv[1]
FR = {0: 'FR_OK', 1: 'FR_DISK_ERR', 2: 'FR_INT_ERR', 3: 'FR_NOT_READY', 13: 'FR_NO_FILESYSTEM'}
STAGE = {0: 'not run', 1: 'CMD0: no idle answer', 2: 'ACMD41 (v1 fallback)', 3: 'CMD58', 4: 'CMD8 answer', 100: 'ok'}


def symbol(name):
    out = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) == 4 and parts[3] == name:
            return int(parts[0], 16), int(parts[1], 16)
    raise SystemExit('no symbol ' + name)


addr, size = symbol('fs_diag')
words = size // 4
out = subprocess.run(
    ['openocd', '-f', 'interface/stlink.cfg', '-c', 'transport select hla_swd', '-f', 'target/stm32wbx.cfg',
     '-c', 'stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}', '-c', 'init', '-c', 'halt',
     '-c', 'echo [format PC=%s [reg pc]]', '-c', 'mdw 0x%08x %d' % (addr, words), '-c', 'resume', '-c', 'exit'],
    capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)
text = out.stdout + out.stderr
pc = re.findall(r'PC=.*?(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)', text)
data = []
for line in text.splitlines():
    m = re.match(r'^0x[0-9a-f]+: (.*)$', line.strip())
    if m:
        data += [int(w, 16) for w in m.group(1).split()]
if len(data) < words:
    raise SystemExit('SWD read failed:\n' + text)
raw = struct.pack('<%dI' % words, *data[:words])
off_tick, count = struct.unpack_from('<II', raw, 0)
where = '?'
if pc:
    where = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-addr2line', '-f', '-e', ELF, pc[-1]],
                           capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()[0]
print('firmware is in: %s   mounts recorded: %d' % (where, count))
first = max(0, count - 32)
for n in range(first, count):
    gap, fr, stage, tries, r1 = struct.unpack_from('<IBBBB', raw, 8 + 8 * (n & 31))
    gap_text = 'first since boot' if gap == 0xffffffff else '%6d ms without power' % gap
    print('  mount %3d: %-22s f_mount=%-16s SD init: %-22s CMD0 tries=%3d last R1=0x%02x'
          % (n + 1, gap_text, FR.get(fr, str(fr)), STAGE.get(stage, str(stage)), tries, r1))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Makes a bonded FlySight mount its microSD card twice, a chosen time apart.

Each READ of a file that does not exist makes the firmware power the card, mount it, answer NAK,
unmount it and cut its power. The second READ is written <delay> ms after the answer to the first
one (or right behind the first one with --back-to-back), then a ping says whether the firmware
is still alive.

usage: sd_remount.py <delay ms> [--back-to-back] [--pairs N]
"""
import argparse
import sys
import time

import dbus
import dbus.mainloop.glib
from gi.repository import GLib

FT_IN = '00000002-8e22-4541-9d4c-21edae82ed19'
DEV = 'org.bluez.Device1'
CHR = 'org.bluez.GattCharacteristic1'
READ_MISSING = bytes([0x02]) + bytes(8) + b'/NOFILE.TXT'
PING = bytes([0xfe])

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('delay', type=float)
parser.add_argument('--back-to-back', action='store_true')
parser.add_argument('--pairs', type=int, default=1)
args = parser.parse_args()

dbus.mainloop.glib.DBusGMainLoop(set_as_default=True)
bus = dbus.SystemBus()
ctx = GLib.MainLoop().get_context()
t0 = time.time()
received = []


def log(msg):
    print('%7.3f %s' % (time.time() - t0, msg), flush=True)


def pump(seconds, until=None):
    end = time.time() + seconds
    while time.time() < end:
        while ctx.iteration(False):
            pass
        if until and until():
            return True
        time.sleep(0.002)
    return False


def objects():
    return dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', '/'), 'org.freedesktop.DBus.ObjectManager').GetManagedObjects()


path = next((p for p, i in objects().items()
             if DEV in i and str(i[DEV].get('Name', '')) == 'FlySight' and i[DEV].get('Paired')), None)
if not path:
    sys.exit('no bonded FlySight known to BlueZ')
device = dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', path), DEV)
props = dbus.Interface(bus.get_object('org.bluez', path), 'org.freedesktop.DBus.Properties')
for attempt in range(3):

except dbus.DBusException:

pump(0.5)
print('RESULT delay=%g back_to_back=%s alive=%s' % (args.delay, args.back_to_back, alive))
sys.exit(0 if alive else 4)

	uint32_t ssr, tr, ssr2, prediv_s, sec;
	do { ssr = RTC->SSR; tr = RTC->TR; ssr2 = RTC->SSR; } while (ssr != ssr2);
	prediv_s = RTC->PRER & 0x7fff;
	sec = ((tr >> 20) & 3) * 36000 + ((tr >> 16) & 0xf) * 3600 + ((tr >> 12) & 7) * 600
			+ ((tr >> 8) & 0xf) * 60 + ((tr >> 4) & 7) * 10 + (tr & 0xf);
	fs_diag.prer = RTC->PRER;
	return sec * (prediv_s + 1) + (prediv_s - (ssr & 0xffff));
}

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/sd/sweep.sh`

~~~~
#!/bin/bash
# usage: sweep.sh <elf> <delay ms>...   One pair of mounts per delay, then what the firmware recorded.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli
ELF=$1; shift
for D in "$@"; do
  if [ "$D" = "b2b" ]; then
    R=$(timeout 60 python3 $S/sd/sd_remount.py 0 --back-to-back 2>&1 | grep RESULT)
  else
    R=$(timeout 60 python3 $S/sd/sd_remount.py $D 2>&1 | grep RESULT)
  fi
  echo "### delay=$D  ${R:-no result}"
  python3 $S/sd/read_diag.py $ELF | tail -2
  if ! echo "$R" | grep -q "alive=True"; then
    python3 $CLI/vbus.py reset --settle 6 > /dev/null 2>&1
    sleep 6
  fi
  sleep 2
done
echo SWEEP_DONE
~~~~

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/sd/diag_repro.sh`

~~~~
#!/bin/bash
# usage: diag_repro.sh <elf> <attempt name>...
# Replays the perturbed session on the diagnostic firmware until it ends in the error handler,
# and prints what the firmware recorded about its mounts each time.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli
ELF=$1; shift
for A in "$@"; do
  echo "--- attempt $A  $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  "$S/four/repro.sh" $A | grep -v "stale subscriber\|REPRO_DONE"
  D=$(python3 $S/sd/read_diag.py $ELF)
  echo "$D"
  if echo "$D" | grep -q "firmware is in: Error_Handler"; then
    echo "LOCKED on attempt $A"
    break
  fi
  python3 $CLI/vbus.py reset --settle 6 > /dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 4
done
echo DIAG_REPRO_DONE
~~~~

static void Custom_CRS_OnConnect(Custom_App_ConnHandle_Not_evt_t *pNotification)
{
  // Reset buffer indices
  tx_read_index = 0;
  tx_write_index = 0;

  rx_read_index = 0;
  rx_write_index = 0;

  start_read_index = 0;
  start_write_index = 0;

  // Update state
  connected_flag = 1;

  // Remember connection handle
  Custom_App_Context.ConnectionHandle = pNotification->ConnectionHandle;

  // Start timeout timer
  HW_TS_Start(timeout_timer_id, TIMEOUT_TICKS);
}

static void Custom_CRS_OnDisconnect(void)
{
  // Stop timeout timer
  HW_TS_Stop(timeout_timer_id);

  // Update state
  connected_flag = 0;

  // Call update task
  UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1<<CFG_TASK_FS_CRS_UPDATE_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
}

	UTIL_SEQ_SetTask(1<<CFG_TASK_FS_CRS_UPDATE_ID, CFG_SCH_PRIO_1);
