**Tool: Bash** — Read the pairing mode module of the firmware

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; T=$S/four/master-unmodified; sed -n 24,200p $T/FlySight/pairing_mode.c
~~~~
Result:

~~~~
#include "main.h"
#include "app_ble.h"
#include "app_common.h"
#include "led.h"
#include "mode.h"

static void FS_PairingMode_Callback(void)
{
	FS_Mode_PushQueue(FS_MODE_EVENT_FORCE_UPDATE);
}

void FS_PairingMode_Init(void)
{
	// Initialize LEDs
	FS_LED_SetColour(FS_LED_GREEN);
	FS_LED_Pulse();

	// Request pairing
	APP_BLE_RequestPairing(FS_PairingMode_Callback);
}

void FS_PairingMode_DeInit(void)
{
	// Turn off LEDs
	FS_LED_Off();

	// Cancel pairing
	APP_BLE_CancelPairing();
}
~~~~

{
	while (!FS_Mode_QueueEmpty())

/* Cache of CubeMX-configured SPI2 CR1.BR bits so we can restore the exact
 * operating-mode SPI speed after SD initialization. */
static uint32_t sd_spi2_fast_br_bits = 0;
static uint8_t  sd_spi2_fast_br_valid = 0;

/**
  * @brief  Set SPI2 to fast speed for SD card data transfer (CubeMX configured)
  * @retval None
  */
void SD_IO_SetFastSpeed(void)
{
  if (sd_spi2_fast_br_valid)
  {
    /* Restore prescaler configured by CubeMX in MX_SPI2_Init() */
    SD_SPI_SetPrescaler(sd_spi2_fast_br_bits);
  }
  else
  {
    /* Fallback: CubeMX default used previously */
    SD_SPI_SetPrescaler(SPI_BAUDRATEPRESCALER_2);
  }
}

/**
  * @brief  Set SPI2 to default-speed SD data transfer (16 MHz).
  * @retval None
  */
void SD_IO_SetDefaultSpeed(void)
{
  /* 64 MHz / 4 = 16 MHz, below the 25 MHz SD default-speed limit. */
  SD_SPI_SetPrescaler(SPI_BAUDRATEPRESCALER_4);
}

void UTIL_SEQ_Idle(void)
{
#if (CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED == 1)
  if (FS_Mode_State() == FS_MODE_STATE_SLEEP)
  {
    UTIL_LPM_EnterLowPower();
  }
#endif /* CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED == 1 */
  return;
}

void UTIL_SEQ_PreIdle(void)
{
#if (CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED == 1)
  SHCI_CmdStatus_t status;

  if ((SystemClockCommandPending == 0U) &&
      (SystemClockHandoffToHse == 0U) &&
      (CPU2_Started != 0U) &&
      (FS_Mode_State() == FS_MODE_STATE_SLEEP) &&
      (UTIL_LPM_GetMode() != UTIL_LPM_SLEEPMODE) &&
      (LL_RCC_GetSysClkSource() == LL_RCC_SYS_CLKSOURCE_STATUS_PLL))
  {
    LL_RCC_HSE_Enable();

    SystemClockCommandPending = 1U;
    status = SHCI_C2_SetSystemClock(SET_SYSTEM_CLOCK_PLL_ON_TO_HSE);
    SystemClockCommandPending = 0U;

    if (status != SHCI_Success)
    {
      Error_Handler();
    }

    SystemClockHandoffToHse = 1U;
    SystemCoreClockUpdate();
    HAL_InitTick(HAL_GetTickPrio());
  }
#endif /* CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED == 1 */
  return;
}

void UTIL_SEQ_PostIdle(void)
{
#if (CFG_LPM_SUPPORTED == 1)
  SHCI_CmdStatus_t status;

  if ((SystemClockCommandPending == 0U) &&
      (SystemClockHandoffToHse != 0U))
  {
    LL_RCC_PLL_Enable();

    SystemClockCommandPending = 1U;
    status = SHCI_C2_SetSystemClock(SET_SYSTEM_CLOCK_HSE_TO_PLL);
    SystemClockCommandPending = 0U;

    if (status != SHCI_Success)
    {
      Error_Handler();
    }

    SystemClockHandoffToHse = 0U;
    SystemCoreClockUpdate();
    HAL_InitTick(HAL_GetTickPrio());
  }

/******************************************************************************
                            BUS OPERATIONS
*******************************************************************************/
/**
  * @brief  SPI Write byte(s) to device
  * @param  DataIn: Pointer to data buffer to write
  * @param  DataOut: Pointer to data buffer for read data
  * @param  DataLength: number of bytes to write
  * @retval None
  */
static void SPIx_WriteReadData(const uint8_t *DataIn, uint8_t *DataOut, uint16_t DataLength)
{
  main_transfer_state = TRANSFER_WAIT;
  HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_DMA(&hspi2, (uint8_t*) DataIn, DataOut, DataLength);
  while (main_transfer_state == TRANSFER_WAIT);
}

/**
  * @brief  SPI Write a byte to device
  * @param  Value: value to be written
  * @retval None
  */
static uint8_t SPIx_WriteRead(uint8_t Value)
{
  *(__IO uint8_t *)&hspi2.Instance->DR = Value;
  while (!__HAL_SPI_GET_FLAG(&hspi2, SPI_FLAG_RXNE));
  return *(__IO uint8_t *)&hspi2.Instance->DR;
}

frame[3] = (uint8_t)(Arg >> 8);  /* Construct byte 4 */
  frame[4] = (uint8_t)(Arg);       /* Construct byte 5 */
  frame[5] = (Crc | 0x01);         /* Construct byte 6 */

  /* Send the command */
  SD_IO_CSState(0);
  SD_IO_WriteReadData(frame, frameout, SD_CMD_LENGTH); /* Send the Cmd bytes */

  switch(Answer)
  {
  case SD_ANSWER_R1_EXPECTED :
    retr.r1 = SD_ReadData();
    break;
  case SD_ANSWER_R1B_EXPECTED :
    retr.r1 = SD_ReadData();
    retr.r2 = SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);
    /* Set CS High */
    SD_IO_CSState(1);
    HAL_Delay(1);
    /* Set CS Low */
    SD_IO_CSState(0);

    /* Wait IO line return 0xFF */
    while (SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE) != 0xFF);
    break;
  case SD_ANSWER_R2_EXPECTED :
    retr.r1 = SD_ReadData();
    retr.r2 = SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);
    break;
  case SD_ANSWER_R3_EXPECTED :
  case SD_ANSWER_R7_EXPECTED :
    retr.r1 = SD_ReadData();
    retr.r2 = SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);
    retr.r3 = SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);
    retr.r4 = SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);
    retr.r5 = SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);
    break;
  default :
    break;
  }
  return retr;
}

/**
  * @brief  Stops an active multi-block read transaction.
  * @param  Timeout: Timeout count while waiting for the card to become ready.
  * @retval SD status
  */
static uint8_t SD_StopTransmission(uint32_t Timeout)
{
  uint8_t frame[SD_CMD_LENGTH], frameout[SD_CMD_LENGTH];
  uint8_t response;

  frame[0] = (SD_CMD_STOP_TRANSMISSION | 0x40);
  frame[1] = 0x00;
  frame[2] = 0x00;
  frame[3] = 0x00;
  frame[4] = 0x00;
  frame[5] = 0xFF;

  SD_IO_CSState(0);
  SD_IO_WriteReadData(frame, frameout, SD_CMD_LENGTH);

  /* CMD12 returns one stuff byte before the R1 response in SPI mode. */
  SD_IO_WriteByte(SD_DUMMY_BYTE);

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reads over SWD, from a firmware stopped in Error_Handler, what tells why the mount failed.

usage: postmortem.py <elf> [output file]
"""
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys

ELF = sys.argv[1]
OUT = open(sys.argv[2], 'w') if len(sys.argv) > 2 else None


def say(text):
    print(text)
    if OUT:
        OUT.write(text + '\n')


def symbols():
    out = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    table = {}
    for line in out.splitlines():
        parts = line.split()
        if len(parts) == 4:
            table.setdefault(parts[3], (int(parts[0], 16), int(parts[1], 16)))
    return table


SYM = symbols()
READS = []   # (label, address, word count)


def want(label, addr, words):
    READS.append((label, addr, words))


for name in ('Stat', 'resource_counts', 'fs', 'flag_SDHC', 'SdStatus', 'hspi2', 'main_transfer_state',
             'SystemCoreClock', 'uwTick', 'state', 'rx_read_index', 'rx_write_index', 'tx_read_index',
             'tx_write_index', 'mode_state', 'sd_diag_stage', 'fs_diag'):
    if name in SYM:
        addr, size = SYM[name]
        want(name, addr & ~3, (size + (addr & 3) + 3) // 4)
want('SPI2 CR1 CR2 SR', 0x40003800, 3)
want('RCC CR', 0x58000000, 1)
want('RCC CFGR', 0x58000008, 1)
want('GPIOH MODER', 0x48001C00, 1)
want('GPIOH ODR', 0x48001C14, 1)
want('GPIOD MODER', 0x48000C00, 1)
want('GPIOD IDR ODR', 0x48000C10, 2)
want('GPIOB MODER', 0x48000400, 1)
want('GPIOB IDR', 0x48000410, 1)

cmd = ['openocd', '-f', 'interface/stlink.cfg', '-c', 'transport select hla_swd', '-f', 'target/stm32wbx.cfg',
       '-c', 'stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}', '-c', 'init', '-c', 'halt',
       '-c', 'echo [format PC=%s [reg pc]]', '-c', 'echo [format SP=%s [reg sp]]', '-c', 'echo [format LR=%s [reg lr]]']
for i, (label, addr, words) in enumerate(READS):
    cmd += ['-c', 'echo "@@%d"' % i, '-c', 'mdw 0x%08x %d' % (addr, words)]
cmd += ['-c', 'echo "@@stack"', '-c', 'mdw [expr {[lindex [reg sp] 2] - 0x300}] 0x140', '-c', 'exit']
out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
text = out.stdout + out.stderr

regs = dict(re.findall(r'(PC|SP|LR)=.*?(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)', text))
blocks = {}

seen = 0

~~~~bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: lock_hunt.sh <elf> <attempt name>...
# Replays the perturbed session until the firmware ends in Error_Handler, then reads the post-mortem.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli
ELF=$1; shift
where() {
  PC=$(timeout 20 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}" -c "init" -c "halt" -c "echo [format PC=%s [reg pc]]" -c "resume" -c "exit" 2>&1 | grep "^PC=" | grep -o "0x[0-9a-f]*" | tail -1)
  arm-none-eabi-addr2line -f -e $ELF $PC | head -1
}
for A in "$@"; do
  echo "--- attempt $A  $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  "$S/four/repro.sh" $A | grep -v "stale subscriber\|REPRO_DONE"
  W=$(where)
  echo "firmware is in: $W"
  if [ "$W" = "Error_Handler" ]; then
    echo "LOCKED on attempt $A"
    python3 $S/sd/postmortem.py $ELF $S/sd/postmortem_$A.txt
    break
  fi
  python3 $CLI/vbus.py reset --settle 6 > /dev/null 2>&1
  sleep 4
done
echo HUNT_DONE
EOF
chmod +x $S/sd/lock_hunt.sh; ELF=$S/four/master-patched/build/master-patched.elf; timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $ELF verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 8; cd $S/sd && setsid nohup ./lock_hunt.sh $ELF h1 h2 h3 h4 h5 h6 h7 h8 h9 h10 h11 h12 > $S/sd/hunt_patched.log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown; date +%H:%M:%S
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Search the frozen RAM for the stray pattern and for other copies of the boot sector

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; E=$S/four/master-patched/build/master-patched.elf; python3 - "$E" <<'PY'
import re,subprocess,sys
ram=open('[scratchpad]/sd/h2_ram.bin','rb').read()
syms=[]
for l in subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm','-S','-n',sys.argv[1]],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines():
    p=l.split()
    if len(p)==4 and p[0].startswith('200'): syms.append((int(p[0],16),int(p[1],16),p[3]))
def sym(a):
    for s,z,n in syms:
        if s<=a<s+z: return '%s+%d'%(n,a-s)
    return '?'
for m in re.finditer(rb'(?:\x55\xaa){4,}', ram):
    print('55aa run: 0x%08x len %d  %s'%(0x20000000+m.start(), m.end()-m.start(), sym(0x20000000+m.start())))
for m in re.finditer(rb'y to', ram):
    print('"y to": 0x%08x %s'%(0x20000000+m.start(), sym(0x20000000+m.start())))
for m in re.finditer(rb'MSDOS5\.0|MSWIN4\.1|mkfs\.fat|NO NAME', ram):
    print('%r: 0x%08x %s'%(m.group(0),0x20000000+m.start(), sym(0x20000000+m.start())))
d=ram[0xe74:0xe74+0x200]
print('sd_dummy_buf: %d bytes ff of 512; first 40: %s'%(d.count(0xff), d[:40].hex()))
PY
~~~~

## Assistant, note while working (12:15)

Le post-mortem révèle que la carte a été mal identifiée comme SDSC au lieu de SDHC, avec un échec de passage en haute vitesse et des octets parasites dans le secteur de boot, ce qui suggère une coupure d'alimentation trop brève pour une réinitialisation propre. Je vais vérifier cette hypothèse avec une expérience firmware testant des coupures de 0 à 45 ms sur 6 passes (~5 min).

| Nothing | 7 of 10: two with `CONFIG.TXT` stalled for 20 s, one with a file 242 bytes short |
| In the app: 2, and the read request sent again (1) | 12 of 12, six of them after a second read request |
| Plus the firmware fix (1) | 11 of 12, no second request any more; one killed by 3 |
| Plus 3 | 24 of 25; one with a file 242 bytes short (4) |
| Plus 4, that is everything | 40 of 40: no second request, no packet sent again |
| Everything in the app, firmware without its fix | 20 of 20, eight of them after a second read request |

1. **Firmware, `FlySight/crs.c`.** A command that reaches the FlySight right behind the last
   acknowledgement of a file read is taken out of the queue while the firmware is still in its
   reading state, and dropped without an answer. BlueZ sends the acknowledgement and the next
   read request back to back, so the request for `CONFIG.TXT` was lost in 6 runs of 12.
   Fix: stop reading the queue once the file is fully acknowledged, and run the idle state for
   what is left. In the app, a read request that nothing answers within 2 s is now sent again,
   which is what makes it work with a firmware that does not have the fix.
2. **`KmpGatt.desktop.kt` / `DesktopKmpBleSocket.kt`.** One coroutine was launched per native
   callback on a parallel dispatcher, so two notifications received back to back could be
   handled in the wrong order. They now go through one single-file dispatcher.
......
| `master` + patch | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 30 s, then `00`, still advertising at 256 s |
| `develop`, unmodified | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 209 s, then no advertising (bug 2) |
| `develop` + patch | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 30 s, then `00`, still advertising at 255 s |

Linux connects on the two unmodified builds: bug 1 does not concern it. Bug 2 shows from Linux as
from the other hosts, and the patch removes it.

The row of `master` + patch is its second run. In the first series SkyGames was left open, idle,
next to the scripts, and two things came out of that:

- **The library left its notification sessions behind.** BlueZ keeps such a session for as long
  as the program that asked for it is on the bus, across disconnections, and emits each
  notification once per session: the idle application made every other program receive each
  notification twice. `ble_linux.c` now gives its sessions back when a link ends
  (`stop_notifications`). The three other builds went through that first series all the same.
- **The firmware can end in `Error_Handler()`.** On `master` + patch that first series stopped
  there: the FlySight no longer advertised and answered nothing. Read over SWD, the firmware was
  in the endless loop of `Error_Handler()`, called from `FatFS_Init()` (`f_mount()` failed,
  `resource_manager.c`), itself reached from `FS_CRS_State_Idle()` on a read request. Replayed on
  purpose with doubled notifications, it happened in 2 sessions out of 4 on `master` + patch and
  in 1 out of 4 on unmodified `master`, so the patch is not the cause; not in 2 sessions on the
  branch build. Only a reset brings the FlySight back. Why the mount fails then was not
  established, and nothing is changed for it here.

### The SkyGames application itself

SkyGames did not build on this PC, for two reasons that have nothing to do with BLE, both dealt
with in the SkyGames repository:

- eSpeak-ng keeps paths in a buffer of 160 characters, and the build tree under a long home
  directory overflowed it (`Bad vowel file`). The buffer is now 1024 (`AudioModule`).
- The Firebase C++ SDK ships static libraries for Linux that are not position independent, so
  `libskygames_firebase.so` could not be linked. On Linux the same functions are now built into
  a program the JVM talks to (`skygames_firebase_helper`

#!/bin/bash
# usage: ui_build.sh <variant>   In the SkyGames window: connect with the FlySight idle, then in pairing mode.
V=$1; S=[scratchpad]; export DISPLAY=:99 XAUTHORITY=$S/gui/xauth
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli; L=$S/four/logs/$V; mkdir -p $L
state() { python3 $S/gui/uistate.py "$@"; }
wait_state() { for i in $(seq 1 $2); do [ "$(state)" = "$1" ] && return 0; sleep 1; done; return 1; }
ensure_card() { [ "$(state)" = "home" ] && { $S/gui/ui.sh click 416 366; sleep 2; }; true; }
connect_check() {   # $1 = name of the screenshot, $2 = label
  N=$(wc -l < $S/skygames-run.log)
  [ "$(state)" = "disconnected" ] && $S/gui/ui.sh click 640 450
  if wait_state connected 25; then
    for i in $(seq 1 25); do sed -n "$((N+1)),\$p" $S/skygames-run.log | grep -q "readConfigFile: final _configFile=" && break; sleep 1; done
    sleep 1; state $L/ui_$1.png >/dev/null
    echo "SkyGames, $2 : connected; $(sed -n "$((N+1)),\$p" $S/skygames-run.log | grep -o 'readConfigFile: final _configFile=[A-Za-z]*' | tail -1 | sed 's/readConfigFile: final _configFile=/configuration /'); second requests=$(sed -n "$((N+1)),\$p" $S/skygames-run.log | grep -c 'sending it again')"
  else
    state $L/ui_$1.png >/dev/null; echo "SkyGames, $2 : NOT CONNECTED after 25 s (state=$(state))"
  fi
}
disconnect() { [ "$(state)" = "connected" ] && $S/gui/ui.sh click 1190 87; wait_state disconnected 10 || echo "  (still $(state) after Disconnect)"; }
ensure_card
[ "$(state)" = "connected" ] && disconnect
sleep 2
connect_check idle "idle   "
disconnect; sleep 3
python3 $CLI/vbus.py button >/dev/null; sleep 1.5
connect_check pairing "pairing"
disconnect

#!/bin/bash
# Drive the nested display :99. usage: ui.sh click X Y | type TEXT | key KEY | shot NAME [scale]
export DISPLAY=:99 XAUTHORITY=[scratchpad]/gui/xauth
case "$1" in
  click) xdotool mousemove "$2" "$3" click 1 ;;
  type)  xdotool type --delay 30 "$2" ;;
  key)   xdotool key "$2" ;;
  scroll) xdotool mousemove "$2" "$3" click --repeat "${5:-3}" "$4" ;;
  shot)  python3 [scratchpad]/gui/shot.py [scratchpad]/gui/"$2".png ${3:-} | tail -1 ;;
esac

if r > 200 and 140 < g < 215 and b < 70:

print("card" if (r, g, b) != (255, 255, 255) and abs(r - 242) < 6 else "home")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rewrites the passage of debug_ble/linux/README.md about the Error_Handler lockup.
usage: edit_readme.py <replays without lockup> <replays run>"""
import os
import sys

ok, total = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
path = os.path.expanduser('~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux/README.md')
s = open(path).read()

start = s.index('- **The firmware can end in `Error_Handler()`.**')
end = s.index('### The SkyGames application itself')
new = '''- **The firmware could end in `Error_Handler()`.** On `master` + patch that first series stopped
  there: the FlySight no longer advertised and answered nothing, until a reset. The patch is not
  the cause; the cause and its fix are in the next section.

### The lockup: a microSD card powered again about 1 ms after losing power

Read over SWD, the firmware was in the endless loop of `Error_Handler()`, called from
`FatFS_Init()` (`resource_manager.c`) because `f_mount()` had failed, itself reached from
`FS_CRS_State_Idle()` on a read request. Replayed on purpose with doubled notifications
(`stale_subscriber.py`), it happened in 2 sessions out of 4 on `master` + patch and in 1 out of 4
on unmodified `master`.

The firmware cuts the power of the card (`VCC_EN`) when a file transfer ends, and turns it on
again for the next command. What the frozen firmware held when it locked up again
(`postmortem.py`): the card had answered its initialisation, but had been taken for a
standard-capacity card when it is a high-capacity one, had refused the switch to high speed, and
the sector read as sector 0 was the boot sector of the partition with 32 foreign bytes at its
start. FatFs found no partition in that and returned `FR_NO_FILESYSTEM`.

The same state can be produced at will, without BLE. `sd-power-gap-experiment.patch` (for
`master`) makes the firmware, at start-up, mount the card, cut its power for a chosen time and
mount it again, six times for each of twenty durations; `sd_power_gap.py` reads the result:

| Time without power | Second mount |
|--------------------|--------------|
| 0 to 0.7 ms | 6 of 6 OK, for each of the 8 durations |
| 1.0 ms | 2 of 6 fail |
| 1.3 ms | 6 of 6 fail |
| 1.6 to 45 ms | 6 of 6 OK, for each of the 10 durations |

Each failure is the one above: `FR_NO_FILESYSTEM`, wrong card type, no high speed. My reading:
under 1 ms the rail has not dropped enough for the card to notice, from 1.6 ms the card restarts
from scratch, and in between it does neither. A firmware that records each of its mounts showed
how a session gets there: the read request that follows a transfer found the card 0.5 to 2 ms
after its power was cut (43 ms when it came one connection event later). Gaps from 76 ms to 36 s,
measured the same way, all mounted.

Fix, in `VCC_DeInit()` (`resource_manager.c`): once `VCC_EN` is low, wait 50 ms before returning,
so that nothing turns the rail on again before it has discharged. With it:

- the same experiment gives 60 mounts OK out of 60, the 1.0 and 1.3 ms ones included;
- `master` + patch + this fix went through %s replayed sessions out of %s without locking up; without
  it, it had just locked up at the second one.

The 50 ms are a margin chosen from these measurements, 30 times the longest gap that failed on
this board with this card; the rail was not looked at with an oscilloscope. A card that cannot be
mounted still ends in `Error_Handler()`: that is how the firmware treats it everywhere, and it is
left as it is. The fix is in the working tree of the branch, not committed.

''' % (ok, total)
s = s[:start] + new + s[end:]

old = '''`stale_subscriber.py` leaves notification sessions behind in BlueZ, which doubles every

**Tool: Bash** — Replace the report's paragraph on the lockup with the established cause, measurements and fix

~~~~bash
cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble && python3 - <<'PY'
p='ble-pairing-fixes-report.html'; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('  <li><code>FlySight/resource_manager.c</code>, <code>FatFS_Init()</code>: when <code>f_mount()</code> fails')
b=s.index('</li>',a)+len('</li>')
new='''  <li><code>FlySight/resource_manager.c</code>: the firmware cuts the power of the microSD card when a file transfer ends, and turns it on again for the next command. When that command comes about 1 ms later, the card does not restart cleanly, <code>f_mount()</code> fails, and <code>FatFS_Init()</code> calls <code>Error_Handler()</code>, which never returns: the FlySight stops advertising and answers nothing until it is reset. It was reached from <code>FS_CRS_State_Idle()</code> on a read request, in sessions where a misbehaving client received every notification twice and answered in bursts: 1 such session out of 4 on unmodified <code>master</code>, 2 out of 4 on <code>master</code> + patch. Read over SWD in the frozen firmware: the card had answered its initialisation but had been taken for a standard-capacity card when it is a high-capacity one, had refused the switch to high speed, and the sector read as sector 0 was not sector 0, so FatFs found no file system. An experiment in the firmware alone (mount the card, cut its power for a chosen time, mount it again, six times per duration) gives exactly that failure 6 times out of 6 at 1.3 ms and 2 times out of 6 at 1.0 ms, and never from 0 to 0.7 ms nor from 1.6 to 45 ms. Keeping <code>VCC_EN</code> low for 50 ms before <code>VCC_DeInit()</code> returns removes it: 60 mounts out of 60 in the same experiment, and 12 such sessions out of 12 on <code>master</code> + patch, which had locked up at the second one just before. The 50 ms are a margin over what was measured on this board with this card; the rail was not looked at with an oscilloscope. The change is in the working tree of the branch, not committed. Measurements and scripts are in <code>linux/README.md</code>.</li>'''
s=s[:a]+new+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('bullet replaced:', 'VCC_DeInit' in s)
PY
~~~~

### The four builds of the report

`master` `9ec7186` and `develop` `e67ee9f` as published upstream, and each with the three fixes
of the report and nothing else, apart from `CFG_DEBUGGER_SUPPORTED` set to 1 for the bench. The
PC was bonded with the board beforehand. For each build: the native library and the Kotlin
layers connect with the FlySight idle and in pairing mode, SkyGames does the same from its
window, then a pairing window is left to expire (double press, scanner for 262 s).

| Firmware | Library, idle and pairing mode | Kotlin layers, idle and pairing mode | SkyGames, idle and pairing mode | Pairing window left to expire |
|----------|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| `master`, unmodified | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 33 s, then `00`, still advertising at 255 s |
| `master` + patch | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 30 s, then `00`, still advertising at 255 s |
| `develop`, unmodified | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 209 s, then no advertising (bug 2) |
| `develop` + patch | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 30 s, then `00`, still advertising at 254 s |
| branch, with the two firmware fixes of this page | connects, encrypted read OK | connects, both files read | connected, configuration loaded | `01` for 34 s, then `00`, still advertising at 255 s |

Linux connects on the two unmodified builds: bug 1 does not concern it. Bug 2 shows from Linux as
from the other hosts, and the patch removes it.

This table is one pass: the five builds one after the other, each flashed once, nothing run
again. The durations are those of the scanner, which sees a change of the pairing flag a few
seconds late at times. An earlier pass had not gone that way: SkyGames had been left open, idle,
next to the scripts, and two things came out of it:

- **The library left its notification sessions behind.** BlueZ keeps such a session for as long
  as the program that asked for it is on the bus, across disconnections, and emits each
  notification once per session: the idle application made every other program receive each
  notification twice. `ble_linux.c` now gives its sessions back when a link ends
  (`stop_notifications`). The three other builds went through that first series all the same.
- **The firmware could end in `Error_Handler()`.** On `master` + patch that first series stopped
  there: the FlySight no longer advertised and answered nothing, until a reset. The patch is not
  the cause; the cause and its fix are in the next section.
~~~~

On the Linux PC (Ubuntu 24.04, BlueZ 5.72), set up on 2026-10-08:

- **Bench FlySight**: on battery, ST-Link V3 attached. `Scripts/cli/vbus.py` and `ble_trace.py` work through OpenOCD (no STM32CubeProgrammer here). A udev rule gives the user access to the ST-Link; no sudo is available to me, the user runs sudo commands when asked.
- **Firmware builds**: no CubeIDE project build here; a Makefile in the session scratchpad compiled an exported tree with `arm-none-eabi-gcc` 13.2 (include paths taken from `.cproject`), flashed with `openocd ... -c "program x.elf verify reset exit"`. `ble_trace.py` needs the ELF that is running (`FLYSIGHT_ELF`).
- **Test scripts and results**: `debug_ble/linux/` in the firmware repo (BlueZ probe, probe for SkyGames' native library, headless JVM probe for FlySightApi, README with every result).
- **SkyGames UI tests without touching the user's pointer**: start `Xephyr :99` with an xauth file, run `./gradlew :composeApp:run` with `DISPLAY=:99 SKIKO_RENDER_API=SOFTWARE`, drive it with `xdotool`, screenshot with PIL `ImageGrab.grab(xdisplay=":99")`, resize the app window with `xdotool windowsize` (there is no window manager). The Google sign-in opens in the user's Chrome on the real display; the user completes it, and the session then persists in the keyring.
- SkyGames checkout: `~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames`, branch `release/1.1.0`; `local.properties` (git-ignored) holds `sdk.dir` and the user's Google keys.
- Gotcha: `pkill -f PATTERN` kills the calling shell when PATTERN also appears literally elsewhere in the same command line; use a bracket (`[X]ephyr`) and keep the plain text out of the command.

Related: [[link-files-and-show-commands]], [[no-ai-signature-in-commits]].

~~~~bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: reset_powered.sh <elf> <count>
# Resets the firmware while the microSD card is powered and mounted (stopped on a breakpoint at
# FatFS_DeInit during start-up), and says where the firmware is 2.5 s after that reset.

done
EOF
~~~~

Result:

~~~~
### The lockup: a microSD card powered again about 1 ms after losing power

Read over SWD, the firmware was in the endless loop of `Error_Handler()`, called from
`FatFS_Init()` (`resource_manager.c`) because `f_mount()` had failed, itself reached from
`FS_CRS_State_Idle()` on a read request. Replayed on purpose with doubled notifications
(`stale_subscriber.py`), it happened in 2 sessions out of 4 on `master` + patch and in 1 out of 4
on unmodified `master`.

The firmware cuts the power of the card (`VCC_EN`) when a file transfer ends, and turns it on
again for the next command. What the frozen firmware held when it locked up again
(`postmortem.py`): the card had answered its initialisation, but had been taken for a
standard-capacity card when it is a high-capacity one, had refused the switch to high speed, and
the sector read as sector 0 was the boot sector of the partition with 32 foreign bytes at its
start. FatFs found no partition in that and returned `FR_NO_FILESYSTEM`.

The same state can be produced at will, without BLE. `sd-power-gap-experiment.patch` (for
`master`) makes the firmware, at start-up, mount the card, cut its power for a chosen time and
mount it again, six times for each of twenty durations; `sd_power_gap.py` reads the result:

| Time without power | Second mount |
|--------------------|--------------|
| 0 to 0.7 ms | 6 of 6 OK, for each of the 8 durations |
| 1.0 ms | 2 of 6 fail |
| 1.3 ms | 6 of 6 fail |
| 1.6 to 45 ms | 6 of 6 OK, for each of the 10 durations |

Each failure is the one above: `FR_NO_FILESYSTEM`, wrong card type, no high speed. My reading:
under 1 ms the rail has not dropped enough for the card to notice, from 1.6 ms the card restarts
from scratch, and in between it does neither. A firmware that records each of its mounts showed
how a session gets there: the read request that follows a transfer found the card 0.5 to 2 ms
after its power was cut (43 ms when it came one connection event later). Gaps from 76 ms to 36 s,
measured the same way, all mounted.

Fix, in `VCC_DeInit()` (`resource_manager.c`): once `VCC_EN` is low, wait 50 ms before returning,
so that nothing turns the rail on again before it has discharged. With it:

- the same experiment gives 60 mounts OK out of 60, the 1.0 and 1.3 ms ones included;
- `master` + patch + this fix went through 12 replayed sessions out of 12 without locking up; without
  it, it had just locked up at the second one;
- the branch build with this fix and the one of `crs.c`: 8 replayed sessions out of 8.

A reset is the other way to cut the power of a card for a short time, and the fix does nothing
there: the firmware turns the rail on again about 1 ms after it starts. Tried twelve times, with
the firmware reset over SWD while the card was powered and mounted: the mount at start-up worked
twelve times.

The 50 ms are a margin chosen from these measurements, 30 times the longest gap that failed on
this board with this card; the rail was not looked at with an oscilloscope. A card that cannot be
mounted still ends in `Error_Handler()`: that is how the firmware treats it everywhere, and it is
left as it is. The fix is in the working tree of the branch, not committed.

### The SkyGames application itself
~~~~

## Assistant (13:25)

Les deux réserves sont levées : le blocage `Error_Handler` est expliqué et corrigé, et les quatre firmwares du rapport passent en un seul passage, sans reprise. Rien n'est commité.

## Le blocage du firmware

**Cause.** Le firmware coupe l'alimentation de la carte microSD à la fin de chaque transfert et la rallume à la commande suivante. Si cette commande arrive environ 1 ms plus tard, la carte ne redémarre pas proprement, `f_mount()` échoue et `FatFS_Init()` appelle `Error_Handler()`, qui ne rend jamais la main.

**Mesure.** Une expérience dans le firmware seul, sans BLE (monter, couper un temps choisi, remonter, 6 fois par durée) :

| Coupure | Remontage |
|---|---|
| 0 à 0,7 ms | 6/6 OK |
| 1,0 ms | 2 échecs sur 6 |
| 1,3 ms | 6 échecs sur 6 |
| 1,6 à 45 ms | 6/6 OK |

Chaque échec a la signature relevée par SWD dans le firmware figé lors d'un vrai blocage : `FR_NO_FILESYSTEM`, carte SDHC prise pour une SDSC, haute vitesse refusée.

**Correctif.** Dans [FlySight/resource_manager.c](FlySight/resource_manager.c), `VCC_DeInit()` attend 50 ms une fois le rail coupé (8 lignes). Avec lui :

- la même expérience donne 60 remontages réussis sur 60 ;
- `master` + patch + correctif tient 12 sessions perturbées sur 12, alors qu'il venait de bloquer à la 2ᵉ sans lui ;
- le firmware de la branche tient 8 sessions perturbées sur 8.

Les 50 ms sont une marge empirique (30 fois la plus longue coupure fautive sur cette carte) : je n'ai pas regardé le rail à l'oscilloscope. Le correctif ne couvre pas un reset avec la carte alimentée ; mesuré à part, le montage au démarrage réussit 12 fois sur 12.

~~~~bash
#!/bin/bash
# usage: normal_gaps.sh <elf> <sessions>   Normal sessions (nothing else on the bus), then the mounts the firmware recorded.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli; LNX=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux
P=$LNX/jvm-probe/build/install/fs-jvm-probe/bin/fs-jvm-probe; ID=58:6B:2A:E4:31:C1
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Flash the bench firmware back, then reset it eight times with the SD card off and check each time, by a hash read over SWD, whether its BLE keys survived (about 1.5 min)

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cat > $S/sd/reset_keys.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resets the firmware and says whether its BLE root keys survived.

usage: reset_keys.py <elf> <count> powered|idle
  powered: the reset comes while the microSD card is powered and mounted (breakpoint at
           FatFS_DeInit during start-up); idle: the reset comes with the card off.
The keys are never printed, only the first characters of their SHA-1.
"""
import hashlib, re, struct, subprocess, sys

ELF, COUNT, MODE = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
nm = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
def sym(name, size=None):
    for l in nm.splitlines():
        p = l.split()
        if len(p) == 4 and p[3] == name and (size is None or int(p[1], 16) == size):
            return int(p[0], 16)
STATE = sym('state', 0x70); DEINIT = sym('FatFS_DeInit')
BASE = ['openocd', '-f', 'interface/stlink.cfg', '-c', 'transport select hla_swd', '-f', 'target/stm32wbx.cfg',
        '-c', 'stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}', '-c', 'init']
READ = ['-c', 'halt', '-c', 'echo [format PC=%s [reg pc]]', '-c', 'mdw 0x%08x 28' % STATE, '-c', 'resume', '-c', 'exit']

def run(cmds):
    out = subprocess.run(BASE + cmds, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=90)
    text = out.stdout + out.stderr
    words = []
    for line in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r'^0x[0-9a-f]+: (.*)$', line.strip())
        if m:
            words += [int(w, 16) for w in m.group(1).split()]
    raw = struct.pack('<%dI' % len(words), *words)
    pc = re.findall(r'PC=.*?(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)', text)
    where = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-addr2line', '-f', '-e', ELF, pc[-1]], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.splitlines()[0] if pc else '?'
    keys = hashlib.sha1(raw[77:109]).hexdigest()[:8] if len(raw) >= 112 else '????????'
    temp = struct.unpack_from('<I', raw, 40)[0] if len(raw) >= 112 else -1
    return keys, temp, where

keys, temp, where = run(READ)
print('before: keys %s  Temp_Folder %d  firmware in %s' % (keys, temp, where), flush=True)
changed = 0
for n in range(1, COUNT + 1):
    if MODE == 'powered':
        k, t, w = run(['-c', 'reset halt', '-c', 'bp 0x%x 2 hw' % DEINIT, '-c', 'resume', '-c', 'wait_halt 8000',
                       '-c', 'rbp 0x%x' % DEINIT, '-c', 'reset run', '-c', 'sleep 2500'] + READ)
    else:
        k, t, w = run(['-c', 'reset run', '-c', 'sleep 2500'] + READ)
    note = 'KEYS CHANGED' if k != keys else 'keys kept'
    changed += k != keys
    print('reset %2d (%s): %s (%s)  Temp_Folder %d  firmware in %s' % (n, MODE, note, k, t, w), flush=True)
    keys = k
print('%d of %d resets changed the keys' % (changed, COUNT))
EOF
E=$S/fw/build/flysight.elf; timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $E verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 6; python3 $S/sd/reset_keys.py $E 8 idle 2>&1 | tail -11
~~~~

## Assistant (17:54)

Sur le fond, tu as raison : je n'ai jamais vu ce blocage dans une session normale, seulement avec un client qui recevait chaque notification en double. Mais il n'est pas hors de portée d'un utilisateur, et j'ai un incident à te signaler sur le FlySight du banc.

## Le blocage en usage réel

Ce n'est pas l'humain qui fait le timing, c'est l'application : SkyGames lit deux fichiers coup sur coup à chaque connexion. J'ai mesuré, avec un firmware qui enregistre chaque montage, combien de temps après la coupure de la carte arrive la seconde demande :

| Sessions | Écart mesuré | Blocage |
|---|---|---|
| 16 normales (8 `master`, 8 `develop`) | moins de 1 ms dans 13, environ 2 s dans 3 | aucun |
| Avec notifications doublées | 0,5 à 2 ms | oui, par moments |

La fenêtre fautive commence à 1,0 ms. Une session normale reste donc en dessous, mais de moins d'une milliseconde. La mesure ne vaut que pour Linux : je n'ai pas mesuré cet écart depuis macOS, Android ou iOS.

Le premier blocage est d'ailleurs arrivé dans une situation banale : SkyGames laissé ouvert et inactif à côté d'un autre programme. La bibliothèque Linux ne laisse plus traîner ses sessions de notification, donc ce cas précis n'existe plus.

Je garderais quand même le correctif de 8 lignes : c'est rare, mais quand ça arrive le FlySight est mort jusqu'au reset.

## Incident sur le FlySight du banc

Vers 15:24, juste après mon essai « 12 resets avec la carte alimentée », le PC n'a plus reconnu le FlySight et a dû s'appairer de nouveau avec lui.

- **Ce qui est sûr** : BlueZ a maintenant deux entrées pour ce FlySight, l'ancienne étant morte. Le firmware liste toujours ses 4 appareils appairés. Les fichiers de la carte sont intacts. Huit resets carte éteinte conservent les clés.
- **Mon interprétation, non prouvée** : à l'un de ces resets, le firmware n'a pas pu relire `flysight.txt` et a tiré de nouvelles clés BLE, comme le code le prévoit dans ce cas.
- **Conséquences probables pour toi** : le Mac, le téléphone Android et l'iPad devront sans doute oublier ce FlySight et le réappairer. Dans SkyGames sur Linux, la carte du FlySight enregistrée pointe vers l'ancien identifiant : il faudra le supprimer et le rajouter.

J'avais écrit que ce test de reset passait 12 fois sur 12 : c'est vrai pour le démarrage, mais pas pour les clés. C'est corrigé dans [debug_ble/linux/README.md](debug_ble/linux/README.md), avec la mesure des sessions normales.

Je n'ai pas reproduit l'incident : le refaire change encore les clés du FlySight. Si tu veux que j'établisse la cause, dis-le-moi ; ça coûte un réappairage de plus côté PC, et si mon interprétation est juste c'est un vrai défaut du firmware, atteignable par un simple reset au mauvais moment.

Le banc est revenu sur le firmware de la branche avec les correctifs, et il répond sous son nouvel identifiant. Rien n'est commité.

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/sd/reset_proof.py`

~~~~
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resets the firmware and watches, with hardware breakpoints, how it reads /flysight.txt at start-up.

usage: reset_proof.py <elf> <count> powered|idle [dump directory]
  powered: the reset comes while the microSD card is powered and mounted (firmware stopped at
           FatFS_DeInit during start-up); idle: the reset comes with the card off.
For each reset: the result of f_open() in FS_State_Read(), the card type and SPI speed at that
moment, whether keys were found in the file, and whether the keys in RAM changed afterwards.
The keys themselves are never printed, only the first characters of their SHA-1.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ELF, COUNT, MODE = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3]
DUMPS = sys.argv[4] if len(sys.argv) > 4 else None
FR = {0: 'FR_OK', 1: 'FR_DISK_ERR', 2: 'FR_INT_ERR', 3: 'FR_NOT_READY', 4: 'FR_NO_FILE', 5: 'FR_NO_PATH',
      6: 'FR_INVALID_NAME', 7: 'FR_DENIED', 9: 'FR_INVALID_OBJECT', 12: 'FR_NOT_ENABLED', 13: 'FR_NO_FILESYSTEM'}

nm = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def sym(name, size=None):
    for line in nm.splitlines():
        p = line.split()
        if len(p) == 4 and p[3] == name and (size is None or int(p[1], 16) == size):
            return int(p[0], 16)
        if len(p) == 3 and p[2] == name and size is None:
            return int(p[0], 16)
    raise SystemExit('no symbol ' + name)


def after_call(function, callee, nth=1):
    """Address of the instruction that follows the nth call to callee in function."""
    dis = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-objdump', '-d', '--no-show-raw-insn', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    inside, seen, take = False, 0, False
    for line in dis.splitlines():
        if re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <%s>:' % re.escape(function), line):
            inside = True
            continue
        if inside and re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <', line):
            break
        m = re.match(r'^\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s+(\S+)\s*(.*)$', line)
        if not inside or not m:
            continue
        if take:
            return int(m.group(1), 16)
        if m.group(2) == 'bl' and '<%s>' % callee in m.group(3):
            seen += 1
            take = seen == nth
    raise SystemExit('no call to %s in %s' % (callee, function))


STATE = sym('state', 0x70)
FS = sym('fs', 0x234)
FLAG = sym('flag_SDHC')
STAT = sym('Stat')
TICK = sym('uwTick')
DEINIT = sym('FatFS_DeInit')
ERROR = sym('Error_Handler') & ~1
OPENED = after_call('FS_State_Read', 'f_open')            # r0 = result of f_open
[... 97 lines omitted ...]
        n, MODE, FR.get(r0, r0), tick[0] if tick else '?', flag[0] if flag else '?', divider)
    if h2 is not None and (h2 & ~1) == PARSED:
        line += '; file read, keys in it: %s' % ('NONE' if parsed_zero else 'yes')
    elif r0:
        line += '; file not read'
    note = 'KEYS CHANGED' if final_hash != previous else 'keys kept'
    changed += final_hash != previous
    failed += bool(r0)
    line += '; afterwards %s (%s), firmware in %s' % (note, final_hash, where(end))
    print(line, flush=True)
    if DUMPS and (r0 or final_hash != previous) and fs:
        os.makedirs(DUMPS, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(DUMPS, 'fs_reset_%s_%d.bin' % (MODE, n)), 'wb').write(struct.pack('<%dI' % len(fs), *fs))
    previous = final_hash
print('%d of %d resets: the state file could not be read; %d of %d: keys changed' % (failed, COUNT, changed, COUNT))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resets the firmware while its microSD card is powered, lets it start without stopping it, and
catches it only if it fails to open /flysight.txt or is about to draw new BLE keys.

usage: reset_free.py <elf> <count> powered|idle <dump directory>
Keys are never printed, only the first characters of their SHA-1. The dumps hold raw memory.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ELF, COUNT, MODE, DUMPS = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
os.makedirs(DUMPS, exist_ok=True)
FR = {0: 'FR_OK', 1: 'FR_DISK_ERR', 2: 'FR_INT_ERR', 3: 'FR_NOT_READY', 4: 'FR_NO_FILE', 5: 'FR_NO_PATH',
      6: 'FR_INVALID_NAME', 7: 'FR_DENIED', 9: 'FR_INVALID_OBJECT', 13: 'FR_NO_FILESYSTEM'}
nm = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
dis = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-objdump', '-d', '--no-show-raw-insn', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def sym(name, size=None):
    for line in nm.splitlines():
        p = line.split()
        if len(p) == 4 and p[3] == name and (size is None or int(p[1], 16) == size):
            return int(p[0], 16)
    raise SystemExit('no symbol ' + name)


def calls(function, callee):
    """Addresses of the calls to callee in function."""
    inside, found = False, []
    for line in dis.splitlines():
        if re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <%s>:' % re.escape(function), line):
            inside = True
            continue
        if inside and re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <', line):
            break
        m = re.match(r'^\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s+bl\s+[0-9a-f]+ <%s>' % re.escape(callee), line)
        if inside and m:
            found.append(int(m.group(1), 16))
    return found


STATE, FS, FILE = sym('state', 0x70), sym('fs', 0x234), sym('stateFile', 0x230)
FLAG, TICK = sym('flag_SDHC'), sym('uwTick')
DEINIT, ERROR = sym('FatFS_DeInit'), sym('Error_Handler') & ~1
NO_OPEN = calls('FS_State_Read', 'FS_State_Complete')[0]       # reached only when f_open failed; r3 = its result
NEW_IRK = calls('FS_State_Complete', 'FS_Common_GetRandomBytes')[0]   # reached only when no IRK was read
NAMES = {NO_OPEN: 'f_open of /flysight.txt FAILED', NEW_IRK: 'no key read from the file: drawing a NEW IRK', ERROR: 'Error_Handler'}


def capture(tag):
    return ['echo [format "%sPC=%%s" [reg pc]]' % tag, 'echo [format "%sR3=%%s" [reg r3]]' % tag,
            'echo "@@%sflag"' % tag, 'echo [mdb 0x%x 2]' % FLAG, 'echo "@@%sspi"' % tag, 'echo [mdw 0x40003800 1]',
            'echo "@@%stick"' % tag, 'echo [mdw 0x%x 1]' % TICK, 'echo "@@%sfile"' % tag, 'echo [mdw 0x%x 140]' % FILE,
            'echo "@@%sfs"' % tag, 'echo [mdw 0x%x 141]' % FS, 'echo "@@%sstate"' % tag, 'echo [mdw 0x%x 28]' % STATE,
            'echo "@@%sstack"' % tag, 'echo [mdw [lindex [reg sp] 2] 64]', 'echo "@@end"']


def openocd(tcl):
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile('w', suffix='.tcl', delete=False) as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(tcl) + '\n')

**Tool: Bash** — Replay eight times the exact three back-to-back measurements made just before the incident, and check after each whether the firmware's keys changed (about 1.5 min)

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cat > $S/sd/replay_triple.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Replays the three back-to-back measurements made at 15:23 (reset, stop at VCC_Init, read the
tick, let go, and at once the same again), then says whether the BLE keys of the firmware changed.
usage: replay_triple.py <elf> <count>"""
import hashlib, re, struct, subprocess, sys, time
ELF, COUNT = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
nm = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
def sym(name, size=None):
    for l in nm.splitlines():
        p = l.split()
        if len(p) == 4 and p[3] == name and (size is None or int(p[1], 16) == size):
            return int(p[0], 16)
STATE, VCC, TICK = sym('state', 0x70), sym('VCC_Init'), sym('uwTick')
BASE = ['openocd', '-f', 'interface/stlink.cfg', '-c', 'transport select hla_swd', '-f', 'target/stm32wbx.cfg',
        '-c', 'stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}', '-c', 'init']
def keys():
    out = subprocess.run(BASE + ['-c', 'halt', '-c', 'sleep 200', '-c', 'mdw 0x%x 28' % STATE, '-c', 'sleep 100',
                                 '-c', 'mdw 0x%x 28' % STATE, '-c', 'resume', '-c', 'exit'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    words = []
    for line in (out.stdout + out.stderr).splitlines():
        m = re.match(r'^0x[0-9a-f]+: (.*)$', line.strip())
        if m:
            words += [int(w, 16) for w in m.group(1).split()]
    if len(words) != 56 or words[:28] != words[28:]:
        return None, None
    raw = struct.pack('<28I', *words[:28])
    return hashlib.sha1(raw[77:109]).hexdigest()[:8], struct.unpack_from('<I', raw, 40)[0]
previous, _ = keys()
print('before: keys %s' % previous, flush=True)
changed = 0
for n in range(1, COUNT + 1):
    gaps = []
    last = None
    for i in range(3):
        t = time.time()
        subprocess.run(BASE + ['-c', 'reset halt', '-c', 'bp 0x%x 2 hw' % VCC, '-c', 'resume', '-c', 'wait_halt 8000',
                               '-c', 'echo [format PC=%s [reg pc]]', '-c', 'mdw 0x%x 1' % TICK, '-c', 'rbp 0x%x' % VCC,
                               '-c', 'resume', '-c', 'exit'], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
        if last is not None:
            gaps.append(t - last)
        last = time.time()
    time.sleep(3)
    k, temp = keys()
    note = 'unreadable' if k is None else 'KEYS CHANGED' if k != previous else 'keys kept'
    changed += k is not None and k != previous
    print('triple %2d: next command started %s after the previous one let the firmware go; %s (%s)'
          % (n, ', '.join('%.2f s' % g for g in gaps), note, k), flush=True)
    if k is not None:
        previous = k
print('%d of %d triples changed the keys' % (changed, COUNT))
EOF
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Rewrite the README with the proven cause, add the finding to the report and the summary, and keep the reproduction script with a warning

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; R=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware; cd $R && python3 - <<'PY'
p='debug_ble/linux/README.md'; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('A reset is the other way to cut the power of a card for a short time')
b=s.index('The 50 ms are a margin chosen from these measurements')
s=s[:a]+'''A reset is the other way to cut the power of a card for a short time, and the fix does nothing
there: the firmware turns the rail on again when its millisecond counter reads 1. It does no harm:
in 68 resets sent over SWD while the card was powered and mounted, the firmware started every
time, opened and read `flysight.txt` correctly, and kept its keys.

'''+s[b:]
a=s.index('### The SkyGames application itself')
s=s[:a]+'''### A reset while `flysight.txt` is being rewritten: the FlySight forgets its BLE keys

Found by accident while measuring the above, then reproduced on purpose. It has nothing to do
with Linux, nor with the card losing power.

At every start, `FS_State_Init()` (`state.c`) reads `/flysight.txt`, then writes it back from
memory with `FA_CREATE_ALWAYS`, which empties the file first. On the bench build, timed with
breakpoints on three starts: the write begins 125 ms after the reset, the file is emptied at
130 ms and closed at 145 ms. A reset that falls in between leaves an empty file. At the next
start the firmware opens it, finds no `BLE_IRK` and no `BLE_ERK`, draws new ones, and writes them:
the change is permanent, and every other value of the file is back to its default.

| Reset sent while the firmware is stopped... | Keys afterwards |
|---------------------------------------------|-----------------|
| in `FS_State_Write()`, at its entry or just after its `f_open()` | changed, 6 times out of 6 |
| in `FS_State_Read()`, just after its `f_open()` (50 ms earlier) | kept, 4 out of 4 |
| in `FatFS_DeInit()`, once the file is closed | kept, 68 out of 68 |
| nowhere: an ordinary reset, card off | kept, 17 out of 17 |

In the six cases of the first row the next start was caught at the call that draws the new IRK,
in `FS_State_Complete()`, and the root directory it had just read showed `FLYSIGHT.TXT` with a
size of 0 and no cluster. A reset sent at the entry of `FS_State_Write()` counts as "during the
write" because the reset of OpenOCD lets the firmware run a few milliseconds more.

How it happened the first time: three SWD measurements run back to back, each one starting with a
reset about 0.15 s after the previous one had let the firmware go. Replayed eight times, that
sequence changed the keys six times. The keys were compared by the SHA-1 of what the firmware
holds in memory, read twice.

What it does to the hosts: with a new IRK, a bonded host no longer recognises the FlySight, and
the PC had to pair again each time. The FlySight still lists its bonded devices (4 here).

`master` `9ec7186` and `develop` `e67ee9f` have the same `FS_State_Init()`, the same emptying
`f_open()` and draw keys the same way when none was read; that is from reading their code, the
experiment was run on the branch build only. Nothing is changed for it here. Writing the file
only when its content changes, or writing a second file and renaming it, would close the window.

`state_rewrite_reset.py` is the script of the table. Its `midwrite` and `prewrite` modes change
the keys of the FlySight for good: every host has to pair again afterwards.

'''+s[a:]
old='''For that lockup, with the ST-Link connected and `arm-none-eabi-binutils` installed:
'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,'''For the two firmware defects of the SD card, with the ST-Link connected and
~~~~

~~~~bash
import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('- Caution, ask the user first: do not reset the bench FlySight while its microSD card is powered')
b=s.index('- Gotcha: `pkill -f PATTERN`')
s=s[:a]+'''- Caution: never send a reset to the FlySight within about 0.2 s of its previous start (for instance two OpenOCD commands with `reset halt` back to back). The firmware empties and rewrites `flysight.txt` 130-145 ms after each start; a reset in that window makes it draw new BLE keys for good, and every host must pair again. ## Assistant (18:47)
~~~~

Mon interprétation était fausse, et la vraie cause est maintenant prouvée. Ce n'est pas le reset avec la carte alimentée qui a changé les clés du FlySight : c'est un reset tombé pendant que le firmware réécrivait `flysight.txt`.

## Ce qui est réfuté

Sur 68 resets avec la carte alimentée et montée, le firmware a démarré à chaque fois, lu `flysight.txt` correctement et gardé ses clés. Les « clés changées en RAM » que j'avais vues en cours de route étaient un artefact de lecture SWD.

## Ce qui est prouvé

À chaque démarrage, `FS_State_Init()` relit `/flysight.txt` puis le réécrit avec `FA_CREATE_ALWAYS`, qui commence par le vider. Sur le firmware du banc, le fichier est vidé à 130 ms après le reset et refermé à 145 ms. Un reset dans cet intervalle laisse un fichier vide ; au démarrage suivant le firmware n'y trouve aucune clé, en tire de nouvelles et les écrit. Le changement est définitif, et les autres valeurs du fichier reviennent à leur défaut.

| Reset envoyé pendant que le firmware est arrêté… | Clés ensuite |
|---|---|
| dans `FS_State_Write()` (entrée, ou juste après son `f_open`) | changées, 6 sur 6 |
| dans `FS_State_Read()`, 50 ms plus tôt | conservées, 4 sur 4 |
| après la fermeture du fichier, carte encore alimentée | conservées, 68 sur 68 |
| reset ordinaire, carte éteinte | conservées, 17 sur 17 |

Dans les six cas de la première ligne, le démarrage suivant a été attrapé à l'appel qui tire le nouvel IRK, et le répertoire racine qu'il venait de lire montrait `FLYSIGHT.TXT` avec une taille de 0 et aucun cluster.

L'incident de 15:24 venait de trois mesures SWD enchaînées, chacune commençant par un reset environ 0,15 s après le redémarrage précédent. Rejouée 8 fois, cette séquence a changé les clés 6 fois.

## Ce que ça change pour ta question

Ce défaut-là est plus atteignable par un humain que le blocage : il suffit d'un reset ou d'une coupure dans les 150 premières millisecondes d'un démarrage. Je n'ai pas testé de scénario terrain (batterie faible qui redémarre en boucle, par exemple) ; c'est une hypothèse, pas une mesure.

`master` et `develop` ont le même `FS_State_Init()` et le même `f_open` qui vide le fichier ; je l'ai constaté en lisant le code, l'expérience n'a tourné que sur le firmware de la branche. Je n'ai rien corrigé : écrire le fichier seulement quand son contenu change, ou écrire un second fichier puis le renommer, fermerait la fenêtre.

## État du banc

- **FlySight** : ses clés ont changé une dizaine de fois pendant la preuve. Il liste toujours 4 appareils appairés, et ses fichiers sont intacts (`CONFIG.TXT` 6020 caractères, `FLYSIGHT.TXT` 916).
- **PC** : réappairé, nouvel identifiant `7B:A0:AF:93:D3:E2`. BlueZ garde deux appairages morts (`DC:73:5E:B4:33:86` et `FD:2D:95:CA:5B:D5`) que je n'ai pas supprimés.
- **Tes autres appareils** : le Mac, le téléphone Android et l'iPad devront oublier ce FlySight et le réappairer. Dans SkyGames sur Linux, il faudra supprimer la carte du FlySight et le rajouter.

Tout est consigné dans [debug_ble/linux/README.md](debug_ble/linux/README.md) et [debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html](debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html). Le script de reproduction est [state_rewrite_reset.py](debug_ble/linux/state_rewrite_reset.py) ; ses modes `midwrite` et `prewrite` changent les clés pour de bon. Rien n'est commité.

~~~~bash
"""Applies the state-file fix to a FlySight/state.c (branch, master or develop). usage: apply_statefix.py <state.c>"""

static FIL stateFile;

	{
		/* No state file yet: the keys must still be generated, or this boot would run
		   with all-zero root keys and the next one with different ones */
		FS_State_Complete();
		return;
	}

		return;

		/* A reset between the removal of the previous state file and the renaming of

		if ((f_rename(STATE_TEMP, STATE_FILE) != FR_OK) ||
~~~~

**Tool: Write** `/home/[user]/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux/state_rewrite_reset.py`

~~~~
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Resets the firmware at a chosen point of its start-up, lets the next start run without stopping
it, and says whether the BLE keys kept in /flysight.txt survived.

usage: state_rewrite_reset.py <elf> <count> <mode> <dump directory>

Each mode stops the firmware somewhere during a start-up, then sends the reset:
  idle       nowhere: an ordinary reset, microSD card off
  preread    just after FS_State_Read() has opened the state file
  midwrite   just after FS_State_Write() has opened the file it writes
             (without the fix: /flysight.txt, emptied; with it: /flysight.tmp)
  preunlink  the new file is complete, the previous one is about to be removed   (fix only)
  gap        the previous file is removed and the new one is NOT renamed: the call
             to f_rename() is skipped, the start-up finishes, then an ordinary reset   (fix only)
  powered    in FatFS_DeInit(): everything written and closed, card still powered

WARNING: on a firmware without the fix, midwrite makes the FlySight draw new BLE keys, for good.
Every host bonded with it has to pair again afterwards.

The next start is caught only if it is about to draw a new IRK, or reaches Error_Handler().
Keys are never printed, only the first characters of their SHA-1, read twice. The dumps hold raw
memory of the firmware, keys included: keep them out of the repository.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ELF, COUNT, MODE, DUMPS = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2]), sys.argv[3], sys.argv[4]
os.makedirs(DUMPS, exist_ok=True)
nm = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
dis = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-objdump', '-d', '--no-show-raw-insn', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def sym(name, size=None, optional=False):
    for line in nm.splitlines():
        p = line.split()
        if len(p) == 4 and p[3] == name and (size is None or int(p[1], 16) == size):
            return int(p[0], 16)
    if optional:
        return None
    raise SystemExit('no symbol ' + name)


def calls(function, callee):
    """Addresses of the calls to callee in function."""
    inside, found = False, []
    for line in dis.splitlines():
        if re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <%s>:' % re.escape(function), line):
            inside = True
            continue
        if inside and re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <', line):
            break
        m = re.match(r'^\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s+bl\s+[0-9a-f]+ <%s>' % re.escape(callee), line)
        if inside and m:
            found.append(int(m.group(1), 16))
    return found


STATE, FS = sym('state', 0x70), sym('fs', 0x234)
TICK = sym('uwTick')
ERROR = sym('Error_Handler') & ~1
[... 119 lines omitted ...]
        pc = reg(text, 'C1PC') & ~1
        tick = block(text, 'c1tick')
        line += 'CAUGHT %s at tick %s ms' % ('drawing a NEW IRK' if pc == NEW_IRK else 'in Error_Handler' if pc == ERROR else where(pc),
                                           tick[0] if tick else '?')
    else:
        line += 'no answer from the debugger'
    if final is None:
        line += '; keys: unreadable'
    else:
        line += '; keys %s (%s)' % ('CHANGED' if final != previous else 'kept', final)
        changed += final != previous
        previous = final
    line += '; %s; firmware in %s' % (card(text, 'end'), where(reg(text, 'ENDPC')))
    print(line, flush=True)
print('%s: %d of %d resets changed the keys' % (MODE, changed, COUNT))

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; T=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux/state_rewrite_reset.py; python3 - "$T" <<'PY'
import sys
p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read()
old="""UNLINK, RENAME = calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_unlink'), calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_rename')
FIXED = bool(UNLINK and RENAME)
"""
new="""UNLINK, RENAME = calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_unlink'), calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_rename')
FIXED = bool(UNLINK and RENAME)
# with the fix: reached only when /flysight.txt is missing at start-up and the new file is put in its place
RECOVER = (calls('FS_State_Read', 'f_rename') or [None])[0]
"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
old="""    tcl += ['bp 0x%x 2 hw' % NEW_IRK, 'bp 0x%x 2 hw' % ERROR, 'reset run',
            'if {[catch {wait_halt 3500}]} { echo "@@NORMAL" } else {',
            '  echo [format "C1PC=%s" [reg pc]]', '  echo "@@c1tick"', '  echo [mdw 0x%x 1]' % TICK, '  echo "@@end"', '  resume', '}',
            'catch {rbp 0x%x}' % NEW_IRK, 'catch {rbp 0x%x}' % ERROR,
            'sleep 3000', 'halt', 'sleep 200', 'echo [format "ENDPC=%s" [reg pc]]'] + read_card('end') + ['resume']"""
new="""    watched = [NEW_IRK, ERROR] + ([RECOVER] if RECOVER else [])
    tcl += ['bp 0x%x 2 hw' % a for a in watched] + ['reset run']
    for i in (1, 2):      # at most two of them in one start: the recovery, then new keys
        tcl += ['if {[catch {wait_halt 3500}]} { echo "@@QUIET%d" } else {' % i,
                '  echo [format "C%dPC=%%s" [reg pc]]' % i, '  echo "@@c%dtick"' % i, '  echo [mdw 0x%x 1]' % TICK, '  echo "@@end"', '  resume', '}']
    tcl += ['catch {rbp 0x%x}' % a for a in watched]
    tcl += ['halt', 'sleep 200', 'echo [format "ENDPC=%s" [reg pc]]'] + read_card('end') + ['resume']"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
old="""    if '@@NORMAL' in text:
        line += 'normal'
    elif reg(text, 'C1PC') is not None:
        pc = reg(text, 'C1PC') & ~1
        tick = block(text, 'c1tick')
        line += 'CAUGHT %s at tick %s ms' % ('drawing a NEW IRK' if pc == NEW_IRK else 'in Error_Handler' if pc == ERROR else where(pc),
                                           tick[0] if tick else '?')
    else:
        line += 'no answer from the debugger'"""
new="""    events = []
    for i in (1, 2):
        pc = reg(text, 'C%dPC' % i)
        if pc is None:
            continue
        tick = block(text, 'c%dtick' % i)
        what = {NEW_IRK: 'CAUGHT drawing a NEW IRK', ERROR: 'CAUGHT in Error_Handler',
                RECOVER: 'state file missing, new file put in its place'}.get(pc & ~1, where(pc))
        events.append('%s at tick %s ms' % (what, tick[0] if tick else '?'))
    if events:
        line += ', then '.join(events)
    elif '@@QUIET1' in text:
        line += 'normal'
    else:
        line += 'no answer from the debugger'"""
assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new,1)
s=s.replace("The next start is caught only if it is about to draw a new IRK, or reaches Error_Handler().","The next start is stopped only if it is about to draw a new IRK, reaches Error_Handler(), or\\n(with the fix) finds /flysight.txt missing and puts the new file in its place.")
open(p,'w').write(s)
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Write the campaign script and start it, detached, on the four builds (master and develop, without and with the fix)

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; T=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux/state_rewrite_reset.py; python3 - "$T" <<'PY'

PY
mkdir -p $S/statefix; cat > $S/statefix/campaign.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: campaign.sh <variant>...   For each firmware: BLE check, the resets of state_rewrite_reset.py, BLE check again.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
CLI=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/Scripts/cli; LNX=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux
T=$LNX/state_rewrite_reset.py; P=$LNX/jvm-probe/build/install/fs-jvm-probe/bin/fs-jvm-probe
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 7; }
ble_check() {   # $1 = log directory, $2 = label
  python3 $CLI/vbus.py button > /dev/null
  timeout 90 python3 $LNX/fs_probe.py connect --flag 01 > $1/lib_$2.log 2>&1; RC=$?
  ID=$(grep -o "scan: found 'FlySight' as [0-9A-F:]*" $1/lib_$2.log | awk '{print $NF}' | tail -1)
  echo "BLE $2, library (pairing mode): exit=$RC identifier=$ID $(grep -E 'connected in|RESULT' $1/lib_$2.log | sed 's/^ *[0-9.]* //' | tr '\n' ';')"
  sleep 4
  timeout 120 $P FlySight $ID > $1/jvm_$2.log 2>&1
  echo "BLE $2, Kotlin (idle): exit=$? $(grep -o 'config.txt[^|]*' $1/jvm_$2.log | cut -c1-44); $(grep -o 'flysight.txt: [0-9]* characters' $1/jvm_$2.log); $(grep -o 'RESULT: [A-Z ]*' $1/jvm_$2.log)"
  sleep 3
}
for V in "$@"; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf; L=$S/statefix/$V; mkdir -p $L
  echo "################ $V   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  flash $E
  ble_check $L before
  MODES="idle:3 preread:3 midwrite:4"
  case $V in *statefix*) MODES="$MODES preunlink:4 gap:3";; esac
  MODES="$MODES powered:3"
  for M in $MODES; do python3 $T $E ${M#*:} ${M%:*} $L/dumps 2>&1 | grep -v "^before:"; done
  ble_check $L after
  echo "DONE $V"
done
echo "################ bench firmware back (branch + the three firmware fixes + trace)   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
flash $S/fw/build/flysight.elf
ble_check $S/statefix bench
echo CAMPAIGN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)
EOF
chmod +x $S/statefix/campaign.sh; pgrep -f "skygames[.]MainKt|[s]tale_subscriber" | wc -l; cd $S/statefix && setsid nohup ./campaign.sh master-unmodified master-statefix develop-unmodified develop-statefix > $S/statefix/campaign.log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown; date +%H:%M:%S
~~~~

## Assistant (19:56)

Le correctif est fait et il tient sur les quatre builds : sans lui, `master` et `develop` perdent leurs clés à chaque reset pendant l'écriture ; avec lui, aucun des 20 resets par build ne les change.

## Le correctif

Dans [FlySight/state.c](FlySight/state.c) (33 lignes modifiées) :

- `FS_State_Write()` écrit le nouvel état dans `/flysight.tmp`. Il ne supprime `/flysight.txt` et ne renomme le nouveau fichier qu'une fois celui-ci complet et fermé sans erreur. L'ancien fichier reste donc valide jusque-là.
- `FS_State_Read()`, s'il ne peut pas ouvrir `/flysight.txt`, renomme `/flysight.tmp` et le lit. Cela couvre un reset tombé entre la suppression et le renommage.

## Les tests

Chaque build a reçu les mêmes resets par SWD, firmware arrêté à l'endroit indiqué. « + fix » = le commit publié avec ce seul correctif.

| Reset envoyé, firmware arrêté… | `master` | `master` + fix | `develop` | `develop` + fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nulle part (reset ordinaire) | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 |
| juste après l'ouverture en lecture | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 |
| juste après l'ouverture du fichier à écrire | **changées 4/4** | conservées 4/4 | **changées 4/4** | conservées 4/4 |
| nouveau fichier complet, ancien pas encore supprimé | — | conservées 4/4 | — | conservées 4/4 |
| ancien supprimé, renommage sauté par le débogueur | — | conservées 3/3 | — | conservées 3/3 |
| tout écrit et fermé, carte alimentée | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 | conservées 3/3 |

- **Sans correctif** : les 8 resets de la troisième ligne ont chacun été suivis d'un démarrage attrapé en train de tirer un nouvel IRK, et le PC a dû se réappairer.
- **Avec correctif** : après les 7 resets des lignes quatre et cinq de chaque build, le démarrage suivant a trouvé `/flysight.txt` absent, remis le nouveau fichier en place et relu les mêmes clés. La carte montrait ensuite `FLYSIGHT.TXT` à sa taille habituelle et pas de `FLYSIGHT.TMP`.
- **Contrôle BLE** avant et après les resets, sur chaque build : connexion du PC et lecture de `CONFIG.TXT` (6020 caractères) et `FLYSIGHT.TXT`. Sur les deux builds avec correctif, le PC s'est reconnecté sous le même identifiant, sans nouvel appairage.
- **Firmware de la branche** avec les trois correctifs : même série, 0 changement sur 20.

Les tests unitaires du firmware et ceux des scripts passent toujours.

Je n'ai pas rejoué le jeu de test d'appairage complet (bibliothèque, Kotlin, SkyGames, fenêtre d'appairage) sur ces builds : le correctif ne touche que l'écriture du fichier d'état. Dis-moi si tu le veux aussi.

## Limite

Un `flysight.txt` déjà vidé par un firmware sans le correctif ne peut pas être récupéré : ses clés sont perdues.

## État laissé

- Le banc tourne sur le firmware de la branche avec les trois correctifs (`crs.c`, `resource_manager.c`, `state.c`) et il répond.
- Les clés du FlySight ont encore changé pendant les tests sans correctif : le Mac, le téléphone Android et l'iPad restent à réappairer.
- Le PC est appairé sous l'identifiant `4E:55:D9:E4:DB:04`. BlueZ garde quatre appairages morts de ce FlySight (`DC:73:5E:B4:33:86`, `FD:2D:95:CA:5B:D5`, `DA:0D:D5:F8:32:D7`, `F8:3A:B2:DD:94:D1`) que je n'ai pas supprimés.
- Rien n'est commité.

Le détail est dans [debug_ble/linux/README.md](debug_ble/linux/README.md), le résumé dans [debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html](debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html), et le script des tests est [state_rewrite_reset.py](debug_ble/linux/state_rewrite_reset.py).

No `Co-Authored-By: Claude`, no "Generated with Claude Code", no mention of an assistant in commit messages or PR/MR descriptions, in flysight-2-firmware, SkyGames and its submodule FlySightApi. Commit and push only when the user asks.

**Why:** SkyGames' `CLAUDE.md` states it ("You never sign or co-sign a commit"). For the firmware repo the user said on 2026-10-07 (macOS session, recorded in `debug_ble/conversation.md`): "concernant les commits, même règle sur ce projet. tu peux refaire l'historique pour virer les IA qui signent". The firmware's `AGENTS.md` does not say it, hence this note.

**How to apply:** Write messages in the repository's style: English, imperative subject, then a body. This overrides the default attribution lines. SkyGames also forbids mutable git commands without a request, except `git submodule update --init --recursive` and `git config core.hooksPath Tools/git-hooks`. SkyGames work happens on `release/1.1.0`, not `master`.
=== branch: fix/ble_pairing_issues
--- 47e458f Guillaume Imbert
Generate the BLE keys when flysight.txt cannot be opened
FS_State_Read() returned as soon as f_open() failed, before the device ID was
read and before the IRK and ERK were generated. On a boot without
flysight.txt the BLE stack was therefore started with all-zero root keys,
the file was then written with those zeros, and the next boot generated
different keys.

Move that last step to FS_State_Complete() and call it on both paths.

--- dab59f0 Guillaume Imbert
Stop USB before flushing the storage cache on VBUS loss
FS_USBMode_DeInit flushed the USB mass-storage write cache while the USB
device was still attached. A host command arriving during the flush made the
USB interrupt use the microSD while the flush was using it from the task, and
the SPI/DMA transfer in SPIx_WriteReadData (which waits with no timeout) could
then never complete, leaving the firmware stuck or in Error_Handler.

Call USBD_LL_Stop() first. USBD_DeInit() already starts with it, so this only
moves the disconnection before the flush.

Reproduced with a host writing to the card while VBUS is faked low over
ST-Link: 4 of 12 unplugs stalled on this branch and 1 of 12 on master. With
this change 0 of 24 stalled, and 256 KB written just before the unplug is
intact after replugging.

--- 578ce22 Michael Cooper
Add configurable rate for ActiveLook

--- e6e1aea Michael Cooper
Add battery level service

<h2 id="b1"><span class="num">1.</span>Bug 1: a bonded Mac can no longer connect</h2>

<h2 id="b3"><span class="num">3.</span>Bug 3: all-zero BLE keys on a first boot without <code>flysight.txt</code></h2>

<h3 class="step">Glossary</h3>
<dl>
  <dt><code>BLE_IRK</code> and <code>BLE_ERK</code></dt>
  <dd>The two root keys stored in <code>flysight.txt</code> and given to the stack at start-up (<code>CONFIG_DATA_IR_OFFSET</code>, <code>CONFIG_DATA_ER_OFFSET</code>). The first one determines how bonded devices recognise the FlySight; the second one is used for the link keys. <code>FS_State_Read()</code> generates them randoml
</dl>

<h3 class="step">Problem</h3>
<p><code>FS_State_Read()</code> returns as soon as <code>flysight.txt</code> cannot be opened, before the code that generates the keys:</p>
<div class="file">FlySight/state.c</div>
<pre><code>memset(state.ble_irk, 0, CONFIG_DATA_IR_LEN);
memset(state.ble_erk, 0, CONFIG_DATA_ER_LEN);
...
if (f_open(&amp;stateFile, "/flysight.txt", FA_READ) != FR_OK)
    return;                                  <span class="cm">// keys stay all zero for this boot</span>
...
<span class="cm">/* Initialize IRK if needed */</span>             <span class="cm">// never reached in that case</span>
while (is_all_zeros(state.ble_irk, CONFIG_DATA_IR_LEN)) { ... }</code></pre>
<p>So on a first boot with no file (a new card, or a file deleted to reset the device, which <code>Docs/ble.md</code> suggests), the stack runs with all-zero root keys and the new <code>flysight.txt</code> is written with zeros. At the following boot the file exists, the zeros are replaced by random keys, and the FlySight's iden
<p><strong>Measured:</strong> delete <code>flysight.txt</code>, reboot: the recreated file contains <code>BLE_IRK: 0000&hellip;0000</code>. With the fix it contains random keys, unchanged after another reboot. The effect on an existing bond was not measured.</p>

<h3 class="step">Proposed fix</h3>
<p>Move the end of the function (device ID, key generation) into a helper called on both paths:</p>
<div class="file">FlySight/state.c</div>
<pre><code><span class="add">+static void FS_State_Complete(void)
+{
+	/* Get device ID */
+	...
+	/* Initialize IRK if needed */
+	...
+	/* Initialize ERK if needed */
+	...
+}
+</span>

**Tool: Bash** — Commit the state file fix alone on the branch, with a message in the repository's style and no AI attribution

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware && cat > $S/commit_statefix.txt <<'EOF'
Keep the previous flysight.txt until the new one is written

FS_State_Write() opened flysight.txt with FA_CREATE_ALWAYS, which empties the
file before it is rewritten. FS_State_Init() does that at every start, so the
card holds an empty state file for about 15 ms, 130 ms after a reset. A reset
in that window leaves it empty: the next start reads no BLE_IRK and no
BLE_ERK, draws new ones and writes them. Bonded hosts then no longer recognise
the FlySight, and the other values of the file are back to their defaults.

Write the new state to flysight.tmp, and remove flysight.txt and rename the
new file only once it is complete and was closed without error. A reset
between the removal and the renaming leaves only the new file:
FS_State_Read() renames it when flysight.txt cannot be opened.

Reproduced by sending resets over ST-Link with the firmware stopped during a
start. With the reset sent just after the file to write is opened, 4 of 4
changed the keys on master and 4 of 4 on develop. With this change 0 of 20
resets did, on master, on develop and on this branch, 7 of the 20 falling
between the removal and the renaming.

FS_State_Write() also runs when active mode or start mode starts, when config
mode ends and after USB is unplugged. Those paths were not tested with this
change.
EOF
git diff --cached --quiet && echo "nothing staged before" ; git add FlySight/state.c && git diff --cached --stat | tail -2 && git commit -q -F $S/commit_statefix.txt && git log -1 --format='%h %an <%ae>%n%s' && git status --short | cat
~~~~

## Assistant, note while working (20:32)

J'ai confirmé que sur une carte pleine, FatFs n'écrit que partiellement sans renvoyer d'erreur (`f_write` donne `FR_OK` mais avec moins d'octets, seul le retour de `f_printf` le révèle). Je corrige donc le code : si l'écriture du nouveau fichier est incomplète, on retombe sur la réécriture en place comme avant, pour ne jamais faire pire que l'ancien comportement.

**Tool: Bash** — Rewrite the fix so that a card with no room falls back to the previous in-place rewrite, apply it to the working tree and show the changed part

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cat > $S/four/apply_statefix.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Applies the state-file fix to a FlySight/state.c (branch, master or develop). usage: apply_statefix.py <state.c>"""
import sys
p = sys.argv[1]
s = open(p).read()


def swap(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old
    s = s.replace(old, new)


swap('''static FS_State_Data_t state;
static FIL stateFile;
''', '''#define STATE_FILE "/flysight.txt"
#define STATE_TEMP "/flysight.tmp"

static FS_State_Data_t state;
static FIL stateFile;
''')

branch = '''	if (f_open(&stateFile, "/flysight.txt", FA_READ) != FR_OK)
	{
		/* No state file yet: the keys must still be generated, or this boot would run
		   with all-zero root keys and the next one with different ones */
		FS_State_Complete();
		return;
	}
'''
if branch in s:
    swap(branch, '''	if (f_open(&stateFile, STATE_FILE, FA_READ) != FR_OK)
	{
		/* A reset between the removal of the previous state file and the renaming of
		   the new one leaves only the new one: put it in place and read it */
		if ((f_rename(STATE_TEMP, STATE_FILE) != FR_OK) ||
				(f_open(&stateFile, STATE_FILE, FA_READ) != FR_OK))
		{
			/* No state file yet: the keys must still be generated, or this boot would run
			   with all-zero root keys and the next one with different ones */
			FS_State_Complete();
			return;
		}
	}
''')
else:
~~~~
