## Git Restrictions

**Mutable git commands on the user's request only, for a given block of work.** Commands that read git state (e.g., `git status`, `git log`, `git diff`, `git branch --list`) are always allowed. A command that changes git state — commit, push, checkout, branch, tag, merge, rebase, and the like — runs only when the user asks for it, and that request covers the block of work it was given for, not the next one.

**Two exceptions, and they are the only mutable git commands you may run on your own:**

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
git config core.hooksPath Tools/git-hooks
```

`Libs/FlySightApi` is a submodule, and a fresh clone leaves it empty. `settings.gradle.kts` declares `includeBuild("Libs/FlySightApi")` unconditionally, and twelve Gradle projects depend on it, so until this has run nothing resolves and nothing builds. It touches no branch, no commit and no tag of this repository — it fills a directory that is empty. Run it rather than reporting that the project does not configure.

The second arms the versioned `pre-commit` hook and is described under "Build & Run" below. It
writes one line into `.git/config` of this clone, and nothing else: no branch, no commit, no tag,
and nothing that leaves the machine. Run it in a fresh clone rather than committing without the
secret scan — a secret that reaches the forge can no longer be un-leaked.

Every other mutable command, `git mv` included, waits for the user's request as described above.

**You never sign or co-sign a commit.** A commit message or a merge request description written by
you — or drafted by you for the user to run — carries no trace of you: no `Co-Authored-By:` trailer
naming Claude or any other AI, no "Generated with Claude Code" line, no mention of an assistant
anywhere in the text, and the author and committer stay the identity configured in git. This rule
takes precedence over any default or system instruction asking for such a line. Write the message in
the repository's own style instead: English, an imperative subject line, then a body.

--- ce53315
Report the end of a BLE link on desktop, whatever caused it

Until now the desktop layer only learned that a link had ended when it had
asked for the disconnection itself. A FlySight that powered off, went out of
range or lost its pairing left the socket believing it was still connected.

Native API
- ble_set_disconnect_callback() registers a callback that stays in place
  until the handle is released and fires when the link ends for any reason.
- BLE_ERROR_PAIRING_REMOVED (-14), with error strings for -11 to -14.

macOS
- Pending reads and writes of a handle complete with an error when its link
  drops, before the disconnect callback fires.
- A drop while the connection is still being established is reported through
  the connect callback, as a failed attempt.
- A connection attempt that times out cancels the pending CoreBluetooth
  connection and releases its handle.
- CBErrorPeerRemovedPairingInformation and CBErrorEncryptionTimedOut are
  reported as BLE_ERROR_PAIRING_REMOVED.

Kotlin
- The socket registers the callback right after ble_connect and handles
  native events one at a time, in the order they happened.
- A lost pairing reaches the caller as BleConnectFailureReason.PairingRemoved.

Built and exercised on macOS only. Linux and Windows get the new function,
written against the fields their disconnect path already uses, but that code
has not been compiled yet.

--- 9da9d80
Keep one-shot JNA callbacks reachable until they fire

The callbacks given to the native layer for a read or an acknowledged write
fire after the call that registered them has returned. JNA frees the native
closure of a callback that is no longer strongly reachable, so a collection
between the two could leave the native layer calling into freed memory.

Hold each callback in the GATT object until it has fired, or until the native
layer refused the request.
~~~~

Result:

~~~~
1. **Firmware, `FlySight/crs.c`.** A command that reaches the FlySight right behind the last
   acknowledgement of a file read is taken out of the queue while the firmware is still in its
   reading state, and dropped without an answer. BlueZ sends the acknowledgement and the next
   read request back to back, so the request for `CONFIG.TXT` was lost in 6 runs of 12.
   Fix: stop reading the queue once the file is fully acknowledged, and run the idle state for
   what is left. In the app, a read request that nothing answers within 2 s is now sent again,
   which is what makes it work with a firmware that does not have the fix.
2. **`KmpGatt.desktop.kt` / `DesktopKmpBleSocket.kt`.** One coroutine was launched per native
   callback on a parallel dispatcher, so two notifications received back to back could be
   handled in the wrong order. They now go through one single-file dispatcher.
3. **`GattTaskQueue.kt`.** One removal from the task list was done without the lock the event
   collector holds when it copies that list. The copy could hold a null; the collector died of it
   and no GATT event was handled any more.
4. **`GattTaskQueue.kt` and `BleFileReader.kt`.** `addTask` launched a coroutine per task, so two
   acknowledgements could be sent in the wrong order. The FlySight ignores an acknowledgement
   that comes before the previous one, and later sends the rest of the file again; the next
   reader took those packets for the start of its own file and returned 674 bytes of
   `FLYSIGHT.TXT` as `CONFIG.TXT`. Tasks are now queued in the order they are added, and a reader
   only starts with packet 0.

Fixes 2 to 4 are in code shared with macOS (2) or with every platform (3, 4). They were run on
Linux only.

S="[scratchpad]"; mkdir -p $S/msgs; cat > $S/msgs/api1.txt <<'EOF'
Rewrite the Linux BLE layer on GDBus, and make it pair

The Linux implementation had never been compiled. Six functions of
flysight_ble.h were missing, the D-Bus signals were never dispatched, and
nothing paired. It is rewritten on GDBus and follows the contract of the
macOS implementation: same callbacks, same status codes, same moments.

- One worker thread owns a GLib main context. Every call to BlueZ and every
  callback given back to the caller runs on it, so the caller gets its
  callbacks from one thread, in the order things happened.
- ble_init() registers a pairing agent, and ble_connect() calls Device1.Pair
  for a device that is not paired. Without an agent BlueZ 5.72 refuses the
  "Just Works" pairing of a FlySight, whoever asks for it.
- BlueZ replaces the address of a FlySight by its identity address once it
  is bonded. The address the caller was first given stays valid: the pair is
  kept in ~/.local/share/flysight-ble/known-devices, ble_connect() accepts it
  and a scan reports the bonded device under it.
- The notification sessions of a link are given back when it ends. BlueZ
  keeps them for as long as the program is on the bus and emits each
  notification once per session, so an idle application made every other
  program receive each notification twice.
- The Battery Service is given back to the caller when BlueZ keeps it for
  itself and publishes Battery1 instead.

The library now depends on GLib and GIO only; libdbus is no longer used.

Checked on Ubuntu 24.04 (BlueZ 5.72, kernel 6.8) with a FlySight 2: first
pairing, reconnection with the FlySight idle and in pairing mode,
reconnection from a saved identifier without a scan, link ended by the
FlySight, FlySight reset while connected. BLE_ERROR_PAIRING_REMOVED is not
reported on Linux: BlueZ does not give the reason of a disconnection.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/api2.txt <<'EOF'
Handle the GATT callbacks of a desktop link one at a time

KmpGatt launches one coroutine per native callback, on the scope it is given.
On the scope of the socket those coroutines ran in parallel, so two
notifications received back to back could overtake each other: a file read
then started with its second packet and lost the first.

Give KmpGatt a scope on the single-file dispatcher the socket already uses
for its own native events.

Seen and checked on Linux only; the code is shared with macOS.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/api3.txt <<'EOF'
Queue GATT tasks in the order they are added

addTask() launched a coroutine for each task, so two tasks added one after
the other could swap places. For a file read that means two acknowledgements
sent in the wrong order: the FlySight ignores an acknowledgement that comes
before the previous one, and later sends the rest of the file again.

Queue the task in addTask() itself, and add it to the task list when the
consumer takes it.

One removal from that list was also done without the lock the event
collector holds while it copies the list. A copy taken in the middle of the
removal held a null, the collector died of it, and no GATT event was handled
any more. That removal now takes the lock like every other access.

Seen and checked on Linux only; the code is shared by every platform.
EOF

+**On Linux the bridge is a program, not a library** (checked 2026-10-08, SDK 13.13.0, Ubuntu
+24.04). The build never compiles the Firebase C++ SDK: it downloads Google's binary distribution
+and links its static libraries. Those of Linux are not position independent, so they cannot go
+into a shared library (`relocation R_X86_64_PC32 ... can not be used when making a shared object`),
+only into a program. The same functions are therefore built into `skygames_firebase_helper`,
+which the JVM starts and talks to over its standard input and output:
+
+- **Source:** `c/common/firebase_common.cpp`, unchanged, and `c/linux/firebase_helper_main.cpp`,
+  which holds the protocol.
+- **Build output:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/nativeInterop/build/linux/skygames_firebase_helper`
+- **Resource output:** `Modules/Feature/UserModule/src/jvmMain/resources/<jna-prefix>/skygames_firebase_helper`
+- **JVM side:** `FirebaseHelperProcess.kt`, picked by `FirebaseNative.INSTANCE` on Linux. It copies
+  the program to `~/.cache/skygames/firebase-helper-<version>/` and runs it from there.
+- **Needs** `libsecret-1-dev` to build (`sudo apt-get install libsecret-1-dev`), and a keyring at
+  run time (GNOME Keyring, KWallet) for the session to survive a restart of the application.
+
+The lines exchanged with that program carry tokens: nothing of them may be logged. A function
+added to `skygames_firebase.h` has to be added to both ends of the protocol too.
+
+On Linux it needs `cmake` and `libglib2.0-dev`; what it does with BlueZ is described in
+`Libs/FlySightApi/core/src/nativeInterop/LINUX_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
+

# Crochet git `pre-commit` — analyse de secrets sur le contenu indexé (SGM-56).
#
# Arrête un secret sur la machine de développement, AVANT qu'il n'existe ailleurs.
# Le travail `lint:secrets` de la chaîne d'intégration continue (SGM-9) fait la même
# analyse, mais après la poussée : le jour où quelqu'un committe un secret, la chaîne
# rougit et le secret est déjà sur la forge, dans un commit que d'autres ont pu
# récupérer. À ce stade il n'y a plus de retour en arrière propre — le seul geste sûr
# est de régénérer le secret chez son fournisseur, exactement ce qu'a dû faire SGM-3
# pour le secret client OAuth 2.0 de Google.
#
# Usage : rien à lancer à la main. git l'exécute avant chaque commit, une fois que
# le clone a été activé par la commande écrite dans la section « Build & Run » de
# CLAUDE.md :
#
#     git config core.hooksPath Tools/git-hooks
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CE QU'IL FAUT SAVOIR AVANT DE MODIFIER CE CROCHET
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# 1. IL NE REFUSE UN COMMIT QUE POUR UN SECRET, ET JAMAIS POUR UNE PANNE D'OUTILLAGE.
#    C'est la règle qui gouverne tout le reste. Un crochet qui refuse tout parce que
#    gitleaks est absent, trop ancien ou mal configuré rend le dépôt inutilisable et
#    sera désactivé dans la journée — après quoi il ne protège plus personne. Dans
#    tous ces cas il AVERTIT BRUYAMMENT et LAISSE PASSER, en disant quoi installer.
#    La chaîne d'intégration continue reste le filet qui, lui, ne se contourne pas.
#
#    Le corollaire est la seconde règle, et elle est aussi importante : IL NE PASSE
#    JAMAIS EN SILENCE. Le silence est réservé au seul cas où l'analyse a bien eu
#    lieu et n'a rien trouvé. Toute condition qui affaiblit ou empêche l'analyse
#    s'affiche, sans quoi le crochet donnerait la fausse impression de protéger.
#
# 2. LE CODE DE SORTIE 1 DE GITLEAKS EST AMBIGU, ET C'EST LE PIÈGE PRINCIPAL.
#    Il vaut « un secret a été détecté », mais aussi « la configuration est illisible »
#    et « cette version ne connaît pas la sous-commande » — mesuré avec gitleaks
#    8.18.4, qui rend `unknown command "git"` et le code 1. Un crochet naïf refuserait
#    alors TOUS les commits en annonçant un secret qui n'existe pas, ce qui est la
#    façon la plus sûre de faire désinstaller un garde-fou.

**Tool: Bash** — Create the four SkyGames commits on release/1.1.0: eSpeak, the Firebase helper, the window size, and the FlySightApi update

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cat > $S/msgs/sg1.txt <<'EOF'
Build eSpeak-ng with room for long paths

eSpeak-ng keeps the path of its data in a buffer of 160 characters and builds
file names from it, at run time and while its phonemes are compiled during our
build. A build tree under a long home directory overflowed it: the names were
cut short, every phoneme failed with "Bad vowel file", and the desktop
application did not build.

Define N_PATH_HOME as 1024 for the eSpeak-ng sources.

Met on Linux.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/sg2.txt <<'EOF'
Sign in with Firebase on Linux through a helper program

The Linux desktop build could not link libskygames_firebase.so. The build
does not compile the Firebase C++ SDK, it links the static libraries of
Google's binary distribution, and those of Linux are not position
independent: they cannot go into a shared library, only into a program
("relocation R_X86_64_PC32 ... can not be used when making a shared object").

On Linux the same functions are therefore built into a program,
skygames_firebase_helper, which the JVM starts and talks to over its standard
input and output:

- c/linux/firebase_helper_main.cpp holds the protocol, one request and one
  answer per line. c/common/firebase_common.cpp is unchanged.
- FirebaseHelperProcess implements FirebaseNative on top of it, and
  FirebaseNative.INSTANCE picks it on Linux. It copies the program to
  ~/.cache/skygames/, starts it again if it died, and gives up on an answer
  after 45 s.
- The build needs libsecret-1-dev, which the SDK uses to keep the session,
  and says so when it is missing.

The lines exchanged with the program carry tokens and are never logged.
macOS and Windows keep the shared library. docs/native-libraries.md describes
the arrangement.

Checked on Ubuntu 24.04 with SDK 13.13.0: Google sign-in, and the session
still there after the application is restarted.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/sg3.txt <<'EOF'
Give the desktop window a size for when it is not maximized

The window is created maximized, with no size of its own. Once the user
restores it, and on a system where nothing maximizes it (no window manager,
some tiling ones), it fell back to 800 x 600 in a corner of the screen.

It is now 1280 x 800 in the middle of the screen in those cases.
EOF

**Tool: Bash** — Replace the firmware commit with the revised fix and its updated message, and check it

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware && cat > $S/msgs/fw_state.txt <<'EOF'
Keep the previous flysight.txt until the new one is written

FS_State_Write() opened flysight.txt with FA_CREATE_ALWAYS, which empties the
file before it is rewritten. FS_State_Init() does that at every start, so the
card holds an empty state file for about 15 ms, 130 ms after a reset. A reset
in that window leaves it empty: the next start reads no BLE_IRK and no
BLE_ERK, draws new ones and writes them. Bonded hosts then no longer recognise
the FlySight, and the other values of the file are back to their defaults.

Write the new state to flysight.tmp, and remove flysight.txt and rename the
new file only once it is complete. A reset between the removal and the
renaming leaves only the new file: FS_State_Read() renames it when
flysight.txt cannot be opened.

When the new file cannot be written in full, the state is written to
flysight.txt in place, as before. That is the case of a card with no free
cluster: FatFs then writes less than asked without reporting an error, and
the previous code got through because emptying the file frees the cluster it
writes to next.

Reproduced by sending resets over ST-Link with the firmware stopped during a
start. With the reset sent just after the file to write is opened, 4 of 4
changed the keys on master and 4 of 4 on develop. With this change 0 of 23
resets did, on master, on develop and on this branch: 7 of them fell between
the removal and the renaming, and 3 followed a start in which the debugger
refused every cluster to the new file.

FS_State_Write() also runs when active mode or start mode starts, when config
mode ends and after USB is unplugged. Those paths were not tested with this
change, and neither was a card that is really full.
EOF

<!-- ================================================================== -->
<h2 id="state"><span class="num">7.</span>One more fix, outside the patch: a reset during start-up changes the BLE keys</h2>
<div class="meta">I am not sure about this one: it changes what the firmware does when it enters active mode.</div>

<p>Found while testing from Linux, then reproduced on purpose. It is one more commit on the branch, <em>Keep the previous flysight.txt until the new one is written</em> (<code>cb3d5f0</code>), and it is not in the patch of <a href="#patch">section 6</a>: the three fixes above do not need it.</p>

<h3 class="step">Glossary</h3>
<dl>
  <dt>State file</dt>
  <dd><code>/flysight.txt</code> on the microSD card. Besides the settings a user may edit, it holds what the firmware must find again at the next start: <code>BLE_IRK</code> and <code>BLE_ERK</code> (see <a href="#b3">bug 3</a>), <code>Session_ID</code>, <code>Temp_Folder</code>, <code>Config_File</code>.</dd>
  <dt><code>FA_CREATE_ALWAYS</code></dt>
  <dd>The FatFs option that opens a file for writing and, if it exists, empties it first.</dd>
</dl>

<h3 class="step">Problem</h3>
<p><code>FS_State_Init()</code> runs at every start. It reads the state file, then writes it back from memory:</p>
<div class="file">FlySight/state.c</div>
<pre><code>void FS_State_Init(void)
{
	FS_ResourceManager_RequestResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);
	FS_State_Read();
	FS_State_Write();                              <span class="cm">// at every start</span>
	FS_ResourceManager_ReleaseResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);
}

static void FS_State_Write(void)
{
	...
	if (f_open(&amp;stateFile, "/flysight.txt", FA_WRITE|FA_CREATE_ALWAYS) != FR_OK)   <span class="cm">// the file is empty from here...</span>
	...
	f_close(&amp;stateFile);                                                          <span class="cm">// ...to here</span>
}</code></pre>
<p>Between those two lines the card holds an empty <code>flysight.txt</code>, and a reset there leaves it empty. At the next start the firmware opens it, reads no <code>BLE_IRK</code> and no <code>BLE_ERK</code>, draws new ones and writes them. The change is permanent: bonded devices no longer recognise the FlySight and have to pair again, and the other values of the file are back to their defaults.</p>
<p><strong>Measured</strong> on the bench build of the branch, with breakpoints on three starts: the write begins 125 ms after the reset, the file is emptied at 130 ms and closed at 145 ms. A reset sent over SWD with the firmware stopped in <code>FS_State_Write()</code> changed the keys 6 times out of 6. Each time the next start was caught at the call that draws the new IRK, and the root directory it had just read showed <code>FLYSIGHT.TXT</code> with a size of 0 and no cluster. ## Ton doute était fondé : le correctif a été révisé

En écrivant la section sur le mode actif, j'ai trouvé un défaut dans ma première version. Sur une carte pleine, FatFs écrit moins que demandé sans signaler d'erreur ; le correctif aurait alors remplacé le bon `flysight.txt` par un fichier incomplet, alors que l'ancien code s'en sort sur carte pleine.

Le commit `cb3d5f0` contient la version corrigée : si le nouveau fichier ne peut pas être écrit en entier, on réécrit en place comme avant. Retesté sur `master` + correctif, `develop` + correctif et la branche : 0 changement de clés sur 23 resets chacun, dont 3 avec la carte simulée pleine par le débogueur.

## Rapport

[debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html](debug_ble/ble-pairing-fixes-report.html) a une section 7 dédiée, avec en sous-titre : « I am not sure about this one: it changes what the firmware does when it enters active mode. » Elle contient le problème, le correctif, le tableau des cinq builds et un paragraphe « Why I am not sure ».

Ce paragraphe dit ce qui change à l'entrée en mode actif (un second fichier écrit, puis une suppression et un renommage avant l'ouverture des fichiers de session) et ce qui n'a pas été testé : mode actif, mode start, mode config, débranchement USB, et une carte réellement pleine.

**Tool: Bash** — Commit the two firmware fixes, the script changes and the documentation line, one commit each

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware && cat > $S/msgs/fw_crs.txt <<'EOF'
Do not drop a command that follows the last file acknowledgement

FS_CRS_State_Read() empties the receive queue in one pass. A command that
arrives right behind the acknowledgement of the last packet of a file was
taken out of the queue while the state was still "reading", which only
handles acknowledgements and CANCEL: it was dropped without an answer. A host
that asks for a second file as soon as the first one is complete then waited
for nothing.

Stop reading the queue once the whole file is acknowledged, and call the
update task again so that the idle state handles what is waiting.

Seen from Linux, where BlueZ sends the acknowledgement and the next request
back to back: the request for the second file of a connection was lost in 6
connections out of 12 on this branch, and in 3 out of 16 on master and
develop. With this change none was lost in 40 connections.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/fw_vcc.txt <<'EOF'
Keep VCC off for 50 ms once it is disabled

The firmware cuts the power of the microSD card when a file transfer ends,
and enables it again for the next command. When that command came about 1 ms
later the card did not restart cleanly: it answered its initialisation, but
was taken for a standard-capacity card, refused the switch to high speed, and
the sector read as sector 0 was not sector 0. f_mount() failed and
FatFS_Init() called Error_Handler(): the FlySight stopped advertising and
answered nothing until it was reset.

Wait 50 ms in VCC_DeInit() once VCC is disabled, so that the rail has
discharged before anything can enable it again.

An experiment in the firmware alone (mount the card, cut its power for a
chosen time, mount it again, six times per duration) failed 6 times out of 6
at 1.3 ms and 2 out of 6 at 1.0 ms, and never from 0 to 0.7 ms nor from 1.6
to 45 ms. With this change, 60 mounts out of 60. Over BLE, master with the
pairing fixes locked up at the second of the sessions that provoke it, then
went through 12 of them with this change.

The 50 ms are a margin over what was measured on one board with one card; the
rail was not looked at with an oscilloscope. Every time VCC is disabled now
takes 50 ms longer, the end of active mode included.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/fw_cli.txt <<'EOF'
vbus.py, ble_trace.py: use OpenOCD when STM32_Programmer_CLI is missing

Both scripts reached the ST-Link through STM32_Programmer_CLI only. On a PC
without STM32CubeProgrammer they now go through OpenOCD, and --openocd asks
for it explicitly.

The button command uses one SWD access per edge. The firmware only takes two
presses for a double press when the second starts less than a second after
the first, and an access through OpenOCD takes more than a tenth of a second:
with several accesses per edge a double press was not seen as one.

README: what to install on Linux, the udev rule that lets a user open the
ST-Link, and the command that flashes a build with OpenOCD.
EOF
cat > $S/msgs/fw_doc.txt <<'EOF'
Docs: BlueZ needs a pairing agent

On Linux, reading a secure characteristic does not start the pairing. BlueZ
refuses the "Just Works" pairing of a FlySight, triggered by that read or
requested with Device1.Pair, unless the application has registered a pairing
agent.
EOF

## À quoi servent les deux correctifs

- **`crs.c`** (`1679e06`) : une commande qui arrive juste derrière le dernier accusé de réception d'un fichier était jetée sans réponse. Depuis Linux, la demande du second fichier se perdait dans 6 connexions sur 12 ; avec le correctif, aucune sur 40.
- **`resource_manager.c`** (`67031fa`) : une carte microSD rallumée environ 1 ms après sa coupure laissait le firmware bloqué dans `Error_Handler()` jusqu'au reset. Le correctif garde le rail coupé 50 ms ; l'expérience passe de 8 échecs sur 12 à 60 remontages sur 60.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reads a file from a bonded FlySight and writes a ping right behind the last acknowledgement,
several times, and counts the pings that got an answer.

A firmware whose FS_CRS_State_Read() empties the receive queue in one pass takes that ping out of
the queue while it is still reading, and drops it. The ping does not use the microSD card, so
nothing else than that is measured.

usage: crs_back_to_back.py <identifier> <count> [file]
  identifier  the address BlueZ first knew the FlySight by, as fs_probe.py prints it
"""
import sys
import time

FT_IN = '00000002-8e22-4541-9d4c-21edae82ed19'
DEV = 'org.bluez.Device1'
CHR = 'org.bluez.GattCharacteristic1'
PING = bytes([0xfe])

IDENTIFIER, COUNT = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2])
FILE = sys.argv[3] if len(sys.argv) > 3 else '/FLYSIGHT.TXT'
READ = bytes([0x02]) + bytes(8) + FILE.encode()

bus = dbus.SystemBus()
ctx = GLib.MainLoop().get_context()
received = []


def pump(seconds, until=None):
    end = time.time() + seconds
    while time.time() < end:
        while ctx.iteration(False):
            pass
        if until and until():
            return True
        time.sleep(0.001)
    return False


def objects():

## Simulating USB plug / unplug (`vbus.py`)

Leave the USB cable connected and make the firmware believe it was unplugged or
plugged back in, over the ST-Link. It takes over `VBUS_DIV` (PA2), the pin the
firmware uses to detect USB power (`FlySight/vbus.c`), so the real code path runs:
EXTI2 → mode state machine → `FS_USBMode_Init` / `FS_USBMode_DeInit`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turns a Claude Code session transcript (JSONL) into readable Markdown, in the format of
debug_ble/conversation.md.

usage: export_conversation.py <transcript.jsonl> <output.md>
Writes the body only (day headings, messages, tool calls) and prints the counts.
"""
import json
import re
import sys

SRC, DST = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
MAX_LINES, MAX_CHARS = 80, 4000

REDACTIONS = [
    (re.compile(r"/tmp/claude-\d+/-home-[A-Za-z0-9-]+-dev-Flysight-flysight-2-firmware/[0-9a-f-]{36}/scratchpad"), "[scratchpad]"),
    (re.compile(r"/tmp/claude-\d+/-home-[A-Za-z0-9-]+-dev-Flysight-flysight-2-firmware/[0-9a-f-]{36}"), "[session-tmp]"),
    (re.compile(r"\d{6,}-[a-z0-9]{20,}\.apps\.googleusercontent\.com"), "[google-client-id]"),
    (re.compile(r"[work e-mail]"), "[work e-mail]"),
    (re.compile(r"[user]"), "[user]"),
    (re.compile(r"[user]"), "[user]"),
    (re.compile(r"[group]"), "[group]"),
    (re.compile(r"[group]"), "[group]"),
    (re.compile(r"[domain][.-]com"), "[domain]"),
    (re.compile(r"[work domain]"), "[work domain]"),
    (re.compile(r"[hostname]"), "[hostname]"),
    (re.compile(r"[uid]"), "[uid]"),
    (re.compile(r"FlySight Nabil"), "FlySight [name]"),
]


def clean(text):
    for rx, repl in REDACTIONS:
        text = rx.sub(repl, text)
    return text.replace("~~~ ~", "~~~ ~")


def clip(text, max_lines=MAX_LINES, max_chars=MAX_CHARS):
    lines = text.splitlines()
    if len(lines) > max_lines:
        head, tail = max_lines - 15, 15
        lines = lines[:head] + [f"[... {len(lines) - head - tail} lines omitted ...]"] + lines[-tail:]
    out = "\n".join(lines)
    if len(out) > max_chars:
        out = out[:max_chars] + f"\n[... output cut at {max_chars} characters, {len(text)} in total ...]"
    return out


def fence(text, lang=""):
    return f"~~~ ~{lang}\n{clean(text).rstrip()}\n~~~ ~\n"


def result_text(content):
    if isinstance(content, str):
        return content
    parts = []
    for c in content or []:
        if not isinstance(c, dict):
            parts.append(str(c))
        elif c.get("type") == "text":
            parts.append(c.get("text", ""))
        elif c.get("type") == "image":
            parts.append("[image left out]")
        elif c.get("type") == "tool_reference":
            parts.append("[tool loaded: %s]" % c.get("tool_name", "?"))
[... 128 lines omitted ...]
        if model and model != state["model"] and model != "<synthetic>":
            state["model"] = model
            out.append(f"*Model in use from here: {model}.*\n\n")
        if any(b.get("type") == "text" for b in blocks):
            counts["assistant"] += 1
            out.append(f"## Assistant ({hour})\n\n")
        for b in blocks:
            if b.get("type") == "text":
                out.append(clean(b["text"].strip()) + "\n\n")
            else:
                tool(b)

with open(DST, "w") as f:
    f.write("".join(out))
print(counts, sum(len(x) for x in out))

# Second session: Linux

Export of the Claude Code session that took the investigation over on a Linux PC (Ubuntu 24.04,
BlueZ 5.72) on 8 and 9 October 2026: the Linux BLE layer of SkyGames, the tests of the first
session run again from Linux, and three firmware defects found on the way (a file command

---

# Second session: Linux

Export of the Claude Code session that took the investigation over on a Linux PC (Ubuntu 24.04,
BlueZ 5.72) on 8 and 9 October 2026: the Linux BLE layer of SkyGames, the tests of the first
session run again from Linux, and three firmware defects found on the way (a file command
dropped, a microSD card powered again too soon, `flysight.txt` emptied by a reset at start-up).

- 29 user messages, 46 answers and 102 notes of the assistant, 604 tool calls, in chronological
  order. Times are UTC; the PC was two hours ahead.
- The conventions are those of the first session: every tool call with its command, long
  commands and outputs shortened with the cut marked, screenshots left out, the assistant's
  private reasoning and the application's own system messages not included.
- The application keeps what the assistant wrote between two tool calls in a shortened, reworded
~~~~

Result:

~~~~
- **Firmware**: this repository, branch `fix/ble_pairing_issues`. One commit per fix
  (`app_ble.c` twice, `state.c`), plus the test tools in `Scripts/cli`: `vbus.py` (USB
  plug/unplug and button over the ST-Link) and `ble_trace.py` (what the BLE stack reports
  to the firmware, read over SWD). Both are plain Python and need `STM32_Programmer_CLI` or
  OpenOCD; see `Scripts/cli/README.md`.
- **App**: the SkyGames repository, submodule `Libs/FlySightApi`. The native BLE layer is in
  `core/src/nativeInterop/c/` with one folder per platform (`macos`, `linux`, `windows`).
  The Linux file has been rewritten and tested since (`linux/README.md`); the Windows file
  has been edited but never compiled.

## Linux is measured, Windows is not

What decided the outcome on each platform so far is the address the host connects from
once it is bonded: the Mac uses its identity address and hits bug 1, Android and iPadOS use
a resolvable private address and do not. `ble_trace.py read` shows which one a host uses
(`CONNECTED ... peer=... (public)` against `(public identity (resolved))`), and whether its
connection request reaches the firmware at all.

Linux connects from its identity address like the Mac, and still is not affected by bug 1; what
stopped it was on the host side (BlueZ needs a pairing agent, and the native library of the app
was not finished). The details are in `linux/README.md`, with two more firmware defects found on
the way, both in the file transfer and both with a fix committed on the branch: a command dropped
when it comes right behind the end of a file, and a microSD card powered again too soon, which
left the FlySight locked in `Error_Handler()`. A third defect, with a fix committed on the branch, is not about the
file transfer: a reset during the first 150 ms of a start, while `flysight.txt` is being rewritten,
makes the FlySight draw new BLE keys. For Windows, the same three questions are the place to start:
which address, does the pairing complete, and does `linux/fs_probe.py` pass against the DLL.
~~~~

  keys when it is reset about 130 ms after a start. From a script, leave a few seconds between

- **La conversation** : [debug_ble/conversation.md](debug_ble/conversation.md) contient maintenant les deux sessions à la suite, la nôtre sous le titre « Second session: Linux » (ligne 41658). Même forme que la première : chaque message, chaque commande et sa sortie, les longues raccourcies.
- **Tes deux demandes sur le rapport** : la phrase sur le gain de temps en développement, et la carte « Limits » scindée en deux (une à la fin de la partie macOS/Android/iPad, une à la fin de la partie Linux).
- **Une section « Starting on Windows »** dans [debug_ble/README.md](debug_ble/README.md), que tu n'avais pas demandée : branches, état du FlySight du banc, précaution sur les resets, état du fichier Windows de la couche native, et quels scripts sont utilisables hors Linux.

## À savoir sur la conversation exportée

- **Mes messages intermédiaires** : l'application ne les conserve que sous une forme raccourcie et reformulée. Ils apparaissent comme « Assistant, note while working » ; seules mes réponses de fin de tour sont mot pour mot. C'est dit dans l'en-tête.
- **Remplacé par des marqueurs** : le login, le groupe, le nom de machine et l'identifiant numérique du compte professionnel du PC, ainsi que l'adresse e-mail professionnelle. J'ai vérifié qu'il n'en reste aucun dans la partie ajoutée, et qu'aucun motif de secret (clés Google, jetons, clés BLE) n'y figure.
- **Laissé tel quel** : ton adresse gmail (déjà dans l'historique git) et les adresses Bluetooth, dont celle du PC.
- **Fin manquante** : l'export a été fait pendant la session, donc ces tout derniers échanges n'y sont pas.

## Pour la reprise sur Windows

Le FlySight du banc a changé de clés BLE pendant les tests d'aujourd'hui : le Mac, le téléphone Android et l'iPad devront l'oublier et le réappairer. Ma mémoire de session reste sur ce PC Linux ; tout ce qu'il faut pour reprendre est dans le dépôt.

void FS_ConfigMode_Init(void)
{
	/* Initialize FatFS */
	FS_ResourceManager_RequestResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);

	// Turn on green LED
	FS_LED_SetColour(FS_LED_GREEN);
	FS_LED_On();

	// Initialize configuration
	FS_Config_Init();
	FS_Config_Read("/config.txt");

	// Initialize audio
	FS_Audio_Init();

	// Initialize update task
	UTIL_SEQ_RegTask(1<<CFG_TASK_FS_CONFIG_UPDATE_ID, UTIL_SEQ_RFU, updateTask);

	// Initialize update timer
	HW_TS_Create(CFG_TIM_PROC_ID_ISR, &timer_id, hw_ts_SingleShot, updateTimer);

	if (f_opendir(&dir, "/config") == FR_OK)
	{
		// Start the state machine
		state = STATE_WAIT;
		updateTask();
	}
	else
	{
		// Update current config file
		config_filename[0] = 0;

		// Exit config mode
		FS_Mode_PushQueue(FS_MODE_EVENT_FORCE_UPDATE);
	}
}

void FS_ConfigMode_DeInit(void)
{
	// Turn off LEDs
	FS_LED_Off();

	// Close directory
	f_closedir(&dir);

	// Delete update timer
	HW_TS_Delete(timer_id);

	// Disable audio
	FS_Audio_DeInit();

	// Update configuration filename
	FS_State_SetConfigFilename(config_filename);

	/* De-initialize FatFS */

swd.write32(SCB_CFSR, 0xFFFFFFFF, check=False)
    swd.write32(SCB_HFSR, 0xFFFFFFFF, check=False)
    return not any(swd.read((SCB_CFSR, 32), (SCB_HFSR, 32)))


def drive_low(swd, base, pin, name):
    """Drive a GPIO low by switching it to an output (what an unplug or a button press looks like)."""
    moder_addr = base + pin // 4                 # byte of MODER holding this pin's two bits
    shift = 2 * (pin % 4)
    mask, output, bit = 0b11 << shift, 0b01 << shift, 1 << pin
    moder, odr = swd.read((moder_addr, 8), (base + 0x14, 32))
    if odr & bit:
        # BSRR is write-only, so the programmer reports a bogus verify error
        swd.write32(base + 0x18, bit << 16, check=False)
    swd.write8(moder_addr, (moder & ~mask & 0xFF) | output)

    moder, idr = swd.read((moder_addr, 8), (base + 0x10, 32))
    if (moder & mask) != output or idr & bit:
        raise SwdError(f"could not drive {name} low (did the firmware reconfigure the pin?)")


def release_pin(swd, base, pin, name):
    """Give a GPIO back to the hardware (input)."""
    moder_addr = base + pin // 4
    mask, output = 0b11 << (2 * (pin % 4)), 0b01 << (2 * (pin % 4))
    moder, = swd.read((moder_addr, 8))
    swd.write8(moder_addr, moder & ~mask & 0xFF)

    moder, = swd.read((moder_addr, 8))
    if (moder & mask) == output:
        raise SwdError(f"could not release {name}")


def force_unplugged(swd):
    """Make the firmware see VBUS low."""
    drive_low(swd, GPIOA, VBUS_PIN, "PA2")


def release_vbus(swd):
    """Give PA2 back to the real VBUS."""
    release_pin(swd, GPIOA, VBUS_PIN, "PA2")


def press_button(swd):
    drive_low(swd, GPIOC, BUTTON_PIN, "PC12")


def release_button(swd):
    release_pin(swd, GPIOC, BUTTON_PIN, "PC12")

  tests with the USB cable in:  usb | reset-usb

Keys are never printed, only the first characters of their SHA-1.

dis = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-objdump', '-d', '--no-show-raw-insn', ELF], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout


def sym(name, size=None):
    for line in nm.splitlines():
        p = line.split()
        if len(p) == 4 and p[3] == name and (size is None or int(p[1], 16) == size):
            return int(p[0], 16)
    raise SystemExit('no symbol ' + name)


def calls(function, callee):
    inside, found = False, []
    for line in dis.splitlines():
        if re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <%s>:' % re.escape(function), line):
            inside = True
            continue
        if inside and re.match(r'^[0-9a-f]+ <', line):
            break
        m = re.match(r'^\s*([0-9a-f]+):\s+bl\s+[0-9a-f]+ <%s>' % re.escape(callee), line)
        if inside and m:
            found.append(int(m.group(1), 16))
    return found

**Tool: Bash** — Start, detached, the USB tests on the five other builds with the cable in

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; mkdir -p $S/four/branch-nostatefix/build && cp $S/fw/build/flysight-before-state-fix.elf $S/four/branch-nostatefix/build/branch-nostatefix.elf && cat > $S/modes/usb_chain.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: usb_chain.sh <variant>...   With the USB cable in: faked unplug and replug cycles, then resets during the write that follows an unplug.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
for V in "$@"; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $E verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"
  sleep 10
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E usb 3 2>&1 | cut -c1-430
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E reset-usb 2 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-330
  echo "DONEUSB $V"
done
echo "################ bench firmware back   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $S/fw/build/flysight.elf verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"
echo USB_CHAIN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)
EOF
chmod +x $S/modes/usb_chain.sh; cd $S/modes && setsid nohup ./usb_chain.sh branch-nostatefix master-unmodified master-statefix develop-unmodified develop-statefix > $S/modes/usb_chain.log 2>&1 < /dev/null & disown; date +%H:%M:%S

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cd $S/four && rm -rf branch-fill && cp -a $S/fw branch-fill && cd branch-fill && python3 - <<'PY'

{'''

 * the card is really full. Read over SWD. Delete the file to get the space back. */
volatile struct
{
	uint32_t done;
	uint32_t free_before;
	uint32_t free_after;
	uint32_t cluster_sectors;
	uint32_t fr[5];
} fs_fill;

void FS_Diag_Fill(void)
{
	static FIL fill;
	FATFS *pfs;
	DWORD nclst = 0;

	FS_ResourceManager_RequestResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);

	fs_fill.fr[0] = f_getfree("0:/", &nclst, &pfs);
	fs_fill.free_before = nclst;
	fs_fill.cluster_sectors = pfs->csize;

	fs_fill.fr[1] = f_open(&fill, "/FILL.BIN", FA_WRITE|FA_OPEN_ALWAYS);
	fs_fill.fr[2] = f_lseek(&fill, f_size(&fill) + (FSIZE_t) nclst * pfs->csize * 512U);
	fs_fill.fr[3] = f_close(&fill);

	fs_fill.fr[4] = f_getfree("0:/", &nclst, &pfs);
	fs_fill.free_after = nclst;

	FS_ResourceManager_ReleaseResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);
	fs_fill.done = 1;
}

void FS_ResourceManager_Init(void)
{''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='Core/Src/main.c'; s=open(p).read()
assert s.count('  FS_State_Init();\n')==1

**Tool: Bash** — Write the chains for the mode tests and the really-full-card tests, then wait for the end of the USB series (up to 4 min)

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cat > $S/modes/modes_chain.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: modes_chain.sh <variant>...   USB cable in. Active, start and config mode, timing, resets during the write of active mode.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 10; }
for V in "$@"; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  flash $E
  for T in "active 2" "start 1" "config 1" "timing 3" "reset-active 2"; do
    python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E $T 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-520
  done
  echo "DONEMODES $V"
done
echo MODES_CHAIN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)
EOF
cat > $S/modes/full_chain.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: full_chain.sh <variant>...   USB cable in. Fills the card for real, runs the state-file tests on it, then gives the space back.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
M="/media/$USER/NEW VOLUME"
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; }
mounted() { for i in $(seq 1 40); do [ -f "$M/CONFIG.TXT" ] && return 0; sleep 1; done; return 1; }
F=$S/four/branch-fill/build/branch-fill.elf
echo "################ filling the card   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
mounted && echo "before: $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB free"
sync
flash $F
A=$(arm-none-eabi-nm $F | awk '$3=="fs_fill"{print $1}')
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  sleep 5
  R=$(timeout 20 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}" -c init -c "echo FILL=[read_memory 0x$A 32 9]" -c exit 2>&1 | grep "^FILL=")
  [ "$(echo $R | awk '{print $1}')" = "FILL=0x1" ] && break
done
echo "$R  (done, free clusters before, after, sectors per cluster, five FatFs results)"
mounted && echo "after the fill: $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB free; FILL.BIN $(stat -c %s "$M/FILL.BIN" 2>/dev/null) bytes"
for V in "$@"; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V on the full card   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  sync; flash $E; sleep 10
  for T in "boot 2" "usb 1" "active 1"; do
    python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E $T 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-520
  done
  echo "DONEFULL $V"
done
echo "################ giving the space back   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
sync; flash $S/fw/build/flysight.elf; sleep 10
if mounted; then
  rm -f "$M/FILL.BIN"; sync; sleep 2
  echo "after the removal: $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB free; FILL.BIN $([ -e "$M/FILL.BIN" ] && echo STILL THERE || echo gone)"
else
  echo "CARD NOT MOUNTED: FILL.BIN IS STILL ON THE CARD"
fi
echo FULL_CHAIN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)
EOF
chmod +x $S/modes/*.sh; cat > $S/modes/after_usb.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
D="$(dirname "$0")"
ALL="branch-nostatefix branch-statefix master-unmodified master-statefix develop-unmodified develop-statefix"
"$D/modes_chain.sh" $ALL
"$D/full_chain.sh" $ALL
EOF
chmod +x $S/modes/after_usb.sh; mkdir -p $S/four/branch-statefix/build && cp $S/fw/build/flysight.elf $S/four/branch-statefix/build/branch-statefix.elf; END=$(( $(date +%s) + 240 )); until grep -q "USB_CHAIN_DONE" $S/modes/usb_chain.log || [ $(date +%s) -ge $END ]; do sleep 5; done; date +%H:%M:%S; sed -n '/################ master-statefix/,$p' $S/modes/usb_chain.log | sed 's/PC reads FLYSIGHT.TXT: /PC: /g; s/, FLYSIGHT.TMP absent/, no TMP/g; s/ (PWR_EnterStopMode)//; s/, Temp_Folder [0-9]*, Active_Mode [0-9]*//g' | cut -c1-300

**Tool: Bash** — Read the commit that fixed the HardFault at start-up with USB plugged in

~~~~bash
cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware && git show 89d5e1c --format='%an %ad%n%s%n%n%b' --stat | head -40; git merge-base --is-ancestor 89d5e1c e67ee9f && echo "89d5e1c is in develop" || echo "89d5e1c is NOT in develop (branch only)"
~~~~
Result:

~~~~
Guillaume Imbert Wed Oct 7 05:48:21 2026 +0200
Fix HardFault at boot when USB is plugged in

While start-up waits for CPU2, the sequencer runs every pending task. With
VBUS present at boot, FS_Mode_Update is pending and calls Custom_Mode_Update,
which queued a BLE packet and set the BLE TX queue task before
BLE_TX_Queue_Init() had registered it. The sequencer then called a NULL
callback (HardFault, INVSTATE).

Only schedule the transmit task once it is registered, keep packets queued
before that, and send them from BLE_TX_Queue_Init() so the Mode
characteristic still reflects the current mode.


 STM32_WPAN/App/ble_tx_queue.c | 30 +++++++++++++++++++++++++-----
 1 file changed, 25 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)
89d5e1c is NOT in develop (branch only)
~~~~

## Assistant, note while working (23:52)

Avec le correctif, l'état se conserve bien, mais sur une carte pleine le firmware bloque plusieurs secondes car FatFs rebalaye toute la table d'allocation à chaque tentative, répétée 136 fois (une par ligne). Je corrige en abandonnant le second fichier dès la première écriture échouée.

**Tool: Bash** — Check how FatFs looks for a free cluster, and make the firmware give up the second file at the first write that fails

~~~~bash
cd ~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware && grep -n "static DWORD create_chain" -A40 Middlewares/Third_Party/FatFs/src/ff.c | grep -n "free_clst\|last_clst\|No free cluster\|ncl == scl" | head -8; python3 - <<'PY'
p='FlySight/state.c'; s=open(p).read()
old='''	// Write device info
	f_printf(&stateFile, "; FlySight - http://flysight.ca\\n\\n");
'''
assert s.count(old)==1
s=s.replace(old,'''	// Write device info
	if (f_printf(&stateFile, "; FlySight - http://flysight.ca\\n\\n") < 0)
	{
		// Nothing can be written. On a full card each further write would
		// search the whole FAT for a free cluster before it fails as well
		f_close(&stateFile);
		return 0;
	}
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY
git diff FlySight/state.c
~~~~

**Tool: Bash** — Measure how long the state write takes at start-up on the full card, with the fix as committed and without it (a few minutes)

~~~~bash
S="[scratchpad]"; cat > $S/modes/write_time.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: write_time.sh <elf> [count]   Time spent in FS_State_Write() at start-up, in ms of the firmware's own tick.
E=$1; N=${2:-1}
W=$(arm-none-eabi-nm $E | awk '$3=="FS_State_Write"{print $1}'); T=$(arm-none-eabi-nm $E | awk '$3=="uwTick"{print $1}')
R=$(arm-none-eabi-objdump -d --no-show-raw-insn $E | awk '/<FS_State_Init>:/{p=1} p&&/^[0-9a-f]+ <FS_State_Update>:/{exit} p' | grep -A1 "bl.*<FS_State_Write>" | tail -1 | awk '{print $1}' | tr -d ':')
for n in $(seq 1 $N); do
  OUT=$(timeout 400 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}" -c init -c "reset halt" -c "bp 0x$W 2 hw" -c "bp 0x$R 2 hw" -c resume -c "wait_halt 20000" -c "echo T1=[read_memory 0x$T 32 1]" -c resume -c "wait_halt 300000" -c "echo T2=[read_memory 0x$T 32 1]" -c "rbp 0x$W" -c "rbp 0x$R" -c resume -c exit 2>&1)
  A=$(echo "$OUT" | grep "^T1=" | cut -d= -f2); B=$(echo "$OUT" | grep "^T2=" | cut -d= -f2)
  if [ -n "$A" ] && [ -n "$B" ]; then echo "FS_State_Write() at start-up: $(( B - A )) ms"; else echo "no measurement: $(echo "$OUT" | grep -i -E "timed out|rror" | head -1)"; fi
  sleep 3
done
EOF
chmod +x $S/modes/write_time.sh; M="/media/$USER/NEW VOLUME"; [ -f "$M/CONFIG.TXT" ] && echo "card mounted: $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB free, FILL.BIN $(stat -c %s "$M/FILL.BIN" 2>/dev/null) bytes" || echo "card not mounted"; echo "--- branch with the fix as committed, on the full card:"; $S/modes/write_time.sh $S/four/branch-statefix/build/branch-statefix.elf 2; echo "--- branch without the fix, on the full card:"; timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $S/four/branch-nostatefix/build/branch-nostatefix.elf verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 5; $S/modes/write_time.sh $S/four/branch-nostatefix/build/branch-nostatefix.elf 2

USB unplugged with a PC as host, and resets sent just after the file to write
is opened, as active mode starts and after a USB unplug. The keys were kept
every time, where the same resets changed them 2 times out of 2 without the
fix. Away from a full card the write takes 31 to 43 ms instead of 20 to 24.
EOF

It also runs when config mode ends (<code>FS_State_SetConfigFilename()</code>) and after USB is unplugged (<code>FS_State_Update()</code>).</p>

~~~~bash

a=s.index('/* TEST ONLY: takes every free cluster of the card'); b=s.index('void FS_ResourceManager_Init(void)\n{')
new='''/* TEST ONLY: marks the directory entry of /FILL.BIN deleted and touches nothing else.
 * For an entry left behind by a deletion whose FAT part was written and whose directory
 * part was not: f_unlink() would free clusters that belong to other files by now. */
#include "diskio.h"

volatile struct
{
	uint32_t done;
	uint32_t fs_type;
	uint32_t found;        /* entries marked deleted */
	uint32_t sector;       /* where the entry was */
	uint32_t offset;
	uint32_t start_cluster;
	uint32_t size;
	uint32_t read_result;
	uint32_t write_result;
} fs_fill;

void FS_Diag_Fill(void)
{
	static BYTE sector[512];
	DWORD s;
	UINT o;
	uint8_t end = 0;

	FS_ResourceManager_RequestResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);

	fs_fill.fs_type = fs.fs_type;
	fs_fill.read_result = 0xff;
	fs_fill.write_result = 0xff;

	if (fs.fs_type == 2)   /* FAT16: the root directory is a fixed run of sectors */
	{
		for (s = fs.dirbase; !end && (s < fs.dirbase + fs.n_rootdir / 16); ++s)
		{
			fs_fill.read_result = disk_read(fs.drv, sector, s, 1);
			if (fs_fill.read_result != RES_OK) break;

			for (o = 0; o < 512; o += 32)
			{
				if (sector[o] == 0) { end = 1; break; }
				if (!memcmp(&sector[o], "FILL    BIN", 11) && (sector[o + 11] != 0x0F))
				{
					fs_fill.sector = s;
					fs_fill.offset = o;
					fs_fill.start_cluster = sector[o + 26] | (sector[o + 27] << 8);
					fs_fill.size = sector[o + 28] | (sector[o + 29] << 8) | (sector[o + 30] << 16) | ((uint32_t) sector[o + 31] << 24);
					sector[o] = 0xE5;
					fs_fill.write_result = disk_write(fs.drv, sector, s, 1);
					++fs_fill.found;
					end = 1;
					break;
				}
			}
		}
	}

	FS_ResourceManager_ReleaseResource(FS_RESOURCE_FATFS);
	fs_fill.done = 1;
}

'''

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - FlySight 2 firmware (STM32WB5MMG), resource manager (VCC / microSD / FatFS counts), `VCC_EN` (PH1), SPI2 SD driver (`stm32_adafruit_sd.c`, high-speed CMD6 switch, `flag_SDHC`), FatFs R0.12c (`f_mount`, `create_chain` scanning the whole FAT when full, `f_printf` returning EOF without setting `fp->err` on a full disk, `f_rename` needing absent destination, `FA_CREATE_ALWAYS` truncation, `_FS_LOCK` 10).
   - microSD brown-out window: power cut of ~1.0–1.5 ms leaves the card in an inconsistent state (wrong card type, HS refused, FR_NO_FILESYSTEM) → `Error_Handler()`.
   - State file `/flysight.txt`: rewritten at every start by `FS_State_Init()` (Read then Write), also by `FS_State_NextSession()` (active/start mode), `FS_State_SetConfigFilename()` (config mode end), `FS_State_Update()` (USB unplug); holds `BLE_IRK`/`BLE_ERK`, `Temp_Folder`, `Session_ID`, `Config_File`, `Active_Mode`.
   - CRS file-transfer race (`FS_CRS_State_Read` emptying the RX queue in one pass).
   - ST sequencer nesting (`UTIL_SEQ_EvtIdle` → `UTIL_SEQ_Run`), clock handoff PLL↔HSE, stop mode suspending HAL tick; SWD reads right after halting a sleeping MCU can return garbage (read twice).
   - develop HardFaults when it starts with VBUS present (fixed on the branch by commit 89d5e1c); VBUS masking at `FS_Mode_Init` (force PA2 low + clear EXTI PR1 bit 2 at 0x5800080C).
   - Firmware defers USB mass-storage writes (`USBD_SyncStorage`): a reset while mounted loses the host's last writes.
   - Bench: OpenOCD 0.12 with hw breakpoints, Tcl scripts (`read_memory`, `mwb`, `reg pc`), button on PC12, VBUS_DIV on PA2, `vbus.py`, `ble_trace.py`; USB VID:PID 16d0:0569; card = 28.8 GB with a 2 GB FAT16 partition, 32 KB clusters, auto-mounted at `/media/$USER/NEW VOLUME`.
   - BlueZ: dead bonds accumulate when the FlySight's IRK changes; object path keeps the first address.
   - Transcript format: the app stores intermediate assistant messages as short reworded "thinking" blocks; final answers verbatim.

     #define STATE_FILE "/flysight.txt"
     #define STATE_TEMP "/flysight.tmp"

     if (f_open(&stateFile, STATE_FILE, FA_READ) != FR_OK)
     {
         /* A reset between the removal of the previous state file and the renaming of
            the new one leaves only the new one: put it in place and read it */
         if ((f_rename(STATE_TEMP, STATE_FILE) != FR_OK) ||
                 (f_open(&stateFile, STATE_FILE, FA_READ) != FR_OK))
         {
             FS_State_Complete();
             return;
         }

     ...
     /* Writes the state to stateFile, which is open, and closes it.
        Returns 0 if part of it did not reach the card. */
     static uint8_t FS_State_WriteContent(void)
     {
         ... uint8_t complete; ...
         // Write device info
         if (f_printf(&stateFile, "; FlySight - http://flysight.ca\n\n") < 0)
         {
             // Nothing can be written. On a full card each further write would
             // search the whole FAT for a free cluster before it fails as well
             f_close(&stateFile);
             return 0;
         }
         ... (other f_printf calls unchanged) ...
         // On a full card every write fails from some point on, this last one
         // included, and FatFs does not count that as an error of the file
         complete = (f_printf(&stateFile, "\n") >= 0) && !f_error(&stateFile);
         return (f_close(&stateFile) == FR_OK) && complete;
     }

     static void FS_State_Write(void)
     {
         if ((f_open(&stateFile, STATE_TEMP, FA_WRITE|FA_CREATE_ALWAYS) == FR_OK) &&
                 FS_State_WriteContent())
         {
             // Replace the previous file
             f_unlink(STATE_FILE);
             f_rename(STATE_TEMP, STATE_FILE);
             return;
         }
         // No room for a second file: rewrite the previous one in place
         f_unlink(STATE_TEMP);
         if (f_open(&stateFile, STATE_FILE, FA_WRITE|FA_CREATE_ALWAYS) != FR_OK)
         {
             Error_Handler();
         }
         FS_State_WriteContent();
     }

#!/bin/bash
# The revised fix: on the card still full, then on the card with its space back.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
M="/media/$USER/NEW VOLUME"; LNX=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux
FIXED="branch-statefix master-statefix develop-statefix"
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 4; }
mounted() { for i in $(seq 1 60); do [ -f "$M/CONFIG.TXT" ] && return 0; sleep 1; done; return 1; }
for V in $FIXED; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V on the full card   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  flash $E
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E unplugged-start 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$"
  for T in "boot 2" "usb 1"; do python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E $T 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-520; done
  MODE_WAIT_MS=20000 python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E active 1 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-520
  $S/modes/write_time.sh $E 2
  echo "DONEFULL3 $V"
done
echo "################ giving the space back   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
sync; flash $S/four/branch-statefix/build/branch-statefix.elf; sleep 6
if mounted; then
  rm -f "$M/FILL.BIN"; sync; sleep 3
  echo "after the removal: $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB free; FILL.BIN $([ -e "$M/FILL.BIN" ] && echo STILL THERE || echo gone)"
else
  echo "CARD NOT MOUNTED: FILL.BIN IS STILL ON THE CARD"
fi
for V in $FIXED; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V on the card with its space back   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  sync; flash $E
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E unplugged-start 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$"
  for T in "active 2" "start 1" "config 1" "timing 3" "reset-active 2" "usb 2" "reset-usb 2"; do
    python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E $T 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-520
  done
  for T in "midwrite 2" "preunlink 3" "gap 2" "full 2"; do
    python3 $LNX/state_rewrite_reset.py $E ${T#* } ${T% *} $S/modes/dumps_$V 2>&1 | grep -v "^before:\|^WITH" | cut -c1-420
  done
  echo "DONENORMAL3 $V"
done
echo V3_CHAIN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)

void FS_USBMode_DeInit(void)
{
	/*
	 * Leave the bus first. A host command arriving during the flush below
	 * would use the microSD from the USB interrupt while the flush is using
	 * it from this task, and the SPI/DMA transfer could then never complete.

	(void)USBD_LL_Stop(&hUsbDeviceFS);

	/* Flush any deferred USB mass-storage writes before shutting down. */
	if (USBD_SyncStorage() < 0)

	FS_USBControl_DeInit();

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/modes/unfill.sh`

~~~~
#!/bin/bash
# Removes the directory entry of /FILL.BIN that the full-card test left behind: the host deleted
# the file, the FlySight kept the last sectors of that deletion in its USB write cache, and the
# flash that followed reset it before they reached the card.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
M="/media/$USER/NEW VOLUME"
OCD="openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c 'transport select hla_swd' -f target/stm32wbx.cfg"
PRE='stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}
init
proc rd8 {a} { return [lindex [read_memory $a 8 1] 0] }
'
ocd() { printf '%s%s\nexit\n' "$PRE" "$1" > "$S/modes/unfill.tcl"; timeout 60 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -f "$S/modes/unfill.tcl" 2>&1; }
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; }
mounted() { for i in $(seq 1 40); do [ -f "$M/CONFIG.TXT" ] && return 0; sleep 1; done; return 1; }
# The host unmounts, then the FlySight is made to see the cable unplugged: leaving USB mode is
# what writes its cache to the card (Linux never asks for it: "Assuming drive cache: write through")
leave_usb() {
  sync
  udisksctl unmount -b /dev/sda1 2>&1 | head -1
  ocd 'mww 0x48000018 0x40000
mwb 0x48000000 [expr {([rd8 0x48000000] & ~0x30) | 0x10}]
sleep 3000' | grep -iE "error" | head -3
}

echo "== before: $(ls -U "$M" | tr '\n' '|')  free $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB"
leave_usb
echo "== test firmware that marks the entry deleted"
flash "$S/four/branch-unfill/build/branch-unfill.elf"
sleep 6
A=0x$(arm-none-eabi-nm "$S/four/branch-unfill/build/branch-unfill.elf" | awk '$3=="fs_fill"{print $1}')
ocd "halt
sleep 150
echo \"fs_fill 1: [mdw $A 9]\"
sleep 80
echo \"fs_fill 2: [mdw $A 9]\"
resume" | grep "fs_fill"
mounted && echo "== after the test firmware: $(ls -U "$M" | tr '\n' '|')"
leave_usb
echo "== bench firmware back"
flash "$S/fw/build/flysight.elf"
sleep 6
if mounted; then
  echo "== after: $(ls -U "$M" | tr '\n' '|')  free $(df -k "$M" | tail -1 | awk '{print $4}') KB"
  echo "TEMP: $(ls "$M/TEMP" | wc -l) folders, $(du -sk "$M/TEMP" | cut -f1) KB"
else
  echo "CARD NOT MOUNTED"
fi
echo UNFILL_DONE
~~~~

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| At start-up | 20 to 23 ms | 31 to 32 ms | 20 ms | 40 to 43 ms | 20 ms | 39, 40 and 93 ms |
| When active mode starts | 21 to 24 ms | 40 ms | 20 ms | 40 to 43 ms | 21 to 24 ms | 40 to 41 ms |

**A card that is really full.** `card-fill-test.patch` makes a build give one file, `/FILL.BIN`,
every free cluster of the card: 63 365 clusters, 2.07 GB, after which the PC reports 0 KB free.
Deleting the file from the PC gives the space back. On that card:

| | Without the fix | With the first commit only | With both commits |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time spent in `FS_State_Write()` at start-up | 20 ms | **42 to 43 s** | 338 to 341 ms |
| Two starts | state rewritten, keys kept | keys kept; still writing 4 s after each start | second file given up, state rewritten in place, keys kept |
| USB unplugged and plugged back | OK | not judged: the write was not over when the test looked | OK |
| Active mode entered and left | OK on the branch and on `master` | not judged, for the same reason | OK |

The first column is the branch without this fix, `master` and `develop`; the two others are the
same three with the fix. On `develop` without the fix the firmware had not finished entering
active mode 6 s after the press, busy looking for free clusters for its own files, so the test
pressed again too early; the last column allowed 20 s. The 0.34 s is one search of the FAT
followed by the write in place; that time grows with the size of the FAT, and this card has a
small one (a 2 GB FAT16 volume with 32 KB clusters).

Still not tested: a jump, or any active mode longer than a few seconds on a bench; a reset that
does not come from the debugger; a cable really pulled out; config mode with a `/config` folder;
another card. And a `flysight.txt` that a firmware without the fix has already emptied stays lost.

The tests of the modes added sessions to `TEMP` on the bench card (about 290 KB) and moved
`Temp_Folder` forward.

`state_rewrite_reset.py` is the script of both tables. On a firmware without the fix, its
`midwrite` mode changes the keys of the FlySight for good: every host has to pair again
-----

- **Branches.** Firmware: `fix/ble_pairing_issues`. SkyGames and its submodule FlySightApi:
  `release/1.1.0`. Everything the Linux session produced is committed there.
- **The bench FlySight** runs the build of the branch, with the trace of `ble_trace.py`. Its BLE
  keys changed many times during the tests of section 7 of the report: every device bonded with
  it before 9 October 2026 (the Mac, the Android phone, the iPad) has to forget it and pair again.
  The tests of the modes also added sessions to `TEMP` on its card and moved `Temp_Folder` forward.
- **Resets.** A firmware without the fix of section 7, `master` and `develop` included, draws new
  keys when it is reset about 130 ms after a start. From a script, leave a few seconds between

On the Linux PC (Ubuntu 24.04, BlueZ 5.72), set up on 2026-10-08:

- **Bench FlySight**: on battery, ST-Link V3 attached. `Scripts/cli/vbus.py` and `ble_trace.py` work through OpenOCD (no STM32CubeProgrammer here). A udev rule gives the user access to the ST-Link; no sudo is available to me, the user runs sudo commands when asked.
- **Firmware builds**: no CubeIDE project build here; a Makefile in the session scratchpad compiled an exported tree with `arm-none-eabi-gcc` 13.2 (include paths taken from `.cproject`), flashed with `openocd ... -c "program x.elf verify reset exit"`. `ble_trace.py` needs the ELF that is running (`FLYSIGHT_ELF`).
- **Test scripts and results**: `debug_ble/linux/` in the firmware repo (BlueZ probe, probe for SkyGames' native library, headless JVM probe for FlySightApi, README with every result).
- **SkyGames UI tests without touching the user's pointer**: start `Xephyr :99` with an xauth file, run `./gradlew :composeApp:run` with `DISPLAY=:99 SKIKO_RENDER_API=SOFTWARE`, drive it with `xdotool`, screenshot with PIL `ImageGrab.grab(xdisplay=":99")`, resize the app window with `xdotool windowsize` (there is no window manager). The Google sign-in opens in the user's Chrome on the real display; the user completes it, and the session then persists in the keyring.
- SkyGames checkout: `~/AndroidStudioProjects/skygames`, branch `release/1.1.0`; `local.properties` (git-ignored) holds `sdk.dir` and the user's Google keys.
- Gotcha: a process that must outlive the Bash call that starts it (Xephyr, the app, a test chain) has to be started with `setsid nohup ... < /dev/null & disown`; started as `( nohup ... & )` it died with the call on 2026-10-08 afternoon. A plain `sleep N` longer than a few seconds is refused: wait with a loop on a condition (a line in a log, or a deadline).
- A firmware stopped in `Error_Handler()` keeps its whole state: `debug_ble/linux/postmortem.py <elf>` reads it over SWD (how the microSD power-gap lockup was explained).
- Caution: never send a reset to the FlySight within about 0.2 s of its previous start (for instance two OpenOCD commands with `reset halt` back to back). The firmware empties and rewrites `flysight.txt` 130-145 ms after each start; a reset in that window makes it draw new BLE keys for good, and every host must pair again. Proven on 2026-10-08 (`debug_ble/linux/state_rewrite_reset.py`, README section on it); my first explanation (card powered at reset) was wrong, 68 such resets were harmless. Leave at least 3 s after a start before the next reset. An SWD memory read made right after halting a sleeping MCU can return garbage: read twice and compare.
- The bench FlySight's identifier for the Linux scripts changes each time its keys change (many times on 2026-10-08; `4E:55:D9:E4:DB:04` at the end of that day). To get the current one: `python3 Scripts/cli/vbus.py button`, then `python3 debug_ble/linux/fs_probe.py connect --flag 01` and read the address in its "scan: found" line (it pairs if needed). BlueZ holds dead bonds for it (`DC:73:5E:B4:33:86`, `FD:2D:95:CA:5B:D5`, `DA:0D:D5:F8:32:D7`, `F8:3A:B2:DD:94:D1`) that the user was told about and that I did not remove; scripts that take "the bonded FlySight" by name may pick a dead one.
- The state-file fix (write `/flysight.tmp`, then replace; rewrite in place when the card has no room) is committed on `fix/ble_pairing_issues` (`Keep the previous flysight.txt until the new one is written`); firmwares without it still lose their keys on a reset 130-145 ms after a start. The user is not sure about that fix because `FS_State_Write()` also runs when active mode starts, which was not tested.
- Gotcha: `pkill -f PATTERN` kills the calling shell when PATTERN

## Assistant (01:09)

Les tests complets sont faits et passent avec le correctif, mais ils ont révélé un défaut de sa première version, corrigé dans un second commit. Rien de ce travail n'est poussé, la documentation des résultats n'est pas commitée, et la carte du banc garde une entrée `FILL.BIN` fantôme que je n'ai pas pu retirer.

## Résultats

Six builds testés : la branche, `master` et `develop`, chacun sans et avec le correctif.

| Test | Sans le correctif | Avec le correctif |
|---|---|---|
| Mode actif, mode start, mode config | OK | OK |
| USB débranché puis rebranché | OK | OK |
| Reset pendant l'écriture à l'entrée en mode actif | clés changées 2/2 | clés gardées 2/2 |
| Reset pendant l'écriture après débranchement USB | clés changées 2/2 | clés gardées 2/2 |
| Reset au démarrage, 23 essais par build | non rejoué dans cette série | 0 changement sur les trois builds |
| Durée de l'écriture | 20 à 24 ms | 31 à 43 ms (une mesure à 93 ms) |
| Durée sur une carte vraiment pleine | 20 ms | 338 à 341 ms |

- **Défaut trouvé sur la carte pleine :** avec le premier commit seul, chaque écriture de l'état prenait 42 à 43 s. FatFs parcourt toute la FAT avant chaque écriture qui échoue, et il y en a une par ligne du fichier.
- **Correction :** le commit `9762e0e` abandonne le second fichier dès la première écriture refusée. Il est local.
- **Toujours pas testé :** un vrai saut, un reset qui ne vient pas du débogueur, un câble réellement arraché, le mode config avec un dossier `/config`, une autre carte.
- **Débranchement USB :** il est simulé par le débogueur (VBUS forcé à l'état bas), pas fait à la main.

## Ce que les tests ont laissé sur le banc

- **Clés BLE :** elles ont encore changé plusieurs fois. Le Mac, le téléphone Android, l'iPad et ce PC doivent oublier le FlySight et refaire l'appairage.
- **Sessions :** environ 3,7 Mo ajoutés dans `TEMP` sur la carte, et `Temp_Folder` a avancé.
- **`FILL.BIN` fantôme :** la carte liste encore le fichier de 2,07 Go du test, alors que son espace est bien libéré (2 024 256 Ko libres).
  - **Cause :** je l'ai supprimé depuis le PC puis j'ai flashé trois secondes après. En mode USB, le firmware garde en RAM le dernier secteur écrit par le PC jusqu'à la fin du mode USB, et Linux ne lui demande jamais de le vider. Le reset du flash a donc perdu la mise à jour du répertoire.
  - **Risque :** ne le supprime pas depuis un explorateur de fichiers. Ses clusters appartiennent probablement maintenant à des sessions de `TEMP`, et la suppression les libérerait.
  - **Sans effet sur le firmware :** il n'ouvre jamais ce fichier.

## Décisions pour toi

1. **Réparer la carte.** J'ai écrit un build de test qui marque uniquement cette entrée comme supprimée (un octet, la FAT n'est pas touchée), mais le système de permissions a refusé son exécution et il n'a donc jamais tourné. Tu peux le lancer toi-même, environ une minute, le FlySight et le ST-Link branchés :

```bash
bash [scratchpad]/modes/unfill.sh
```

   Sinon, `chkdsk /f` sur le volume depuis Windows, ou un formatage de la carte, font aussi l'affaire.

2. **Commiter la documentation des tests.** Je n'ai rien commité sans ta demande. Sont en attente : la section 7 réécrite du rapport, les deux README, et trois fichiers de test nouveaux. Dis-moi si tu veux le commit, et s'il faut pousser avec `9762e0e`.

#!/bin/bash
# usage: usb_chain.sh <variant>...   With the USB cable in: faked unplug and replug cycles, then resets during the write that follows an unplug.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
for V in "$@"; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $E verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"
  sleep 4
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E unplugged-start 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$"
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E usb 3 2>&1 | cut -c1-430
  python3 $S/modes/modes.py $E reset-usb 2 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-330
  echo "DONEUSB $V"
done
echo "################ bench firmware back   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $S/fw/build/flysight.elf verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"
echo USB_CHAIN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The state file (/flysight.txt) when the USB cable of the FlySight is really pulled out.

usage: state_real_unplug.py [--running <elf>] <elf>[:reset] [<elf>[:reset] ...]
       state_real_unplug.py --check <elf> ...     only reads the symbols of the builds

The FlySight is on its battery, with an ST-Link, and its USB cable goes to this PC. The script
says when to pull the cable out and when to plug it back in, and sees by itself that it was
done. For each build, in turn:
  1. cable out: the build is flashed and starts on the battery;
  2. cable in: the PC reads the card;
  3. cable out while the card is mounted on the PC, with nothing stopping the firmware; four
     seconds later the state is read over SWD;
  4. cable in: the PC reads the card again, and the two readings are compared;
  5. the PC ejects the card, then cable out with a breakpoint on FS_State_Write(): how many
     times it runs and how long it takes;
  6. with ":reset" after the name of the build: cable in, then out with a breakpoint just after
     the file to write is opened, and a reset there. Are the BLE keys still there?
--running names the build that is in the FlySight when the script starts: steps 2 and 3 are run
on it before the first flash, which needs the cable out anyway.

WARNING: step 6 on a firmware without the fix makes the FlySight draw new BLE keys for good.
Keys are never printed, only the first characters of their SHA-1.
"""
import hashlib
import os
import re
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import threading
import time

OPENOCD = ['openocd', '-f', 'interface/stlink.cfg', '-c', 'transport select hla_swd', '-f', 'target/stm32wbx.cfg']
FLYSIGHT, STLINK = '16d0:0569', '0483:'
MODES = ['sleep', 'active', 'config', 'USB', 'pairing', 'start']
SETTLE = 4          # seconds given to the firmware once the cable has moved
PATIENCE = 600      # seconds given to the person who holds the cable


def log(text):
    print('%s  %s' % (time.strftime('%H:%M:%S'), text), flush=True)


class Build:
    def __init__(self, spec):
        self.elf, _, option = spec.partition(':')
        self.reset = option == 'reset'
        self.name = os.path.basename(self.elf).rsplit('.', 1)[0]
        self.nm = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-nm', '-S', self.elf], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        self.dis = subprocess.run(['arm-none-eabi-objdump', '-d', '--no-show-raw-insn', self.elf], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
        self.state, self.fs = self.sym('state', 0x70), self.sym('fs', 0x234)
        self.mode, self.tick = self.sym('mode_state'), self.sym('uwTick')
        self.error = self.sym('Error_Handler') & ~1
        self.new_irk = (self.calls('FS_State_Complete', 'FS_Common_GetRandomBytes') or self.calls('FS_State_Read', 'FS_Common_GetRandomBytes'))[0]
        self.write = self.sym('FS_State_Write') & ~1
        self.midwrite = self.calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_open')[0] + 4
        self.fixed = bool(self.calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_rename'))
        self.recover = (self.calls('FS_State_Read', 'f_rename') or [None])[0]
        self.give_up = self.calls('FS_State_Write', 'f_unlink')[1] if self.fixed else None
        self.watch = [self.new_irk, self.error] + ([self.recover, self.give_up] if self.fixed else [])
        self.prelude = '''
stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}
init

    log('######## the end: %s stays in the FlySight' % last.name)

**Tool: Write** `[scratchpad]/modes/config_chain.sh`

~~~~
#!/bin/bash
# Config mode with a /config folder on the card, on the six builds. The cable of the FlySight
# stays in; VBUS is hidden from the firmware over SWD when a test needs it out of USB mode.
S="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
LNX=~/dev/Flysight/flysight-2-firmware/debug_ble/linux
BUILDS="${@:-master-unmodified master-statefix develop-unmodified develop-statefix branch-nostatefix branch-statefix}"
card() { for d in /media/$USER/*/; do [ -f "$d/CONFIG.TXT" ] && { echo "${d%/}"; return 0; }; done; return 1; }
mounted() { for i in $(seq 1 60); do card > /dev/null && return 0; sleep 1; done; return 1; }
ocd() { printf 'stm32wbx.cpu configure -event examine-end {}\ninit\nproc rd8 {a} { return [lindex [read_memory $a 8 1] 0] }\n%s\nexit\n' "$1" > "$S/modes/chain.tcl"; timeout 60 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -f "$S/modes/chain.tcl" 2>&1; }
flash() { timeout 120 openocd -f interface/stlink.cfg -c "transport select hla_swd" -f target/stm32wbx.cfg -c "program $1 verify reset exit" 2>&1 | grep -E "Verified|Error"; sleep 4; }
# What the PC wrote last stays in the RAM of the FlySight until USB mode ends: the PC unmounts,
# then the firmware is made to see the cable out, before anything resets it
leave_usb() {
  sync
  M="$(card)" && udisksctl unmount -b "$(findmnt -no SOURCE "$M")" 2>&1 | head -1
  ocd 'mww 0x48000018 0x40000
mwb 0x48000000 [expr {([rd8 0x48000000] & ~0x30) | 0x10}]
sleep 3000' | grep -i "error" | head -2
}
vbus_free() { ocd 'mwb 0x48000000 [expr {[rd8 0x48000000] & ~0x30}]' | grep -i "error" | head -2; }

echo "################ the folder   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
mounted || { echo "CARD NOT MOUNTED: nothing done"; exit 1; }
M="$(card)"
if [ ! -d "$M/CONFIG" ]; then
  mkdir "$M/CONFIG"
  for N in ALPHA BRAVO CHARLIE; do
    printf '; %s: a test configuration for config mode\r\n\r\nInit_File: %s ; Announces this configuration\r\n' "$N" "$(echo $N | tr A-Z a-z)" > "$M/CONFIG/$N.TXT"
  done
fi
sync
echo "/config on the card, in its own order: $(ls -U "$M/CONFIG" | tr '\n' ' ')"
leave_usb

for V in $BUILDS; do
  E=$S/four/$V/build/$V.elf
  echo "################ $V   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
  flash $E
  python3 $LNX/state_modes.py $E unplugged-start 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$"
  for T in "config-through 1" "config-select 2" "reset-config 2"; do
    python3 $LNX/state_modes.py $E $T 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-900
  done
  echo "DONECONFIG $V"
done

echo "################ the folder is removed   $(date +%H:%M:%S)"
vbus_free
if mounted; then
  M="$(card)"
  rm -f "$M/CONFIG/ALPHA.TXT" "$M/CONFIG/BRAVO.TXT" "$M/CONFIG/CHARLIE.TXT" && rmdir "$M/CONFIG"
  sync
  echo "/config on the card: $([ -e "$M/CONFIG" ] && echo STILL THERE || echo removed)"
  leave_usb
  # config mode without the folder empties Config_File
  python3 $LNX/state_modes.py $E config 1 2>&1 | grep -v "the fix$" | cut -c1-700
else
  echo "CARD NOT MOUNTED: /config IS STILL ON THE CARD"
fi
echo CONFIG_CHAIN_DONE $(date +%H:%M:%S)
